> **Round-20 scope split.** GDPR enforcement was split into **GDPR fanout + bounded fanout** after
> two successive "not ready to implement" verdicts (rounds 18/19)
> surfaced issues that cross the auctioneer ↔ EdgeZero boundary. **GDPR fanout
> is this plan** — the executable slice that ships now. bounded fanout tracks
> multi-adapter production fanout, fail-loud config, and streaming
> body caps, all of which need upstream EdgeZero prerequisites
> before they can land. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-10-bounded-fanout-
multi-adapter-production-fanout.md` and spec §14 GDPR enforcement entry.
>
> **⚠ Round-45 B4 — GDPR fanout IS NOT PRODUCTION-DEPLOYABLE. It is the
> DEV-COMPLETE capability.** Two production-safety gaps are
> structural to GDPR fanout and close only in bounded fanout:
>
> 1. **Config is not fail-loud.** `resolve_runtime_config`
>    degrades ANY config-store error — including a MALFORMED
>    host config — to `AuctioneerAppConfig::default()`. Because host
>    config controls GDPR enforcement, a malformed config would
>    silently DISABLE the gate, violating spec §9's fail-loud
>    rule (spec:4419). The typed `StoreAppConfigError` taxonomy
>    that lets auctioneer distinguish "fresh deploy, key absent"
>    (legitimate default) from "malformed, fail loud 500" is an
>    EdgeZero prerequisite (bounded fanout Prereq 1); until it lands, GDPR fanout
>    cannot be fail-loud, so it cannot serve production GDPR
>    traffic.
> 2. **The bidder-response cap is post-hoc, not a peak-memory
>    bound (round-46 B1 correction).** The pinned EdgeZero Axum
>    adapter fully buffers the upstream response with
>    `response.bytes().await` and hands auctioneer a `Body::Once`
>    ([edgezero-adapter-axum/src/proxy.rs](https://github.com/IABTechLab/edgezero/blob/9e661ae/crates/edgezero-adapter-axum/src/proxy.rs) — the
>    whole body is resident **before** auctioneer runs any check).
>    `Body::into_bytes_bounded(cap)` on a `Body::Once` only
>    compares `bytes.len() > cap` **after** that allocation
>    ([edgezero-core/src/body.rs](https://github.com/IABTechLab/edgezero/blob/9e661ae/crates/edgezero-core/src/body.rs) — the
>    incremental, chunk-bounded path exists only in the
>    `Body::Stream` branch, which the pinned Axum adapter never
>    produces). So GDPR fanout can REJECT an oversize response with the
>    correct wire shape, but it CANNOT bound peak memory against
>    a hostile upstream. A true peak bound needs EdgeZero to
>    yield `Body::Stream` incrementally (the outbound-HTTP
>    streaming prerequisite: `Body::Stream` +
>    `into_bytes_bounded_until`), which is an bounded fanout prereq. Until
>    it lands, GDPR fanout's Axum production fanout is memory-unsafe
>    under adversarial response sizes — a dev-complete
>    limitation, not a production guarantee.
>    **Round-92 H2 — the boundary is MECHANICAL, not prose:** Task 23
>    Step 0 bakes `auctioneer_core::capability::Capability =
Capability::DevComplete` into the binary, surfaces it as an
>    `x-auctioneer-capability` response header on `/status`, and pins it with
>    a workspace test — so a deploy pipeline can (and per the release
>    rule MUST) refuse to promote any build whose header is not
>    `production-complete`. The label flips only via the Fanout-8 /
>    Fanout-10 completion commits, each of which must also update the
>    pinning test — a visible, reviewable diff. A deploy manifest that
>    points GDPR fanout at a production `[stores.config]` is therefore a
>    mechanically detectable misconfiguration, not a checklist hope.

**Goal:** Ship the executable slice of GDPR enforcement: real TCF v2 / GDPR gate
in `auctioneer-privacy` + the full config-overlay stack + Axum-only
`ProductionFanout` + all four adapters conformant against
`DevFanout`. GPP-derived consent (D.1) remains deferred to privacy enforcement.

**Architecture:** Three tracks that share integration points but
ship independently commit-by-commit.

1. **Config schema track** — widens the codegen'd config shapes so
   real GDPR + real per-account overlays have somewhere to land.
   Ships first because every downstream track consumes the wider
   types. Landing spots: `crates/auctioneer-config/data/host-defaults.toml`,
   `crates/auctioneer-config/build_codegen.rs`,
   `crates/auctioneer-config/src/types.rs`.
2. **DevFanout conformance track** — proves the neutral
   `BidderFanout` contract holds on all four adapters via
   `DevFanout`. `ProductionFanout` gets its mid-fanout deadline +
   per-call timeout implementation for **Axum only** (GDPR fanout's
   only tokio-native adapter). Cloudflare / Fastly / Spin
   `ProductionFanout` alias to `DevFanout` under GDPR fanout — bounded fanout lands
   the real per-adapter production behaviour once upstream
   EdgeZero prerequisites arrive.
3. **GDPR track** — ships real TCF v2 string parsing, real
   `Signal` math for the GDPR-applies decision (**including
   `regs.gpp_sid` section 2 precedence over `regs.gdpr`** per spec
   §7.1 line 2202), the GVL vendor lookup backed by a bundled real
   IAB GVL archive, per-purpose enforcement, and the
   construction path
   ```rust
   PrivacyContext::resolve(
       &BidRequest, &AccountConfig, &HostConfig, &GvlStore,
       &Gcl, time::OffsetDateTime,   // round-102 B7: six-arg (GCL + now)
   ) -> Result<PrivacyContext, PrivacyError>
   ```
   **Round-44 auction core / round-102 B7: this header now matches Task 8's
   executable signature.** It previously advertised `(.., &Gvl) ->
PrivacyContext` — both the parameter (round-37 B4 moved it
   to the versioned `&GvlStore`) and the return type (round-44
   B1: `Result<_, PrivacyError>`; `AuctionError` would be a
   Cargo cycle) were stale. `run_auction` integration point:
   replaces the auction core `PrivacyContext::allow_all_no_scrub()` call
   site only. The test constructor stays per spec §7.6.

Auxiliary tracks that also close auction core deferrals: single-TOML
host + per-account overlay resolution (Task 15), request-scoped
registry overlay for `enabled = false` (Task 16), bidder
`sample_rate` sampler (Task 17), host-declared alias resolution
(Task 18).

**Deferred to bounded fanout (do NOT implement in this plan):**

- Task 11 (`ProductionFanout` mid-fanout deadline on
  Cloudflare/Fastly/Spin)
- Task 12 (streaming `max_bidder_response_bytes` cap)
- The fail-loud host-config path — PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED in execution:
  Task 15's review landed fail-closed for `Internal`/`ServiceUnavailable`
  (and round 3 added `BadRequest`) inside GDPR fanout, because a corrupt blob
  silently disabling GDPR was a privacy fail-open. What remains deferred
  to bounded fanout is ONLY the `ConfigOutOfDate` umbrella (needs EdgeZero's typed
  `StoreAppConfigError`). Original text follows for the record:
  `RuntimeConfigError::MalformedHost`
  (round-82 L1 — the canonical type is `RuntimeConfigError::MalformedHost`
  from `config/runtime.rs`, NOT an `AuctionError::MalformedHost` variant;
  GDPR fanout's `resolve_runtime_config` silent-degrades, bounded fanout makes it fail-loud)
- Task 20 (snapshot production fanout timeout fixture)
- Task 22 (snapshot production oversize fixture)

GDPR fanout's handler keeps auction core's `AppConfig::from_store()....unwrap_or_
default()` shape at
[auction.rs:261](../../../crates/auctioneer-core/src/handlers/auction.rs#L261).
That's a documented silent-degrade under GDPR fanout; bounded fanout's fail-loud fix

## Global Constraints

- **Workspace clippy stays at `pedantic = warn + restriction = deny`.**
  Every new file must clear the gate the auction core tree clears today.
- **No review-lifecycle markers, auctioneer-spec section citations, or
  Upstream-provenance references in code comments.** Same rule as the
  auction core sweep. This constraint is stated here so it does not depend on a private
  agent-memory file.
  OpenRTB citations remain welcome.
  **Round-38 foundations clarification for implementers:** the code
  snippets embedded in the task bodies below carry `Round-XX`
  markers as reader annotations to trace back to the review
  round that shaped each block. Those markers are for the
  document reader; **strip them when transcribing snippets
  into `.rs` or `.toml` sources**. The prose around each
  snippet explains why the shape is what it is — if the
  intent isn't clear enough to survive without the marker,
  fix the prose, not the code.
  **Mechanically enforced (round-70 foundations).** Task 23's gate runs a
  marker sweep that FAILS the build if any review-lifecycle marker
  reaches committed source, so a stray `round-NN` / `Task N Step` /
  `Phase N` comment can no longer slip through review:
  ```bash
  # Fails (exit 1) if any marker appears in .rs/.toml under crates/ or
  # the root Cargo.toml. `round.?trip` is excluded (a real API term).
  ! rg -n -e 'round-[0-9]' -e 'Round-[0-9]' -e 'Task [0-9]+ Step' \
        -e 'Step [0-9]+:' -e 'Phase [0-9]' -e 'review (High|Blocker|Medium|Low)' \
        --glob '*.rs' --glob '*.toml' crates/ Cargo.toml \
    | rg -v 'round.?trip'
  ```
- **All env variables use `__` (double underscore) to separate
  logical namespace sections.** `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__DIR`,
  not `AUCTIONEER_GVL_ARCHIVE_DIR`. The mapping mirrors dotted
  config paths: `auctioneer.foo.bar.abc` →
  `AUCTIONEER__FOO__BAR__ABC`. Applies to new names AND
  retroactive renames of existing `AUCTIONEER_*` vars — sweep in
  the same commit that introduces the surrounding change.
  Cargo's `CARGO_FEATURE_<...>` build-script pass-through
  names are unchanged.
- **Fmt/tests/clippy gate matches CI.** Every task ends with
  `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and (where the change
  touches wasm-shared code) the wasm cross-check across **every
  library crate consumed by an adapter target**:
  `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p auctioneer-runtime
-p auctioneer-openrtb -p auctioneer-config -p auctioneer-gvl-schema -p auctioneer-privacy
-p auctioneer-bidder -p auctioneer-exchange -p auctioneer-core` and the
  `wasm32-wasip1` equivalent (round-86 creative caching — `auctioneer-gvl-schema` is a
  library crate consumed by the GVL path and MUST cross-compile). This
  list matches Task 23's authoritative gate; a
  narrower per-task check would let a wasm-incompatible dependency
  slip through until the capability-end gate.
- **`RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"` mirrors CI locally** for the
  `auctioneer-config` build-failure harness. Any test that spawns a child
  `cargo build` must serialise via the existing `HARNESS_LOCK` mutex
  in `crates/auctioneer-config/tests/build_failure_harness.rs`.
- **No net-new `#[allow]` / `#[expect]` attributes without a written
  reason string.** Prefer refactoring the code so the lint doesn't
  fire; when unavoidable, quote the exact lint the reason justifies.
- **Frequent small commits, not batched.** Every task ends with a
  commit that (a) compiles on all four adapter targets and (b) has no
  red tests, red clippy, or unformatted files.
- **Per-task verify blocks are MINIMUM local checks, not
  substitutes for the global gate.** Individual task "Verify +
  commit" steps typically list only the crates the task touches
  (e.g. `cargo test -p auctioneer-privacy` for the privacy tasks) so
  the inner loop stays fast during implementation. Before pushing,
  every task MUST also pass the full workspace fmt/clippy/test
  gate + the wasm cross-check enumerated above. The Task 23
  workspace gate runs the same commands one final time at
  capability end; a task that greens its local check but reds the
  global gate is not committable.
- **`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-21-auctioneer-openrtb-server-design.md`
  is authoritative.** When code and spec disagree, either the code is
  wrong (fix the code) or the spec is wrong (raise it in the PR
  description; do not silently drift).
- **Standards-refresh checkpoint — TCF v2.4 behaviour is PRESENT in
  the published IAB TCF specification, and its GVL ARTIFACT is LIVE
  and ADVANCING (round-62 B1 — do NOT hardcode a version).** **Round-69
  foundations — anchor on the SPEC BEHAVIOUR, not the tracking PR's status.**
  Earlier rounds flip-flopped on whether spec PR #443 was open
  (round-59/62) or merged (round-63); the official PR page currently
  still shows it OPEN. That status is now irrelevant to the plan: the
  v2.4 semantics (policy version 5, `standardTexts`, the LI-workaround
  removal) are observable in the published specification text and the
  live GVL artifact, which is what auctioneer validates against. Do NOT
  assert a merge date for #443 anywhere; cite the spec/artifact
  behaviour instead. The live
  IAB GVL carries a v2.4-era shape — `gvlSpecificationVersion = 3`,
  **`tcfPolicyVersion = 5`**, a new **`standardTexts`** field — and
  its `vendorListVersion` / `lastUpdated` / SHA-256 **advance on a
  WEEKLY cadence — IAB publishes on Thursdays** (round-75 L1 —
  corrects the earlier "daily"; `169` @ `2026-07-23`, `170` @
  `2026-07-30`, `171` @ `2026-08-06` are consecutive Thursdays, one
  week apart). **Therefore the plan does NOT pin a specific
  version/SHA** — any literal it wrote would be stale within a week and
  would fail the
  "do not ship stale data" acceptance. The pin is chosen **at
  execution time**: the refresh tool fetches whatever is CURRENTLY
  live and records that version + timestamp + SHA into
  `manifest.json`; the plan asserts only the invariant SHAPE
  (`gvlSpecificationVersion 3`, `tcfPolicyVersion 5`,
  `standardTexts` present), never a value that dates.
  **Round-69 foundations — the v2.4 semantics are present in the published TCF
  specification and the live GVL artifact (do NOT assert #443's merge
  state — it is not the source of truth here).** BOTH halves are
  executable against that observable behaviour:
  - **Task 4a-v24 is RELEASE-BLOCKING:** refresh the pinned GVL to
    the **then-current live** blob (whatever version the tool fetches
    at execution) and accept `tcfPolicyVersion = 5` + the
    `standardTexts` passthrough before an GDPR enforcement release, OR explicitly
    pin+document the exact GVL shipped.
  - **DATA revalidation (executable):** confirm `validate_gvl_json`
    accepts `tcfPolicyVersion = 5` (accepted set is policy `≤ 5`),
    the `gvl_specification_version` mapping
    `tcf_policy_version < 4 → 2 else 3` still yields `3` for policy
    5, and the new `standardTexts` field is tolerated
    (`#[serde(default)]` passthrough — the GVL DTOs do NOT
    `deny_unknown_fields`).
  - **SPEC-CONSTANT revalidation (now EXECUTABLE — round-63 B1):**
    against the ratified v2.4 text, the CORE-segment ENCODING limits are
    UNCHANGED (`MAX_RANGE_ENCODED_ENTRIES` / 12-bit
    `NumEntries`, `PurposeId 1..=24` all carry forward — round-88 B1:
    `MAX_SEGMENTS` is dropped since auctioneer parses core contents only;
    rounds 108-110 add `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS = 2` for the strict
    trailing-segment set + framing validation), so no other
    parser-constant edit is required. **The one SEMANTIC change v2.4
    lands: it REMOVES the legacy workaround that required a
    Special-Purpose-only vendor to also assert the Vendor Legitimate
    Interest bit** (a vendor declaring only special purposes no
    longer needs an LI declaration to be treated as valid). Task
    4a-v24-spec (below) is now ACTIVE, not deferred: record this in
    the spec's Appendix A / TCF-parse notes and audit Task 3 / Task
    6 for any code that assumed the workaround (see the Task 4a-v24
    LI-workaround note).
    - **Round-87 stored requests and accounts — the v2.4 workaround lived in the TC STRING, not
      the GVL vendor record; it is verified by TWO tests in their OWNING
      tasks (NOT a single orphan counted under Task 4a).** The removed
      workaround: a special-purpose-only vendor was historically listed
      in the TC string's Vendor Legitimate-Interest section (its
      `vendor_li` bit set) purely to signal disclosure. Round-88 B1 as
      amended rounds 108-113: auctioneer parses only the TCF core
      segment's CONTENTS (the Disclosed Vendors segment is
      framing-validated but its semantic contents are not retained or
      consulted — see Task 3), so it never inferred LI from
      disclosure; the removed workaround was never implemented. Legitimate-interest legal basis is read from the
      CORE `vendor_li` bit alone, so a vendor whose core `vendor_li` bit
      is UNSET must NOT be granted an LI legal basis. The two split tests:
      - **GVL schema (Task 4):**
        `validate_gvl_json_accepts_special_purpose_only_vendor()` — a GVL
        vendor declaring ONLY `specialPurposes` (empty `purposes` + empty
        `legIntPurposes`) validates; `validate_gvl_json` imposes no
        "special-purpose-only requires LI" rule (the GVL SHAPE is legal —
        a schema fact, independent of any TC string).
      - **TC-string enforcement (Task 6):**
        `disclosed_vendor_with_unset_vendor_li_bit_denied_no_v24_li_workaround()`
        — a valid TCF v2 string listing vendor V in the Disclosed Vendors
        segment but leaving V's core-string `vendor_li` bit UNSET; under
        full LI enforcement of a purpose V declares under legitimate
        interest, the A.2 walk DENIES V (row 6 LI leg (c) reads
        `tcf.vendor_li` directly and never infers LI from disclosure —
        auctioneer never implemented the removed workaround).
        See **Task 4a-v24** for the executable fetch-and-pin-at-execution
        refresh + revalidation steps (it records the resulting version /
        timestamp / SHA; it does not carry a hardcoded one).

## GDPR fanout capability acceptance criteria

**Round-31 diagnostic qualification gate reconciliation.** Two-stage acceptance:

- **GDPR enforcement "dev-complete"** = GDPR fanout completion. Ships the Axum
  auction gate + DevFanout conformance on every adapter +
  GDPR fanout's silent-degrade config path. Downstream capabilities
  (privacy enforcement, user sync) can build against this.
- **GDPR enforcement "behavior-complete"** = GDPR fanout + bounded fanout tasks **Fanout-1..9** (gate:
  Fanout-8; round-72 foundations — NOT all of bounded fanout). Ships multi-adapter
  ProductionFanout, fail-loud config, streaming body cap. Blocks on
  EdgeZero upstream prereqs and may lag GDPR fanout by weeks or months.
- **GDPR enforcement "production-complete"** = behavior-complete **+ bounded fanout Task
  Fanout-10** (the per-route ingress hook, blocked on EdgeZero Prereq 5) —
  a DISTINCT gate beyond behavior-complete. **Round-76 H2 — the
  production label is PER-TARGET, not "all four build":** Axum requires
  Fanout-10's raw-wire E2E suite + the synthetic `decide` contract tests
  green; **Cloudflare / Fastly / Spin require EdgeZero adapter
  conformance + deployed runtime probes** (a passing BUILD proves
  nothing about the managed runtime's parser / capping / cancellation /
  framing), which land in diagnostic qualification — so until then the production GDPR-gate
  label applies to **Axum only**. **Round-76 B1 — production-complete
  also treats GDPR-via-GPP-section-2 CONSENT as unusable** (fail-closed
  → `default_permissions()`, no ID leak; NOT "excludes GPP-only
  traffic"); honouring section-2 consent lands in privacy enforcement.

The spec §14 gate that matters for downstream capabilities is
**dev-complete** (GDPR fanout). **Round-73 H1 — the gate that matters for a
production release badge / SLA promises is PRODUCTION-complete, NOT
behavior-complete.** Behavior-complete (GDPR fanout + Fanout-1..9) ships
multi-adapter ProductionFanout + fail-loud config + streaming cap, but
request bodies are STILL fully buffered until Fanout-10's pre-buffer
ingress hook lands — so advertising a production release at
behavior-complete would claim a defense (pre-allocation body caps) the
build does not yet have. A production release requires
**production-complete = behavior-complete + Fanout-10** (and it documents
that section-2 GDPR consent is nullified / fail-closed, round-76 B1 —
NOT a "GPP-only exclusion"). Both dev-complete and
behavior-complete are legitimate INTERNAL capabilities; the round-28
draft's "GDPR enforcement == GDPR fanout alone" phrasing conflated them, and round-30 privacy enforcement's
Task Fanout-8 title "behavior-complete workspace gate" was the bounded fanout-side
signal. Round-31 diagnostic qualification makes the names first-class here and in bounded fanout; the
production-release gate is the strictest of the three.

GDPR fanout is **dev-complete** when:

1. **Real `PrivacyContext::resolve` on the auction path.**
   ```rust
   auctioneer_privacy::PrivacyContext::resolve(
       &BidRequest, &AccountConfig, &HostConfig, &GvlStore,
       &Gcl, time::OffsetDateTime,   // round-102 B7: six-arg (GCL + now)
   ) -> Result<PrivacyContext, PrivacyError>
   ```
   **Round-45 H1 / round-102 B7: this acceptance criterion now matches
   Task 8's executable signature.** It previously advertised `(.., &Gvl)
-> PrivacyContext` — both the parameter (round-37 B4 moved it
   to the versioned `&GvlStore`) and the return (round-44 B1:
   `Result<_, PrivacyError>`; `AuctionError` is a Cargo cycle)
   were stale. Returns a real context computed from the request's
   TCF v2 string + GDPR signal + host / account gates. The
   `allow_all_no_scrub()` constructor stays for tests per spec
   §7.6; the production `run_auction` call site is the only
   removal.
2. **Real `PrivacyContext::permissions(core_name, bidder)`.** Vendor
   id is resolved from `BidderInfo.gvl_vendor_id` OR request
   `ext.prebid.aliasgvlids[<alias>]` per spec §7.3 line 2350. Aliases
   are handled with the two-arg key. The auction core `AllowAll` short-circuit
   is deleted from the production call site (constructor remains).
   2b. **The two GDPR scrubs are ENFORCED, not just decided**
   (round-49 H4 — this criterion was missing while Task 13 Step 3b
   already required the behaviour). For every surviving bidder the
   bidder-scoped request is scrubbed before fan-out per spec
   Appendix C.2: `PassID=false` → `scrub_gdpr_id`, `PassGeo=false`
   → `scrub_geo_and_device_ip`. `AllowAll` scrubs nothing. The
   remaining C.2 rows (activities, `scrub_user_fpd`, CCPA,
   LMT/COPPA, `scrub_tid`) stay privacy enforcement.
3. **`run_auction` integration.** `run_auction` calls
   `PrivacyContext::resolve` before splitting, passes the resulting
   permissions into the existing `live` filter via
   `permissions(&pbr.base, &pbr.bidder)`, and emits any resulting
   warnings via `PrivacyContext::take_warnings`.
4. **`BidderFanout` conformance — host-tested behavior + four-target
   compilation (round-58 H1: narrowed to what the harness actually
   proves).** The Bucket A conformance suite (oversize, transport
   error, zero calls, single call, no-retry, results order,
   per-bidder isolation) runs against `DevFanout` on the **host
   (native) target** — `DevFanout` is target-agnostic
   `auctioneer-core`/`auctioneer-exchange` code, so exercising it once on the
   host proves the behavior for every adapter that embeds it. The
   four adapter _targets_ are covered by **compilation only** (the
   spec §11 multi-target matrix, criterion 11:
   `cargo build --release -p auctioneer-adapter-cloudflare --target
wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `wasm32-wasip1` for Fastly/Spin, native
   for Axum). There is **NO wasm-runtime conformance test** in GDPR fanout —
   running the suite inside a CF/Fastly/Spin isolate would need an
   emulator/live-target harness, which is out of scope. So the
   guarantee is precisely: _shared `DevFanout` behavior is
   host-verified once + all four targets compile_, NOT "each adapter
   runs the suite in its own runtime."
5. **Axum `ProductionFanout` dev-complete.** (Round-47 B3: this
   criterion is part of GDPR fanout, which is dev-complete — NOT
   behavior-complete; the two-stage definition above is
   authoritative.) On the Axum
   adapter only, `ProductionFanout` (a) enforces `AuctionDeadline`
   mid-fanout (in-flight calls dropped at the deadline via the
   runtime-neutral `BiasedRace3` over the `Timer` abstraction —
   round-52 H3: NOT `tokio::select!`, since `RaceTimersStrategy`
   lives in wasm-portable `auctioneer-core`; the deadline arm is
   `timer.sleep(deadline_remaining)`), (b) applies
   `BidderCall.timeout` per call (the bidder arm of the same
   `BiasedRace3`). The non-Axum
   adapters keep the auction core delegating shape
   (`ProductionFanout::send_all` → `DevFanout::send_all`) — Bucket B
   production-side rows are `#[ignore]`d on Cloudflare / Fastly /
   Spin under GDPR fanout. Multi-adapter behaviour is bounded fanout, gated on
   upstream EdgeZero prerequisites. `FanoutError::OversizeResponse`
   maps to bidder error code 4 + `seatnonbid` statuscode 100 at
   [run.rs:589](../../../crates/auctioneer-exchange/src/run.rs#L589),
   unchanged from auction core; streaming cap is bounded fanout.
6. **Config-store account resolution.** The account-id extraction
   walks `app.publisher.ext.prebid.parentAccount` →
   `app.publisher.id` → `site.publisher.ext.prebid.parentAccount` →
   `site.publisher.id` → `dooh.publisher.ext.prebid.parentAccount` →
   `dooh.publisher.id` per spec §9 line 3858 (app → site → dooh, and
   within each `parentAccount` before `publisher.id`). Resolved
   against `AuctioneerAppConfig.accounts` — the same TOML blob the
   `AppConfig` extractor loads at boot; there is no per-account
   config-store key and no async per-request read. Result →
   `ResolvedAccount { source: AccountSource::Configured, ... }`.
   Missing entry → `AccountSource::DefaultFallback` (per spec §9).
   Disabled account → `AuctionError::AccountDisabled` (code 7)
   surfaces as HTTP 503. `AuctionError::MalformedAcct` (code 10)
   stays in the taxonomy for forward-compat with a future
   remote-account fetch path but is never emitted by the GDPR enforcement
   single-TOML resolver; when emitted, it surfaces as HTTP 500 per
   spec §9 line 3890.
7. **Config schema wide enough for real GDPR.**
   `HostConfig.gdpr` carries `host_vendor_id: Option<u32>`,
   `tcf2.enabled: bool`, the per-purpose enforce toggles per spec
   §7.9:2277, AND `non_standard_publishers: Vec<String>` (a list of
   account ids the host flags as non-standard per §9:3758 — host-
   owned, account-id keyed, NOT an account-level bool).
   `AccountConfig` grows a new `gdpr: AccountGdprConfig` block
   carrying `enabled: TriState` (account-level fallback checked
   BEFORE the host default per §7.1:2277),
   `channel_enabled.{web,app,amp,video,dooh}: TriState`, per-purpose
   `{enforce_algo, enforce_purpose, enforce_vendors,
vendor_exceptions}`, and `basic_enforcement_vendors: Vec<String>`.
   `AccountConfig` ALSO grows a `privacy: AccountPrivacyConfig`
   block (round-51 H5 — `ipv4/ipv6.anon_keep_bits`, defaults 24/56,
   `ip_keep_bits()` accessor, build-time range checks 32/128) that
   drives the `PassGeo=false` IP-mask scrub. Codegen widened, TOML
   validator widened; per-account overlay uses the typed-struct
   Some/None form documented in Task 15 (RFC 7396 structural
   semantics without the null-removes case).
8. **Registry overlay + sample_rate + host aliases.**
   `[bidders.<name>] enabled = false` in `auctioneer.toml` drops the
   bidder from participation. **Round-25 GDPR enforcement correction:** the
   implementation KEEPS the baked `AuctionContext.bidders`
   registry intact (adapters cannot rebuild `Box<dyn Bidder>`
   per request) and instead threads a `disabled_bidders:
&BTreeSet<BidderName>` through the split step at
   `auctioneer-exchange::split`, which filters out disabled names
   AND emits code-6 `BidderTemporarilyDisabled` warnings under
   the request-facing name. Task 16 owns this shape.
   `[bidders.<name>] sample_rate` actually samples requests using
   `AuctionContext.rng` (Task 17, sampled BEFORE the max-bidders
   cap per round-22 H6). `HostConfig.aliases` populated from
   `data/host-defaults.toml` flow through
   `alias::resolve_aliases` alongside request-declared aliases.
9. **Snapshot fixture coverage — GDPR fanout subset.** Task 19 (GDPR-applies
   snapshot with host + account TOML overlays enabling enforcement)
   and Task 21 (single-TOML account resolution snapshot). Task 20
   (production fanout mid-flight timeout) and Task 22 (oversize
   response streaming) are bounded fanout.
10. **All four adapters build.** `cargo build --release` for axum +
    cloudflare + fastly + spin all exit 0.
11. **spec §11 multi-target `cargo check` matrix stays green.**

GDPR fanout is **dev-complete** when the above holds and Task 19 / 21
snapshots pass byte-stable (round-47 B3: dev-complete, NOT
behavior-complete — the two-stage definition above is
authoritative, and Task 23's gate emits `GDPR fanout = dev-complete`).
**Byte-stable multi-adapter production fanout + fail-loud config +
streaming cap — and the behavior-complete badge — are bounded fanout**; do
not gate GDPR fanout on them.

  ```rust
  //! TCF v2 consent string parsing. Real impl lands in Task 3 once
  //! Task 1's spike decides between wrapping and hand-rolling.

  use std::collections::BTreeSet;

  /// Fixed-size bitset for vendor consent / LI. Round-24 C4:
  /// earlier drafts used `BTreeSet<u16>`, which allocates one
  /// tree node per vendor id. A single compact range entry
  /// like `1..=65535` in the encoded string would then expand
  /// into 65 535 tree nodes on decode — a memory blowup the
  /// hostile-input caps were supposed to prevent. `VendorBitSet`
  /// is a fixed `[u64; 1024]` (8 KiB, `65_536 / 64 = 1024`
  /// words) whose size does NOT depend on encoded cardinality.
  #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  pub struct VendorBitSet([u64; 1024]);
  impl VendorBitSet {
      /// Round-27 C2: ID `0` is not a valid GVL vendor id; it is
      /// unrepresentable in the set. `contains(0)` is UNCONDITIONALLY
      /// `false` — the storage bit is never inspected. This is the
      /// safety net that makes `purpose_allowed_basic(.., 0, ..)`
      /// safe: bidders without a GVL id (vendor_id 0) CANNOT be granted
      /// consent by a malformed range entry that started at `0`.
      // Round-60 B1: `#[must_use]` — a pure bool-returning getter
      // trips pedantic `must_use_candidate` under Task 23's
      // `-D warnings`. All the other getters carry it too.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn contains(&self, id: u16) -> bool {
          if id == 0 {
              return false;
          }
          // Round-48 B3: `usize::from(id)` not `id as usize`
          // (`as_conversions` is denied). Round-55 H2: total methods
          // (`wrapping_div`/`wrapping_rem`/`wrapping_shl`) plus
          // `.get` keep this clear of the `integer_division`,
          // `arithmetic_side_effects`, and `indexing_slicing`
          // restriction lints. word = idx/64 ≤ 65535/64 = 1023 <
          // 1024, so the `None` arm is unreachable but fail-safe.
          let idx = usize::from(id);
          let word = idx.wrapping_div(64);
          let bit = u32::try_from(idx.wrapping_rem(64)).unwrap_or(0);
          match self.0.get(word) {
              Some(w) => (w & 1_u64.wrapping_shl(bit)) != 0,
              None => false,
          }
      }
      /// Round-27 C2: `set(0)` and any set covering id 0 is a
      /// silent no-op for id 0 (the underlying bit is untouched
      /// even if the parser was tricked into invoking it). The
      /// PARSER MUST still reject range entries whose interval
      /// includes 0 or exceeds `MAX_VENDOR_ID`; this is defence
      /// in depth for the storage layer.
      pub fn set(&mut self, id: u16) {
          if id == 0 {
              return;
          }
          let idx = usize::from(id);  // round-48 B3: not `id as usize`
          // Round-55 H2: `.get_mut` + `wrapping_*` avoid
          // `indexing_slicing` / `integer_division` /
          // `arithmetic_side_effects`. word ≤ 1023 < 1024, so
          // `get_mut` is always `Some`; the `if let` is fail-safe.
          let word = idx.wrapping_div(64);
          let bit = u32::try_from(idx.wrapping_rem(64)).unwrap_or(0);
          if let Some(w) = self.0.get_mut(word) {
              *w |= 1_u64.wrapping_shl(bit);
          }
      }
      /// Set every id in `start..=end` by filling whole `u64` words.
      /// Round-61 H1: work is **O(words touched) ≤ 1024**, NOT
      /// O(range width) — a per-id loop let a hostile
      /// `[1, 65535]` entry do 65 535 mutations that the parser's
      /// operation counter (Task 3) never charged, so a stream of
      /// broad overlapping ranges could exceed the intended work
      /// ceiling without tripping it. The parser MUST charge the
      /// word count `(end/64 - start.max(1)/64 + 1)` to its counter
      /// and check the running total against the ceiling BEFORE
      /// calling `set_range` (validate-before-mutate); this method
      /// then does exactly that many word writes.
      /// Round-27 C2: `start.max(1)` guarantees bit 0 is never set
      /// even on a bypassed invocation.
      pub fn set_range(&mut self, start: u16, end: u16) {
          let lo = usize::from(start.max(1));
          let hi = usize::from(end);
          if hi < lo {
              return;
          }
          let first_word = lo.wrapping_div(64);
          let last_word = hi.wrapping_div(64);
          for word in first_word..=last_word {
              let base = word.wrapping_mul(64);
              let from = u32::try_from(lo.max(base).wrapping_sub(base)).unwrap_or(0);
              let word_top = base.wrapping_add(63);
              let to = u32::try_from(hi.min(word_top).wrapping_sub(base)).unwrap_or(63);
              if let Some(w) = self.0.get_mut(word) {
                  *w |= Self::word_bits(from, to);   // one word write
              }
          }
      }

      /// Inclusive bit mask for bits `from..=to` (`0 <= from <= to
      /// <= 63`). Round-61 H1: lint-safe — `checked_shr`/`checked_shl`
      /// avoid `arithmetic_side_effects`, and `width == 64` (whole
      /// word) is handled without a 64-bit shift overflow.
      fn word_bits(from: u32, to: u32) -> u64 {
          let width = to.saturating_sub(from).saturating_add(1); // 1..=64
          let ones = u64::MAX.checked_shr(64_u32.saturating_sub(width)).unwrap_or(0);
          ones.checked_shl(from).unwrap_or(0)
      }
  }

  #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  pub struct TcfString {
      pub tcf_policy_version: u8,
      pub vendor_list_version: u16,
      /// Round-98 H7: the core segment's `CmpId` (12 bits) — RETAINED
      /// (earlier drafts dropped it after decoding). Task 8's resolve
      /// validates it against the bundled Global CMP List: a TC string
      /// whose CMP is absent from the GCL, or whose CMP was DELETED
      /// before the string's `created`, makes consent UNUSABLE
      /// (fail-closed via `consent_usable = false` — per the TCF rule
      /// that only registered CMPs may create TC strings and IAB
      /// vendor guidance to discard strings from deleted CMPs).
      pub cmp_id: u16,
      /// Round-98 H7: `CmpVersion` (12 bits) — retained for
      /// diagnostics alongside `cmp_id`; not consulted by enforcement.
      pub cmp_version: u16,
      /// Round-88 B1: decoded from the core segment's `Created`
      /// epoch-deciseconds field (36 bits). Retained for
      /// policy-version gating (Axis B) and staleness diagnostics.
      pub created: time::OffsetDateTime,
      /// Round-88 B1: decoded from the core segment's `LastUpdated`
      /// field; retained for staleness diagnostics and the
      /// created/last-updated equality check (Axis C).
      pub last_updated: time::OffsetDateTime,
      pub purposes_consent: BTreeSet<u8>,
      pub purposes_li_transparency: BTreeSet<u8>,
      pub vendor_consent: VendorBitSet,
      pub vendor_li: VendorBitSet,
      pub special_feature_optins: BTreeSet<u8>,
      pub purpose_one_treatment: bool,
      pub publisher_cc: [u8; 2],
      /// Publisher restrictions decoded from the core segment's
      /// publisher-restrictions section (round-29 C1: this is
      /// NOT a separate SegmentType — it lives inside the core
      /// bitstream after `NumPubRestrictions`). The purpose
      /// enforcement matrix (Task 6) consults this via
      /// `check_pub_restriction(...)` and MAY override
      /// consent-vs-LI legal basis per vendor.
      /// **Stored as normalised inclusive vendor-id INTERVALS**,
      /// NOT one entry per vendor id (round-24 C4). A single
      /// `RangeSection` with `[start=1, end=65535]` in the wire
      /// format produces exactly ONE `PublisherRestriction`
      /// entry with `vendor_range = 1..=65535`, not 65 535
      /// entries. The cap is on ENCODED RANGE ENTRIES, not
      /// expanded cardinality.
      pub publisher_restrictions: Vec<PublisherRestriction>,
      // Round-88 B1: no `disclosed_vendors` field. auctioneer parses ONLY
      // the core segment's CONTENTS (reference consent parser discards everything
      // after the first `.`); the Disclosed Vendors segment's
      // semantic contents are not retained or consulted (its FRAMING
      // is validated — round-113 privacy enforcement wording). Round-108 H5 / round-109 B1: its
      // PRESENCE + FRAMING are mandatory, and the trailing SET is
      // exact (round-110 B2): {DV} or {DV, PublisherTC}, every
      // segment bounded-decoded and framing-validated (see the
      // MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS caps row). TcfParseError variants
      // (all fail-closed to unusable consent):
      // MissingDisclosedVendorsSegment,
      // DuplicateDisclosedVendorsSegment,
      // MalformedDisclosedVendorsSegment { reason },
      // DuplicatePublisherTcSegment,
      // MalformedPublisherTcSegment { reason },
      // TooManyTrailingSegments { actual }, EmptyTrailingSegment,
      // UnknownSegmentType { segment_type } — obsolete type 2
      // included; the current official format defines only 0/1/3
      // (the official TCF spec, May 2026 publication, makes the DV
      // segment mandatory). Special-purpose
      // disclosure resolution (privacy enforcement) will re-derive contents from the
      // raw string if/when needed, not from a core parse.
  }

  /// Round-25 C2: no `Copy` derive — `RangeInclusive<u16>` is
  /// not `Copy` in stable Rust (its iterator state prevents it),
  /// and derive(Copy) would fail to compile. `Clone` is enough
  /// for the `.iter()` walk in `check_pub_restriction` below.
  #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct PublisherRestriction {
      pub purpose_id: u8,
      pub restriction_type: PubRestrictionType,
      pub vendor_range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<u16>,
  }
  impl PublisherRestriction {
      // Round-61 B2: `#[must_use]` — a pure bool getter trips
      // pedantic `must_use_candidate` under Task 23's `-D warnings`
      // (same as `VendorBitSet::contains`).
      #[must_use]
      pub fn covers(&self, vendor_id: u16) -> bool {
          self.vendor_range.contains(&vendor_id)
      }
  }

  #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum PubRestrictionType {
      NotAllowed,
      RequireConsent,
      RequireLegitInterest,
  }

  impl TcfString {
      /// The IAB `CheckPubRestriction(purpose, type, vendor)`
      /// oracle. Returns true if the given restriction is declared
      /// for the given vendor/purpose combination.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn check_pub_restriction(
          &self,
          purpose_id: u8,
          restriction_type: PubRestrictionType,
          vendor_id: u16,
      ) -> bool {
          // Round-25 C2 fix — earlier draft read `r.vendor_id`,
          // which no longer exists; the C4 rewrite replaced that
          // field with `vendor_range`. Use the `.covers()` helper.
          self.publisher_restrictions.iter().any(|r| {
              r.purpose_id == purpose_id
                  && r.restriction_type == restriction_type
                  && r.covers(vendor_id)
          })
      }

      // Round-87 B4: companion to `check_pub_restriction` — returns the
      // restriction (if any) declared for this (purpose, vendor) pair.
      // A.2/A.3 row 6 is restriction-first: this feeds
      // `declares_purpose_for_consent`/`_for_li`, whose signatures take
      // `Option<PubRestrictionType>`.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn pub_restriction_for(
          &self,
          purpose_id: u8,
          vendor_id: u16,
      ) -> Option<PubRestrictionType> {
          self.publisher_restrictions
              .iter()
              .find(|r| r.purpose_id == purpose_id && r.covers(vendor_id))
              .map(|r| r.restriction_type)
      }
  }

  #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum TcfParseError {
      InvalidBase64,
      TruncatedCoreSegment,
      UnsupportedTcfVersion(u8),
      InvalidBitfield,
  }

  /// # Errors
  /// Returns `TcfParseError::InvalidBase64` unconditionally until
  /// Task 3 ships the real parser.
  pub fn parse_tcf_v2(_input: &str) -> Result<TcfString, TcfParseError> {
      Err(TcfParseError::InvalidBase64)
  }
  ```

**Task 1 decision (fill in during Step 3):**

> **Decision: HAND-ROLL.** Survey (Step 1): the only live TCF-string
> candidate on crates.io is `lib_tcstring 0.5.0` (Apache-2.0, sole
> dep `base64 0.22`; the other hits — `iab_gpp`, `iab-specs*` — are
> GPP/OpenRTB, not TC-string decoders; release-date lookup was
> unavailable offline and is moot given the capability outcome).
> Step 2: `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` on a probe
> with `lib_tcstring --no-default-features` PASSES clean; `cargo
tree` shows no tokio/openssl/mio/native deps. Step 2b capability
> audit against the pinned 0.5.0 source
> (`src/decode/{model,tcf_2}.rs`):
>
> - Raw CORE fields: EXPOSED (`TcModelV2` carries `cmp_id`,
>   `cmp_version`, `created_at`/`updated_at` (deciseconds ×100 →
>   millis), `tcf_policy_version`, purpose consent/LI, special
>   features, `purpose_one_treatment`, publisher restrictions).
> - Allocation controls: **HIDDEN/UNCONTROLLABLE — FAIL.**
>   `vendors_consent`/`vendors_li_consent` are `Vec<u16>` of
>   EXPANDED per-vendor ids and `PublisherRestriction.vendor_list`
>   likewise — a range entry `1..=65535` materializes 65 535
>   elements with no cap hook (exactly the round-24 C4 blowup
>   `VendorBitSet`/interval storage exists to prevent).
> - Strict trailing-bit/length control: PARTIAL —
>   `TcsError::{InsufficientLength, InvalidSegmentDefinition}` exist
>   but there is no leftover-bits strictness hook matching auctioneer's
>   `TruncatedCoreSegment`/`InvalidBitfield` taxonomy.
> - Strict trailing-segment SET contract: **UNCONTROLLABLE — FAIL.**
>   The decoder PARSES obsolete type-2 `allowed_vendors` into the
>   model instead of rejecting it, and has no
>   duplicate/unknown/extra-segment rejection auctioneer can reach.
>   Per the Step 2b rule (one hidden capability suffices; we have
>   two), auctioneer hand-rolls the parser in Task 3. No workspace dep is
>   added. Field-taxonomy source persisted in `tcf.rs` module docs:
>   the IAB Europe Transparency & Consent Framework v2 Technical
>   Specifications — "Consent string and Vendor List Formats v2"
>   (TC String format section),
>   https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/GDPR-Transparency-and-Consent-Framework/blob/master/TCFv2/IAB%20Tech%20Lab%20-%20Consent%20string%20and%20vendor%20list%20formats%20v2.md
>   (v2.4-era revision, May 2026 publication line; the auctioneer spec's
>   Appendix A remains the truth-table reference, not the binary

      (round-54 B1).** The current renderers return `fmt::Error`
      ([build_codegen.rs:394](../../../crates/auctioneer-config/build_codegen.rs#L394)),
      which carries no message — but the validating renderers below
      (and the build-failure harness in Step 6) need TYPED, message-
      bearing errors. Task 2 therefore introduces `RenderError` and
      **migrates every existing renderer signature from
      `Result<String, fmt::Error>` to `Result<String, RenderError>`**
      (`render_host_config`, `render_account_config`,
      `render_resource_limits`, `render_string_string_btreemap`, and
      `StructLit::render`). `RenderError` wraps `fmt::Error` so the
      format-machinery `?` still works:

  ```rust
  // crates/auctioneer-config/build_codegen.rs
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub enum RenderError {
      Fmt(core::fmt::Error),
      InvalidTristate(String),
      InvalidGdprDefaultValue(String),
      IpKeepBitsOutOfRange { family: &'static str, value: u8, max: u8 },
      // Round-55 foundations: baked-config enforcement-map key out of range.
      PurposeIdOutOfRange { id: u8 },
      SpecialFeatureIdOutOfRange { id: u8 },
      // Round-56 B2: `enforce_algo` domain is "full" | "basic", NOT a
      // tri-state — a separate error from `InvalidTristate`.
      InvalidEnforceAlgo(String),
      // Round-56 B3: host_vendor_id must be a u16 (0..=65535); reject
      // rather than clamp.
      HostVendorIdOutOfRange { value: u32 },
  }
  impl From<core::fmt::Error> for RenderError {
      fn from(e: core::fmt::Error) -> Self { RenderError::Fmt(e) }
  }
  impl core::fmt::Display for RenderError {
      fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
          match self {
              RenderError::Fmt(e) => write!(f, "format error: {e}"),
              RenderError::InvalidTristate(v) => write!(f, "invalid tri-state {v:?}"),
              RenderError::InvalidGdprDefaultValue(v) => write!(f, "invalid gdpr default_value {v:?}"),
              RenderError::IpKeepBitsOutOfRange { family, value, max } =>
                  write!(f, "{family}.anon_keep_bits {value} exceeds max {max}"),
              RenderError::PurposeIdOutOfRange { id } =>
                  write!(f, "purpose id {id} out of range (must be 1..=10)"),
              RenderError::SpecialFeatureIdOutOfRange { id } =>
                  write!(f, "special feature id {id} out of range (must be 1..=12)"),
              RenderError::InvalidEnforceAlgo(v) =>
                  write!(f, "invalid enforce_algo {v:?} (must be \"full\" or \"basic\")"),
              RenderError::HostVendorIdOutOfRange { value } =>
                  write!(f, "host_vendor_id {value} out of range (must be 0..=65535)"),
          }
      }
  }
  impl std::error::Error for RenderError {}
  ```

  ```rust
      #[serde(default = "default_ipv6_raw")] pub ipv6: IpAnonConfigRaw,

  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]

  // build the pair is via the two family functions above.
  impl Default for AccountPrivacyConfigRaw {
      fn default() -> Self { Self { ipv4: default_ipv4_raw(), ipv6: default_ipv6_raw() } }
  ```

- [ ] **Step 2: Extend the codegen render helpers.** In
      `build_codegen.rs`, add renderers (all returning
      `Result<_, RenderError>` per Step 2a). **`render_tristate` returns
      `Result` and rejects unknown values (round-22 H4 fix — earlier
      fail-open renderer mapped every unknown string to
      `TriState::Unset`, so a typo in a baked TOML would silently
      disable enforcement without alerting):**

  ```rust
  // Round-55 foundations: enforcement-map key ranges. **MUST match the
  // runtime `PURPOSE_ID_RANGE` / `SPECIAL_FEATURE_ID_RANGE` in
  // auctioneer-config/src.** Purposes 1..=10, special features 1..=12.
  const PURPOSE_ID_RANGE: core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> = 1..=10;
  const SPECIAL_FEATURE_ID_RANGE: core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> = 1..=12;

  pub fn render_tcf2(cfg: &Tcf2ConfigRaw) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
      // Round-55 foundations: reject out-of-range keys (0 or overflow) BEFORE
      // emitting the baked maps, so a mistyped `[gdpr.tcf2.purposes.0]`
      // or `.99` fails the build instead of baking a dead entry.
      for &id in cfg.purposes.keys() {
          if !PURPOSE_ID_RANGE.contains(&id) {
              return Err(RenderError::PurposeIdOutOfRange { id });
          }
      }
      for &id in cfg.special_features.keys() {
          if !SPECIAL_FEATURE_ID_RANGE.contains(&id) {
              return Err(RenderError::SpecialFeatureIdOutOfRange { id });
          }
      }
      // ... render each purpose via
      //     render_purpose_enforcement(p) and
      //     each special feature; emit the two baked BTreeMaps ...
  }
  // `render_account_gdpr` runs the SAME two key-range loops before
  // emitting the account map — the range constants above are shared.
  // Round-87 B2: host and account purposes render identically (no
  // `is_host` distinction) since `allow_li_transparency` is gone.
  // Round-54 B1: the privacy renderer — validates the range HERE
  // (runtime types can't derive Validate) and emits the struct
  // literal. Absent block → family defaults 24/56.
  pub fn render_account_privacy(cfg: &AccountPrivacyConfigRaw) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
      for (family, max, bits) in [("ipv4", 32_u8, cfg.ipv4.anon_keep_bits),
                                  ("ipv6", 128_u8, cfg.ipv6.anon_keep_bits)] {
          if bits > max {
              return Err(RenderError::IpKeepBitsOutOfRange { family, value: bits, max });
          }
      }
      Ok(format!(
          "AccountPrivacyConfig {{ ipv4: IpAnonConfig {{ anon_keep_bits: {} }}, \
           ipv6: IpAnonConfig {{ anon_keep_bits: {} }} }}",
          cfg.ipv4.anon_keep_bits, cfg.ipv6.anon_keep_bits))
  }
  // Round-87 B2: `render_purpose_enforcement` takes NO `is_host` flag
  // and no `purpose_id` — `allow_li_transparency` is no longer a config
  // field on either side, so there is nothing host-specific to reject
  // and host/account purposes render identically.
  pub fn render_purpose_enforcement(
      p: &PurposeEnforcementRaw,
  ) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
      // Round-56 B2: `enforce_algo` is `"full" | "basic"` (an
      // `EnforceAlgo`, NOT a tri-state) — route it through
      // `render_enforce_algo`, NOT `render_tristate`. Only
      // `enforce_purpose` / `enforce_vendors` are tri-states.
      let algo = render_enforce_algo(&p.enforce_algo)?;
      let purpose = render_tristate(&p.enforce_purpose)?;
      let vendors = render_tristate(&p.enforce_vendors)?;
      let exceptions = format!(
          "vec![{}]",
          p.vendor_exceptions
              .iter()
              .map(|v| format!("{v:?}.to_owned()"))
              .collect::<Vec<_>>()
              .join(", ")
      );
      Ok(format!(
          "PurposeEnforcement {{ enforce_algo: {algo}, \
           enforce_purpose: {purpose}, enforce_vendors: {vendors}, \
           vendor_exceptions: {exceptions} }}"
      ))
  }

  // Round-56 B2: dedicated renderer for the two-value `enforce_algo`
  // domain. `render_tristate` would reject BOTH valid values ("full"
  // / "basic" are not "unset"/"enabled"/"disabled").
  pub fn render_enforce_algo(s: &str) -> Result<&'static str, RenderError> {
      match s {
          "full"  => Ok("EnforceAlgo::Full"),
          "basic" => Ok("EnforceAlgo::Basic"),
          other   => Err(RenderError::InvalidEnforceAlgo(other.to_owned())),
      }
  }

  // Round-56 B3: host_vendor_id renders into the baked
  // `HostGdprConfig.host_vendor_id: Option<u32>` (this file, §
  // types). The raw DTO is `u32` because TOML has no `u16` and 0 is
  // a valid "skip host-company GDPR check" sentinel (spec §7.9). The
  // renderer REJECTS anything above `u16::MAX` — it does NOT clamp
  // into `u16` (the pre-round-56 draft's "clamps into u16
  // internally" language was wrong and is deleted). Called from
  // `render_host_config`; the baked default is always a concrete
  // value, so it emits `Some(..)`, never `None`.
  pub fn render_host_vendor_id(value: u32) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
      if value > u32::from(u16::MAX) {
          return Err(RenderError::HostVendorIdOutOfRange { value });
      }
      Ok(format!("Some({value}_u32)"))
  }

  pub fn render_tristate(s: &str) -> Result<&'static str, RenderError> {
      match s {
          "unset"    => Ok("TriState::Unset"),
          "enabled"  => Ok("TriState::Enabled"),
          "disabled" => Ok("TriState::Disabled"),
          other      => Err(RenderError::InvalidTristate(other.to_owned())),
      }
  }

  pub fn render_gdpr_default_value(s: &str) -> Result<&'static str, RenderError> {
      match s {
          "0" => Ok("\"0\""),
          "1" => Ok("\"1\""),
          other => Err(RenderError::InvalidGdprDefaultValue(other.to_owned())),
      }
  }

  pub fn render_account_gdpr(cfg: &AccountGdprConfigRaw) -> Result<String, RenderError> { ... }
  ```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the parser — hostile-input hardened.**
      The parser processes untrusted request data (`user.consent` is
      attacker-controlled), so bounds are non-negotiable. Land these
      input caps regardless of wrap-vs-hand-roll choice.

  disclosed-vendor bitfield" rationale is retired for the CORE caps:
  the DV segment is framing-validated under its OWN per-segment
  bounds and its membership set is not retained):**

Among inputs longer than any valid TC string, no parse outcome is reachable anyway, so the precedence contract below is scoped to inputs within the step-zero cap: for those, the count check still runs FIRST, before any per-segment content. Exact order (round-108 H5 inserts step 2; round-109 B1 upgrades it to framing validation): (1) split the raw input on the FIRST `.`; (2) validate the trailing segments per the `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` row — the trailing set must be EXACTLY `{DV}` or `{DV, PublisherTC}`, every segment framing-complete (round-110 B2; the full rejection taxonomy lives in that row); (3) DISCARD the validated contents (nothing from the suffix is retained); (4) apply `MAX_INPUT_LEN` to the CORE substring — reject a CORE longer than 64 KiB before base64-decoding; (5) base64-decode the core; (6) apply `MAX_DECODED_LEN` to the decoded CORE. Round-111 B1 (removes the round-89 sentence this row still carried): a trailing segment over its per-segment bounds is REJECTED (`Malformed*Segment` — the `oversize_trailing_segment_rejected` fixture), never silently discarded; the property this row pins is only that such a rejection is a TRAILING-segment error, not a core-over-cap error. Real-world TCF cores are ≤ ~2 KiB; publishers hitting this must trim.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS`               | `2`                       | round-110 B2 (REPLACES the round-108/109 `MAX_SNIFFED_SEGMENTS = 8` tolerate-and-scan contract, which let duplicate DV segments hide past the scan cap and accepted unknown/obsolete types): the current IAB TCF v2 format defines exactly three segment types — Core (0), Disclosed Vendors (1, MANDATORY), Publisher TC (3) — so a valid string has AT MOST three segments. auctioneer requires the trailing set to be EXACTLY `{DV}` or `{DV, PublisherTC}` (order-agnostic). Per trailing segment: bounded base64url decode (raw ≤ `MAX_INPUT_LEN`, decoded ≤ `MAX_DECODED_LEN`), read the 3-bit SegmentType, then FRAMING-validate: type 1 per the DV rules (bitfield/range completeness — round-109 B1); type 3 per the Publisher-TC layout (`SegmentType(3) + PubPurposesConsent(24) + PubPurposesLITransparency(24) + NumCustomPurposes(6) + 2 x N custom bits` = 57 + 2N bits, post-consumption remainder < 8, zero padding) — contents of both validated-then-DISCARDED (unretained; DV membership lands privacy enforcement, publisher-TC enforcement is a later capability). Rejections (all fail-closed → consent unusable, never a 400): more than 2 trailing segments → `TooManyTrailingSegments { actual }`; an empty segment (`..`, or a trailing `.`) → `EmptyTrailingSegment`; type 0 in trailing position, obsolete type 2 (Allowed Vendors/OOB — REMOVED from the current format), or any other type → `UnknownSegmentType { segment_type }`; two type-1 → `DuplicateDisclosedVendorsSegment`; two type-3 → `DuplicatePublisherTcSegment`; incomplete/overlong framing → `MalformedDisclosedVendorsSegment { reason }` / `MalformedPublisherTcSegment { reason }`; zero type-1 → `MissingDisclosedVendorsSegment`. **Round-111 B1 — EXPLICIT precedence (one deterministic order, so every multi-defect fixture has ONE expected error):** (1) the count check runs FIRST — more than 2 trailing segments is `TooManyTrailingSegments` regardless of their contents; (2) then segments are processed LEFT TO RIGHT — per segment: empty → `EmptyTrailingSegment`; type-read → unknown type → `UnknownSegmentType`; a repeated type (second type-1 / second type-3) → the matching `Duplicate*` the moment the repeat is seen; otherwise framing-validate → `Malformed*Segment`; (3) `MissingDisclosedVendorsSegment` is checked LAST, only after every trailing segment validated cleanly. So `{PubTC, PubTC}` → `DuplicatePublisherTcSegment` (the repeat fires before the final missing-DV check), and `{DV, PubTC, PubTC}` → `TooManyTrailingSegments`. |

  Every allocation the parser performs MUST be reservation-bounded
  by one of these caps — no unbounded `Vec::with_capacity(n)`
  where `n` comes from the input.

  **Core-segment parsing (round-88 B1 — upstream parity at the core
  CONTENT layer; trailing-segment story amended rounds 108-110,
  round-110 B2 = the strict exact-set contract).** auctioneer splits the base64url TC
  string on the FIRST `.` and parses ONLY the leading (core) segment's
  CONTENTS for retention; the trailing set must be EXACTLY
  `{Disclosed Vendors}` or `{Disclosed Vendors, Publisher TC}` per
  the `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` contract (round-110 B2) — both segment
  kinds framing-VALIDATED then discarded; empty, duplicate, unknown,
  obsolete-type-2, extra, or structurally incomplete segments are
  REJECTED (fail-closed to unusable consent). **Round-111 B1 — the
  round-88 "matches reference consent parser / suffix can NEVER reject / no
  SegmentType decode / no DV requirement / no duplicate detection"
  paragraph that used to stand here is DELETED, not amended: every
  one of its claims is the retired contract.** The authoritative
  statement is spec §7.2 (the strict segment-set contract) and the
  `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` row above; reference consent parser parity holds ONLY for
  the CORE segment's content semantics. Where reference consent parser accepts a
  core-only or malformed-suffix string, auctioneer rejects fail-closed —
  the recorded §15 divergence (rounds 108-110): the official format
  makes DV mandatory, and its contents stay unretained until privacy enforcement's
  special-purpose disclosure enforcement (which MUST parse the
  membership before authorizing an undisclosed special-purpose-only
  vendor).

  **Core segment layout:** the leading `.`-separated segment has NO
  segType prefix; its initial 6 bits are the format `Version` field (must
  equal `2` for TCF v2). Version ≠ 2 →
  `TcfParseError::UnsupportedTcfVersion(actual_version)`. Publisher
  RESTRICTIONS remain parsed — they live INSIDE the core segment (see
  below), not in a trailing segment.

  **auctioneer's core-only CONTENT parse matches upstream** (parity at the
  content layer), but round-108 H5's Disclosed-Vendors PRESENCE
  requirement IS a recorded §15 divergence (reference consent parser accepts a
  core-only string; the official TCF spec makes the segment
  mandatory), and auctioneer ADDITIONALLY applies the stricter
  CORE-segment validations below (upstream's `Parse` performs none of them; they only
  make auctioneer reject MALFORMED core strings harder, they never accept a
  string upstream would reject):

  **Axis B — TCF policy version.** **Round-36 foundations —
  two-authority disagreement documented and pinned.** The
  TCF technical specification says policy-v3 strings
  created after 2023-09-30 are invalid; IAB Europe's
  transition FAQ says policy-v3 strings created before
  2023-11-20 remain valid. **auctioneer follows the TCF
  technical specification** — that's the normative parser
  contract; the FAQ is operational guidance to CMPs. Rule:
  - `tcfPolicyVersion < 4` is only valid when the `Created`
    timestamp is `< 2023-10-01T00:00:00Z`. Otherwise →
    `TcfParseError::PolicyVersionTooOldForCreated {
created, policy_version }`.
  - `tcfPolicyVersion >= 4` is valid regardless of
    `Created`.

  **Disputed-interval tests (round-36 foundations).** Cover the
  two-authority disagreement explicitly:
  - `policy_v3_created_2023_10_15_rejected_per_tech_spec()`
    (inside the FAQ's grace window; auctioneer rejects
    because the tech spec is the parser authority).
  - `policy_v3_created_2023_11_19_rejected_per_tech_spec()`
    (last day of the FAQ's grace window; auctioneer rejects).
    A future spec revision that adopts the FAQ semantics
    would rename these tests to `_accepted` and change the
    cutoff constant; the explicit tests are the tripwire.

  **Axis C — Created / LastUpdated equality rule** (round-35
  H1 correction to round-34 H6). IAB TCF v2.3 §5 requires
  `Created` and `LastUpdated` to hold the **same value**,
  representing the UTC day-truncated timestamp (both fields
  are day-precise per the spec; sub-day resolution isn't
  part of the on-wire semantics even though the encoding
  field is 36-bit deciseconds). Rules:
  - `Created == LastUpdated` (exact equality of the decoded
    `OffsetDateTime`) is required. Unequal → `TcfParse
Error::CreatedLastUpdatedMismatch { created, last_
updated }`.
  - Each timestamp MUST be UTC-day-truncated. A decoded
    `OffsetDateTime` with any non-zero time component (hour,
    minute, second, nanosecond) → `TcfParseError::Timestamp
NotDayTruncated { field, actual }` where `field` is
    `"created"` or `"lastUpdated"`. Encoders that respect
    the spec always emit day-truncated deciseconds.
    Round-35 H1 tests (supersedes the round-34 H6 same-day
    trio):
  - `created_equal_lastupdated_day_truncated_accepted()`.
  - `created_not_equal_lastupdated_rejected()` (even same-
    day sub-day differences fail now).
  - `created_with_sub_day_component_rejected()`.
  - `lastupdated_with_sub_day_component_rejected()`.

  (Axis B and Axis C are the ONLY core-segment timestamp/policy rules;
  round-88 B1 deleted the former "Axis A" disclosed-vendors-segment
  CONTENT transition — rounds 108-110: the DV segment's FRAMING is
  parsed and validated, its semantic contents are NOT retained.)
  - **Retain `Created` / `LastUpdated` on `TcfString`.** Populated from
    the core `epoch_deciseconds * 100 ms` since UNIX epoch; needed for
    Axis B policy-version gating + Axis C equality and staleness
    diagnostics (round-88 B1 as amended rounds 108-112 — no
    disclosed-vendors CONTENT transition; trailing-segment FRAMING is
    validated per the `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` contract, so the
    `Duplicate/Malformed PublisherTc` and DV framing error variants
    DO exist, while `TcfString` still carries NO `publisher_tc` and
    NO `disclosed_vendors` field — framing parsed, semantic contents
    not retained).

  Add explicit CORE-segment rejection fixtures ONLY for the retained
  rules (Axis B / Axis C / `IsServiceSpecific` / range validation /
  publisher restrictions below). There are NO disclosed-vendors /
  Publisher-TC CONTENT fixtures (contents are never retained), and
  `trailing_segments_ignored.txt` (round-112 B1 — the old
  "arbitrary extra `.`-separated bytes" shape violated the strict
  segment-set contract: a well-formed core + a framing-valid minimal
  DV segment + a framing-valid Publisher-TC segment) parses to the
  SAME `TcfString` as core + minimal DV alone (framing parsed,
  semantic contents not retained). **Round-108 H5 — EVERY valid-string fixture
  in the GDPR fanout suites (Tasks 3/6/8/9 and the snapshots) carries a
  minimal type-1 segment after the core, because a core-only string
  is now structurally INVALID (`MissingDisclosedVendorsSegment`);
  the fixture helper appends one canonical FRAMING-VALID minimal DV
  segment (round-109 B1 — `MaxVendorId = 1`, bitfield, one vendor
  bit, zero-padded: a first-char-only stub would now be rejected as
  truncated).**

  - If wrapping (Task 1 chose a crate): implement `parse_tcf_v2` as
    a thin adapter that maps the wrapped crate's error type into
    `TcfParseError`. Validate the caps ABOVE at the input boundary
    before handing to the wrapped crate — most upstream crates
    don't enforce them. Confirm the wrapped crate exposes publisher
    restrictions; if not, add a hand-rolled
    `PubRestrictionsSegment` decoder that runs alongside the
    wrapped core parser.
  - If hand-rolling: implement per the IAB TCF v2 tech spec section
    "Consent String Format". Base64URL-decode the core segment (first
    `.`-separated block), parse fields via a `BitReader` over the
    decoded bytes, then decode vendor consent / LI ranges. Publisher
    restrictions live in the PubRestrictionsSegment inside the core
    segment (immediately after the vendor LI section per the IAB
    binary layout); decode into `Vec<PublisherRestriction>`.

  Range decoding MUST reject:
  - Reversed ranges (`start > end`)
  - Overlapping ranges within the same section
  - **Terminal padding — exact rule (round-89 user sync, resolving the
    "leftover bits" vs "trailing bytes" ambiguity).** After the last
    declared field, let `remaining_bits = decoded.len() * 8 - cursor`.
    A base64-decoded segment ends on a byte boundary but the bitstream
    may end mid-byte, so up to 7 bits of TCF-legal ZERO padding are
    expected and ACCEPTED. Precisely:
    - `remaining_bits < 8` (a partial final byte): every remaining bit
      MUST be `0`. A non-zero padding bit → `TcfParseError::NonZeroPadding`.
      (This is the minimum zero padding needed for byte alignment — the
      ONLY legal leftover.)
    - `remaining_bits >= 8` (one or more WHOLE trailing bytes beyond the
      last partial byte): reject → `TcfParseError::TrailingBytes` (extra
      data is a decoder-side ambiguity / a smuggling attempt), regardless
      of whether those bytes are zero.
      Tests: `zero_padding_for_byte_alignment_accepted()` (a valid string
      whose last byte carries only zero padding), `non_zero_padding_rejected()`,
      `whole_trailing_byte_rejected()` (even an all-zero extra byte).
  - **Zero endpoints and out-of-section endpoints** (round-27 C2):
    - `start == 0` OR `end == 0` → `TcfParseError::InvalidVendorId
{ section, actual: 0 }`. Zero is not a valid GVL vendor id;
      allowing it into any range would let a malformed string flip
      bit 0 in `VendorBitSet`, which is the sentinel that
      `purpose_allowed_basic(.., 0, ..)` relies on to deny bidders that
      lack a GVL id. Defence in depth: `VendorBitSet::contains(0)`
      is also unconditionally `false` at the storage layer.
    - `end > MaxVendorId` for the segment's declared `MaxVendorId`
      field → `TcfParseError::VendorIdBeyondSegmentMax { section,
actual, max }`. Applies to the **core segment's**
      `VendorConsent` `MaxVendorId` field and the core segment's
      `VendorLegitimateInterest` `MaxVendorId` field. Round-112 B1
      (corrects the round-88 "DisclosedVendors is not parsed, check
      removed" claim): the DV segment's OWN `MaxVendorId` bound IS
      enforced — during trailing-segment FRAMING validation
      (`MalformedDisclosedVendorsSegment` on violation, per the
      `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` row), not through this core-section
      error variant; the membership set is still not retained.
    - **NOT applied to publisher-restriction inner ranges**
      (round-29 C1 — publisher-restriction records simply have
      NO section-level maximum). Each record on the wire is
      exactly `{ PurposeId, RestrictionType, NumEntries, [range
entries] }`; the vendor ids inside the ranges are u16
      values with no outer cap. The round-28 draft still called
      out a fictional `PubRestrictionsSegment.MaxVendorId`; that
      field DOES NOT EXIST in TCF v2.3.

  **Publisher-restriction wire layout (round-29 C1 — critical
  correction).** Publisher restrictions live INSIDE the core
  segment, immediately after the vendor legitimate-interest
  section. Layout:

  ```
  Core segment (base64url-decoded, one bitstream):
    Version(6) … VendorLegitimateInterest section …
    NumPubRestrictions(12)
    [ NumPubRestrictions records of: PurposeId(6)
                                     RestrictionType(2)
                                     NumEntries(12)
                                     [range entries] ]
  ```

  Publisher restrictions are NOT a separate segment — they are part of
  the CORE segment, so auctioneer's core-only parser (round-88 B1) reads them
  normally. (The trailing `SegmentType = 3` "Publisher TC" segment — a
  distinct data structure carrying publisher-level consents — is a
  DIFFERENT thing: its FRAMING is validated per the
  `MAX_TRAILING_SEGMENTS` contract and its contents are not retained
  (rounds 108-112); the round-28 confusion of the two is moot.)
  The validation rules below apply to the **core-segment
  publisher-restrictions section**.

  **Publisher-restriction record validity.**
  - **`IsServiceSpecific == 1` required unconditionally.**
    Round-29 H1: per IAB TCF v2.3 §5.1.3, the CMP MUST signal
    `IsServiceSpecific = 1` for a valid TCF v2.3 string —
    **regardless of whether the publisher-restrictions section
    is empty**. A TC string with `IsServiceSpecific = 0` is
    invalid on its face → `TcfParseError::NotServiceSpecific`.
    The earlier "reject only when publisher-restrictions is
    nonempty" rule was incorrect.
  - **Purpose id in 1..=24.** Round-28 C2: the record's 6-bit
    `PurposeId` field encodes 1..=24 for TCF v2.3 (not 1..=10 —
    Purpose 11 is real; C1 covers the full range). `PurposeId ==
0` OR `PurposeId > 24` → `TcfParseError::InvalidPub
RestrictionPurpose { actual }`.
  - **Restriction type in {0, 1, 2}.** The 2-bit
    `RestrictionType` field carries four values: `0 = NotAllowed`,
    `1 = RequireConsent`, `2 = RequireLegitimateInterest`, and
    `3 = Undefined` (reserved). `RestrictionType == 3` →
    `TcfParseError::UndefinedPubRestrictionType`. Every
    downstream code path (Task 6's enforcement matrix) can
    assume the value is in `{0, 1, 2}`.
  - **No LI bits for purposes 3–6 — POLICY-VERSION-GATED
    (round-45 B2).** IAB introduced the "Purposes 3, 4, 5, 6
    cannot use LI legal basis" prohibition with **TCF v2.2 /
    policy version 4**; it does NOT apply to the policy-v3
    strings Axis B accepts (created before 2023-10-01). The
    parser rejects a non-zero core-segment
    `PurposeLITransparency` bit for those positions →
    `TcfParseError::LiBitSetForConsentOnlyPurpose {
purpose_id }` **only when `tcf_policy_version >= 4`**;
    under policy < 4 the bit is preserved. (Round-112 B1: the
    round-45 "PublisherTC check above" cross-reference is retired —
    Publisher-TC CONTENTS are not read under the strict segment-set
    contract, so this core check is the only LI-bit rule.) Fixture pair:
    `core_policy3_purpose4_li_bit_accepted.txt` and
    `core_policy4_purpose4_li_bit_rejected.txt` (round-45
    B2 renames the round-30 `purpose_3_li_bit_set_rejected`
    single fixture, which encoded the prohibition
    unconditionally).
  - **NumEntries wire field is 12-bit; the encoded-entries cap
    is redundant defence.** A `NumEntries > 4_095` value cannot
    exist on the wire (the field only carries 12 bits), so the
    plan's `MAX_RANGE_ENCODED_ENTRIES = 4_095` and
    `MAX_PUB_RESTRICTION_ENCODED_ENTRIES = 4_095` caps are
    **defensive assertions** that fire only on decoder bugs, not
    on adversarial input. Documented explicitly so tests do not
    try to construct a "wire input with 4 096 entries" case that
    the encoder cannot emit.

      ```rust
      // crates/auctioneer-privacy/tests/hostile_input_over_65536_bytes.rs
      // Round-48 B3: the allow carries a reason — `clippy::allow_attributes_without_reason`
      // is denied workspace-wide.
      #![cfg_attr(
          feature = "hostile-input-alloc",
          allow(unsafe_code,
              reason = "counting global allocator needs an unsafe GlobalAlloc impl; \
                        gated behind the opt-in hostile-input-alloc test feature")
      )]
      mod common;                       // tests/common/mod.rs
      use common::ALLOC;

      fn main() {
          // (1) FIRST reset the peak sentinel to current live so
          //     process-startup allocations don't inflate the
          //     baseline (round-29 H6 correction — the round-28
          //     order was baseline → reset → hostile, letting
          //     process warm-up peaks masquerade as parser peak).
          ALLOC.reset_peak_to_live();

          // (2) Parse a valid minimal string to establish
          //     baseline peak from a clean sentinel.
          let baseline_start = ALLOC.snapshot();
          let _ = auctioneer_privacy::tcf::parse_tcf_v2(VALID_MIN).expect("baseline");
          let baseline_peak = ALLOC.peak_since(&baseline_start);

          // (3) Reset again so the hostile measurement starts
          //     from a clean sentinel too.
          ALLOC.reset_peak_to_live();

          // (4) Hostile input — assert it errors and stays inside
          //     baseline_peak * 4.
          let hostile_start = ALLOC.snapshot();
          let err = auctioneer_privacy::tcf::parse_tcf_v2(HOSTILE_INPUT).unwrap_err();
          assert!(matches!(err, TcfParseError::InputTooLong(..)));
          let hostile_peak = ALLOC.peak_since(&hostile_start);
          assert!(
              hostile_peak <= baseline_peak.saturating_mul(4),
              "hostile_peak={hostile_peak} baseline_peak={baseline_peak}"
          );
      }
      ```

tests/support/` from an earlier round is REMOVED —

mod.rs` (per Cargo's subdirectory-skip convention).
      No separate crate needed.
    - The tracker is a **single `TrackingAllocator` value**, not
      a static-in-static. Shape:
      ```rust
      // crates/auctioneer-privacy/tests/common/mod.rs
      // (round-29 H6: under a subdirectory so Cargo does not
      // auto-discover it as a standalone integration binary;
      // compiled once per feature-gated hostile target via
      // `mod common;` from each target file)
      #![cfg_attr(feature = "hostile-input-alloc", allow(unsafe_code))]
      use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
      use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

      pub struct TrackingAllocator {
          live: AtomicUsize,
          peak: AtomicUsize,
      }

      impl TrackingAllocator {
          pub const fn new() -> Self {
              Self { live: AtomicUsize::new(0), peak: AtomicUsize::new(0) }
          }
          /// Snapshot current live bytes; use as a baseline BEFORE
          /// running the code under test. Round-27 H2: there is
          /// no reset-to-zero. Resetting live-bytes to zero while
          /// earlier process allocations were still live would
          /// underflow on their eventual `dealloc`. Measure
          /// deltas from a snapshot instead.
          pub fn snapshot(&self) -> AllocSnapshot {
              AllocSnapshot { live_at_snapshot: self.live.load(Ordering::Relaxed) }
          }
          pub fn peak_since(&self, snap: &AllocSnapshot) -> usize {
              self.peak.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
                  .saturating_sub(snap.live_at_snapshot)
          }
          /// Round-28 H2: reset the peak sentinel back to
          /// current live, so subsequent measurements do not
          /// carry stale peaks from earlier baseline work.
          /// Note we reset `peak` to `live`, NOT to zero —
          /// zeroing peak while live > 0 would break the
          /// invariant `peak >= live` and cause spurious under-
          /// counting when `peak_since(snapshot).saturating_sub`
          /// silently clamps.
          pub fn reset_peak_to_live(&self) {
              let live = self.live.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
              self.peak.store(live, Ordering::Relaxed);
          }
      }

      pub struct AllocSnapshot { live_at_snapshot: usize }

      // Round-32 GDPR enforcement concurrency rewrite. Previous round-31
      // `fetch_add` + `saturating_add` on the TEMPORARY still let
      // the stored counter WRAP under concurrent alloc, and the
      // dealloc path used a racy `load / saturating_sub / store`
      // pair — two concurrent dealloc calls could lose an update.
      // Both operations now use `fetch_update` (compare-exchange
      // loop) so the STORED value is saturating, and the peak
      // fetch_max sees the true running total.
      unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for TrackingAllocator {
          unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
              let ptr = unsafe { System.alloc(layout) };
              if !ptr.is_null() {
                  let size = layout.size();
                  // Round-32 GDPR enforcement: saturating atomic add via CAS loop.
                  let new_live = self
                      .live
                      .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |prev| {
                          Some(prev.saturating_add(size))
                      })
                      .unwrap_or_else(|prev| prev)   // fetch_update on saturating closure never returns None
                      .saturating_add(size);
                  self.peak.fetch_max(new_live, Ordering::Relaxed);
              }
              ptr
          }
          unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
              unsafe { System.dealloc(ptr, layout); }
              let size = layout.size();
              // Round-32 GDPR enforcement: saturating atomic sub via CAS loop.
              let _ = self
                  .live
                  .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |prev| {
                      Some(prev.saturating_sub(size))
                  });
          }
      }

      #[global_allocator]
      pub static ALLOC: TrackingAllocator = TrackingAllocator::new();
      ```
    - **Each hostile-input case is a separate integration test
      binary** (one `crates/auctioneer-privacy/tests/
hostile_input_<name>.rs` per case) because integration
      test binaries share nothing but Cargo's runner. Every
      binary declares the `#[global_allocator]` above via `mod
common;` (round-30 L1: pulls from
      `tests/common/mod.rs`, the round-29 H6 subdirectory
      layout; the earlier `mod hostile_input_common` reference
      was stale). The resulting statics are per-binary, not
      per-workspace.
    - **Baseline subtraction via snapshot** (round-30 L1: the
      two-reset-around-baseline shape is documented in the
      round-29 H6 code block above; this paragraph is
      shorthand). Each test resets the peak sentinel BEFORE
      the baseline parse, records `ALLOC.snapshot()`, parses
