**Interfaces:**

- Produces:
  - `pub struct Gvl { inner: Arc<GvlInner> }` — thin
    `#[derive(Clone)]` wrapper. `Clone` is a single refcount bump,
    not a ~11k-vendor map copy.
  - `pub(crate) struct GvlInner { pub gvl_specification_version: u32, pub vendor_list_version: u32, pub tcf_policy_version: u32, vendors: BTreeMap<u16, Vendor>, purposes: BTreeMap<u8, Purpose>, special_purposes: BTreeMap<u32, SpecialPurpose>, features: BTreeMap<u32, Feature>, special_features: BTreeMap<u8, SpecialFeature> }` — the real storage; only `Gvl` methods reach in. **Round-36 B3:** `gvl_specification_version` field added; `from_baked`/`GvlStore` reads it. **Round-31 H6:** four ID spaces are separate — `purposes` and `special_features` have wire caps (24 and 12 positions, `u8` fits); `special_purposes` and `features` are GVL-declared with no wire cap and stay `u32`. Auction enforcement (Task 6) and PassGeo/PassID derivation (Task 9) reference `vendor.special_purposes` id sets against the top-level table.
  - `pub struct GvlStore { … }` — round-39 B3 lazy-parse
    shape. Round-37 B2's eager shape (parse every bundled
    version at boot into an owned `HashMap<(u32, u32),
Gvl>`) ballooned resident memory: ~30 IAB list versions
    × ~1 MB each parsed into a ~4 MB `Gvl` handle = ~120 MB
    per isolate. Cloudflare Workers cap isolate memory at
    128 MB, and Fastly starts fresh sandbox per request —
    both make eager parsing infeasible. Round-39 B3 keeps
    raw JSON as `include_bytes!` in .rodata (zero heap) and
    parses lazily on first `get(spec, list)`, backed by a
    bounded LRU cache.

    ```rust
    /// Round-46 B2/B3 canonical shape — an ENTRY-COUNT
    /// bounded LRU, correct and executable. The round-45
    /// byte-bounded variant was withdrawn: its accounting
    /// depended on a "counted flag" that was never written,
    /// `LruCache::put` could evict a counted entry without
    /// subtracting its bytes, a cell evicted mid-parse could
    /// be accounted after it left the map, and `heap_bytes()`
    /// had no valid upper bound (`BTreeMap` exposes no
    /// capacity API and the sum ignored tree nodes, the six
    /// nested `BTreeSet`s per vendor, and allocator overhead).
    /// A HARD byte reservation is only needed by the admission
    /// / whole-isolate memory proof, which defers to bounded fanout with
    /// the streaming prerequisite (see the bounded fanout isolate budget);
    /// GDPR fanout bounds the cache by COUNT and documents — does not
    /// prove — the resulting byte envelope.
    ///
    /// Boot cost: one init + zero JSON parses.
    /// Per-lookup cost: cache hit = Arc refcount bump;
    /// cache miss = one JSON parse behind the shared cell.
    pub struct GvlStore {
        /// Immutable index of (spec, list) → &'static raw
        /// bytes. Populated once from `gvl_archive()`; no
        /// per-entry allocation after boot.
        raw_index: std::collections::HashMap<(u32, u32), &'static [u8]>,
        /// Access-recency LRU, bounded by entry COUNT. Holds
        /// `Arc<OnceCell<Gvl>>` so concurrent misses on the
        /// same key singleflight through `OnceCell::get_or_init`
        /// (round-40 H3); the parse runs outside the lock on
        /// the shared cell. If a cell is evicted while its
        /// parse is still in flight, a later miss re-parses
        /// into a fresh cell — a rare, correctness-neutral
        /// duplicate parse under eviction pressure, not a
        /// double-count (there is no byte accounting to
        /// corrupt).
        cache: std::sync::Mutex<
            lru::LruCache<(u32, u32), std::sync::Arc<once_cell::sync::OnceCell<Gvl>>>,
        >,
    }

    /// The cache bound: at most this many parsed `Gvl` handles are
    /// held BY THE CACHE. **Round-68 H5 — this is a CACHE-OWNED-ENTRY
    /// bound, NOT a total-resident-memory bound.** `Gvl` is
    /// `Arc<GvlInner>`; an auction clones the handle out of the cache
    /// and holds it for the auction's lifetime. If the cache evicts
    /// that `(spec, list)` entry while the auction still holds its
    /// clone, the `Arc<GvlInner>` stays resident until the auction
    /// drops it — so total resident parsed-GVL memory can transiently
    /// exceed `GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES × max_gvl_heap` by the
    /// number of concurrent auctions holding evicted handles (bounded fanout
    /// acknowledges the same retained-`Arc` effect for its streaming
    /// budget). The correct statement is: cache-OWNED entries are
    /// `≤ GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES × max_gvl_heap`; a byte-exact,
    /// retention-aware total-resident reservation lands in bounded fanout
    /// alongside the admission gate (round-46 B2/B4/B5).
    ///
    /// Round-47 H3: sized to **4**, NOT 64. A ~4 MiB worst-case
    /// `Gvl` × 4 = ~16 MiB — comfortably inside the isolate. The
    /// old value of 64 was meaningless as a memory bound: the
    /// archive ships only ~30 list versions, and 64 ≥ 30 means
    /// EVERY bundled list could stay resident (~120 MiB — nearly
    /// the entire 128 MB Cloudflare isolate, before code, raw
    /// data, requests, or retained Arcs). The hot working set is
    /// 1–2 versions (current, plus the previous during a
    /// rollover); 4 leaves headroom without letting the cache
    /// approach the ceiling. Raise it only with a real
    /// whole-isolate budget (bounded fanout).
    pub const GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 4;

    impl GvlStore {
        /// Process-wide baked store. Populated from
        /// `auctioneer_config::gvl_archive()` on first call;
        /// no per-entry parsing at init.
        pub fn baked() -> &'static GvlStore { … }

        /// Parse-on-demand. Cache hit → Arc bump.
        /// Cache miss → one JSON parse + LRU insert.
        /// `None` when the (spec, list) isn't bundled.
        /// A parse failure on a bundled entry is a
        /// workspace-invariant violation (build.rs
        /// validated at compile time); the runtime logs
        /// and returns `None` rather than panicking (edge
        /// runtimes tolerate panics poorly).
        pub fn get(&self, spec: u32, list: u32) -> Option<Gvl>;

        /// Test-only constructor. Pre-parsed `Gvl`s, no
        /// raw-index layer.
        pub fn for_test(entries: Vec<(u32, u32, Gvl)>) -> Self;
    }
    ```

    **Retired: `Gvl::from_baked(spec, list)`.** Public read
    path is `GvlStore::baked().get(spec, list)`.

    **Bundle-size + startup-heap gates** (round-40 B5
    canonical, retires round-39 B3's numbers which
    combined 400-day retention with a 12 MiB raw-bundle
    gate — 57 weekly files at ~1 MB each = ~57 MB raw,
    blowing the gate before compression. Round-40 B5
    separates raw and compressed budgets and picks
    retention math that fits within CF Workers' 10 MB
    COMPRESSED-bundle limit):
    - `GVL_BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_BYTES` — sum of `include_bytes!`
      lengths across manifest entries. **Round-44 H1: the
      default is per-target, because the wasm adapters
      budget the GVL against a 128 MB isolate they share
      with everything else:**
      - **wasm targets (CF, Fastly, Spin): 24 MB.** This
        is the number bounded fanout's admission proof reserves; the
        round-43 text said 60 MiB here and 24 MB there,
        and the round-44 review correctly flagged that
        the two must agree. 24 MB raw → ~3.5 MB brotli'd,
        which also keeps the CF Worker inside both the
        10 MB compressed and 64 MB uncompressed ceilings
        once code is added.
      - **native target (Axum): 60 MB.** Its ceiling is
        detected at boot (round-44 H5), not fixed, so a
        wider archive is affordable.
        `build.rs` picks the default from `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH`
        (`wasm32` → 24 MB, else 60 MB). Deployer
        override `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB`
        applies to either.
    - `GVL_BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_BYTES` (default 9 MiB) —
      round-40 B5 addition. `build.rs` after emitting
      `include_bytes!` also runs a brotli-11 compression
      pass over the same bytes and asserts the compressed
      total fits under this cap. Catches deployments
      whose corpus doesn't compress as expected. Deployer

    round-34 shape checked the vendor's declared default

    `RequireLegitimateInterest` restriction against a
    consent-declared vendor was silently ignored. IAB rule
    is **restriction-first**: a restriction overrides the
    default basis. Correct shape:
    ```rust
    impl Vendor {
        /// Round-90 B1 / round-108 stored requests and accounts: a vendor whose `deletedDate`
        /// has PASSED has been removed from the current GVL revision.
        /// Per the IAB contract deletion applies AFTER that instant,
        /// so enforcement denies it from then on (Task 9 Step 1
        /// short-circuit) while a FUTURE-dated vendor stays
        /// authorized until the instant passes — matching the CMP
        /// deletion comparator (`deleted_date <= now`).
        pub fn is_deleted_at(&self, now: OffsetDateTime) -> bool {
            matches!(self.deleted_date, Some(d) if d <= now)
        }

        pub fn declares_purpose_for_consent(
            &self,
            p: u8,
            restriction: Option<PubRestrictionType>,
        ) -> bool {
            match restriction {
                // Round-36 H1: restriction overrides declared basis.
                Some(PubRestrictionType::NotAllowed) => false,
                Some(PubRestrictionType::RequireConsent) => {
                    // Must have declared consent OR flex.
                    self.purposes.contains(&p) || self.flex_purposes.contains(&p)
                }
                Some(PubRestrictionType::RequireLegitInterest) => {
                    // LI required — consent path is
                    // suppressed regardless of the vendor's
                    // declaration.
                    false
                }
                None => {
                    // No restriction — the vendor's DEFAULT declared
                    // basis governs (round-89 B1, reverts round-88 B2).
                    // Per the IAB vendor-list contract every flexible
                    // purpose ALSO has exactly one default in `purposes`
                    // XOR `legIntPurposes` (validator-enforced, Task 4);
                    // absent a publisher restriction ONLY that default
                    // applies. `flex_purposes` is consulted ONLY when a
                    // restriction SWITCHES the basis (the `RequireConsent`
                    // / `RequireLegitInterest` arms above). So the
                    // consent leg here is the CONSENT-default set only —
                    // a consent-default flex purpose is NOT LI-authorized
                    // (and vice versa) unless a restriction flips it. This
                    // fails closed on the privacy boundary; §15 records it
                    // as a DELIBERATE divergence from upstream (reference server
                    // `d7f8515` reference TCF legal-basis evaluation ORs consent+LI with
                    // no restriction — round-90 LOW).
                    self.purposes.contains(&p)
                }
            }
        }

        pub fn declares_purpose_for_li(
            &self,
            p: u8,
            restriction: Option<PubRestrictionType>,
        ) -> bool {
            match restriction {
                Some(PubRestrictionType::NotAllowed) => false,
                Some(PubRestrictionType::RequireLegitInterest) => {
                    self.leg_int_purposes.contains(&p) || self.flex_purposes.contains(&p)
                }
                Some(PubRestrictionType::RequireConsent) => {
                    // Consent required — LI path is
                    // suppressed regardless of declaration.
                    false
                }
                None => self.leg_int_purposes.contains(&p), // round-89 B1: default basis only absent a restriction (reverts round-88 B2); flex is switched only by a pub restriction
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    - `flex_purpose_require_li_allows_via_li()`.

  **Round-35 B7 — GVL revision selection (supersedes round-34
  H2's fallback-with-warn scheme, which violated the IAB
  requirement to use the EXACT list encoded in the TC
  string).** Two dimensions:

  **Spec-version selection.**
  - `tcfPolicyVersion < 4` → GVL spec version = **2**.
  - `tcfPolicyVersion >= 4` → GVL spec version = **3**.
    The round-34 draft always called `Gvl::from_baked(3, list)`,
    which rejects valid v2/policy-v3 combinations. Round-37 B2 +
    B4 code — resolver takes `&GvlStore` and returns
    `Result<_, PrivacyError>` (round-45 H1 — not `AuctionError`,
    a Cargo cycle):

  ```rust
  let gvl_spec = if tcf.tcf_policy_version < 4 { 2 } else { 3 };
  let (gvl, consent_usable) = match gvl_store.get(gvl_spec, tcf.vendor_list_version) {
      Some(g) => (g, true),   // owned cheap-clone Gvl; consent usable
      None => {
          // Round-52 Critical: FAIL CLOSED via the explicit
          // unusable-consent state, NOT via an empty GVL + the
          // normal walk (which vendor_exceptions / basic enforcement
          // bypass — see Task 9 Step 1 row 3 / Step 2). Set
          // `consent_usable = false` so `permissions()` returns the
          // deterministic A.4 default row before any per-bidder
          // evaluation. Push the warning onto the ACCUMULATED vector
          // (round-51 B2: preserving any gpp_sid-conflict warning).
          warnings.push(gvl_version_unavailable(
              gvl_spec, tcf.vendor_list_version));   // FREE fn
          (Gvl::empty(), false)                       // empty gvl is a
                                                      // placeholder; the
                                                      // short-circuit,
                                                      // not the gvl,
                                                      // enforces closure
      }
  };
  // ... the single PrivacyContext is built here with `gvl`,
  //     `consent_usable`, `per_purpose_effective`, `tcf`, aliases,
  //     `warnings`, and the cached `p2_enforced`/`sf1_enforced`.
  //     When `consent_usable == false`, `permissions()` returns the
  //     A.4 default row for EVERY bidder regardless of the gvl.
  ```

  **Round-52 Critical — the GVL-unavailable path fails closed via
  the explicit `consent_usable = false` state.** The round-51 draft
  substituted `Gvl::empty()` and claimed the normal `permissions()`
  walk would then yield the enforced-but-empty row "by
  construction". That is FALSE: `vendor_exceptions` (A.2 row 3 /
  A.3 row 2) and basic enforcement do NOT consult the GVL, so a
  bidder on either list would still get `PassID = true`. The empty
  GVL is retained only as a harmless placeholder value; the actual
  fail-closed guarantee is the `permissions()` short-circuit on
  `consent_usable`. The GVL-unavailable, malformed-TCF, and
  empty-consent cases all set `consent_usable = false` and share
  that one deterministic exit. `PrivacyContext::gvl_unavailable`,
  the round-50 `EffectiveEnforcement`, and the removed
  `default_permissions_with_warning` all stay gone.

  **Not-enforced traffic is unaffected.** When
  `enforcement_active == false` (master switch off, non-standard
  publisher, `Signal::No`, channel disabled) `resolve` already
  returned `allow_all_no_scrub()` BEFORE reaching GVL selection,
  so out-of-scope traffic keeps its IDs. Fail-closed applies only
  where the operator asked for enforcement.

  **List-version selection.** Round-35 B7 + round-36 B3 hard
  rule: use the EXACT `(spec, list)` encoded in the TC
  string OR fail closed via `gvl_unavailable` (round-50 B2).
  No newer/older fallback. Rationale: IAB requires vendors to be
  evaluated against the exact GVL revision the CMP consulted;
  substituting a different revision can change enforcement
  outcomes.

  **Selection sequence (round-36 B3):**
  1. Parse TC string → `TcfString` with
     `tcf_policy_version` + `vendor_list_version`.
  2. Compute required GVL spec: `if
tcf.tcf_policy_version < 4 { 2 } else { 3 }`.
  3. `store.get(spec, tcf.vendor_list_version)` →
     **`Option<Gvl>`** (round-50 B1 — OWNED, not `Option<&Gvl>`.
     The store parses behind an `Arc<OnceCell<Gvl>>` and clones
     the handle out; `Gvl` is an `Arc<GvlInner>` wrapper so the
     clone is a refcount bump. This is the single settled
     signature — see the `GvlStore` impl.)
  4. `None` → FAIL CLOSED by setting **`consent_usable = false`**
     (the resolver's second tuple element) and pushing
     `gvl_version_unavailable(spec, list)` onto the accumulated
     warnings (round-51 B1/B2). **Round-66 H1 — `consent_usable =
false` plus the `permissions()` pre-exception short-circuit is
     the SOLE fail-closed contract.** The `Gvl::empty()` handed back
     alongside it is an inert type-level placeholder; it does NOT
     drive the decision. Do NOT rely on "an empty GVL yields the
     default row" — that mechanism is RETIRED (it is unsafe:
     `vendor_exceptions` (A.2 row 3 / A.3 row 2) and basic
     enforcement do not consult the GVL, so the normal `permissions()`
     walk over an empty GVL could still grant `PassID`, per the
     Interfaces note above). When `consent_usable == false`,
     `permissions()` returns the deterministic A.4 default row
     (`AllowBidRequest=!P2`, `PassGeo=!SF1`, `PassID=false`) for EVERY
     bidder BEFORE any vendor-exception or basic-enforcement branch
     runs. Round-51 foundations: the old §5387 "auction core-permissive fallback"
     phrasing is RETIRED — it described the fail-OPEN behaviour
     round-50 B2 removed; only the diagnostic warning remains.
  5. `Some(gvl)` → additionally verify the policy version.
     **EXECUTION AMENDMENT (post-GO, ratified — do NOT restore the
     `==` form): the shipped check is
     `tcf.tcf_policy_version > gvl.tcf_policy_version()`, not
     equality.** Strict equality is unshippable: the live bundled
     spec-3 archive declares policy 5 while TCF v2.2 CMPs emit
     policy-4 strings, so `!=` marks EVERY v2.2 request unusable —
     a production-wide fail-closed on legitimate traffic (it also
     killed eight landed Task 8 tests). The asymmetric form fails
     closed in the genuinely dangerous direction — a string claiming
     a policy the bundled list PREDATES cannot be interpreted
     against it — while leaving the normal forward direction (newer
     list serving an older string) working. On that failure it
     behaves **exactly like the `None` branch (round-86 B3)** — set `consent_usable = false` and
     push `gvl_version_unavailable(spec, list)` onto the accumulated
     warnings. This is NOT a `TcfParseError` (that enum belongs to the
     TC-string parser, and `GvlStore::get` returns `Option<Gvl>`, not a
     `Result`) and introduces NO new `PrivacyError` variant (`resolve`
     returns `Result<_, PrivacyError>`, and a stale bundled blob is an
     operator/data condition, not a 400-worthy client input); it routes
     through the existing `consent_usable` short-circuit.

  **Global CMP List (GCL) artifact (round-98 H7, made EXECUTABLE
  end-to-end round-99 B1; semantics corrected round-99 B2/B3).** The
  TCF permits only REGISTERED CMPs (using their assigned id) to create
  TC strings, and — per the current IAB specification — a TC string
  from a CMP with a `deletedDate` becomes INVALID once that timestamp
  passes, regardless of when the string was created. auctioneer bundles the
  GCL alongside the GVL and validates `cmp_id` at resolve time (Task 8
  Step 2b). The COMPLETE contract:
  - **Artifact:** `data/gvl_archive/gcl.json` — the official Global CMP
    List (`https://cmplist.consensu.org/v2/cmp-list.json`). SMALL
    (~200 KB raw); `GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES = 1 MiB` bounds the fetch.
  - **Manifest field (round-99 B1):** the manifest schema gains a
    TOP-LEVEL `gcl` object alongside `entries`:
    ```json
    "gcl": { "path": "gcl.json",
             "sha256": "…64-hex…",
             "last_updated": "<upstream lastUpdated RFC3339>",
             "fetched_at": "<tool fetch instant RFC3339>",
             "cache_max_age_secs": 604800 }
    ```
    `cache_max_age_secs` records the upstream `Cache-Control: max-age`
    (the IAB requires honoring it; the list is published weekly, so
    the recorded value is typically ≤ 7 days). `validate_manifest`
    REQUIRES the `gcl` object (absent → `ManifestError::MissingGcl`),
    verifies the sha256 against the blob, and enforces FRESHNESS
    (round-99 B3 / round-100 B2 — the UPSTREAM lifetime EXACTLY, no
    floor and no extension: the IAB requires GCL requests to honor
    `Cache-Control` and forbids caching under different settings;
    `cache_max_age_secs` is the RFC 9111 Age/Date-corrected lifetime
    the refresh tool recorded — see refresh step 2b for the
    missing/invalid/conflicting/`no-cache`/`no-store` directive
    pinning): `now >= fetched_at + cache_max_age_secs` →
    `ManifestError::GclStale` — a HARD
    build failure, NOT the generic 45-day GVL window and NOT
    overrideable (the `--allow-oversize-bundle` age ack does NOT apply
    to the GCL).
  - **Refresh transaction (round-99 B1):** the refresh tool's numbered
    algorithm gains a step between the GVL fetches and manifest write:
    fetch the GCL, capture `Cache-Control`/`Last-Modified`, enforce
    `GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES`, run `validate_gcl_json`, write
    `$tx_dir/gcl.json`, and record the manifest `gcl` object. Same
    locking/atomic-swap/recovery rules as the GVL entries.
  - **Schema validation (`auctioneer-gvl-schema`, added to the crate's
    Contents list) — CANONICAL DTOs + errors (round-101 B2):**
    ```rust
    pub fn validate_gcl_json(raw: &str) -> Result<ValidatedGcl, GclSchemaError>;
    // DTO (serde side): RawGcl { lastUpdated: String,
    //                            cmps: BTreeMap<String, RawCmp> }
    //   RawCmp { id: u32, #[serde(default)] deletedDate: Option<String>,
    //            /* unknown fields ignored — NO deny_unknown_fields */ }
    // Validated: ValidatedGcl { last_updated: OffsetDateTime,
    //                           cmps: BTreeMap<u16, ValidatedCmp> }
    //   ValidatedCmp { id: u16, deleted_date: Option<OffsetDateTime> }
    pub enum GclSchemaError {
        InvalidJson(String),
        MalformedEntry { path: String },        // serde_path_to_error, like the GVL
        MissingLastUpdated,                     // root lastUpdated REQUIRED
        BadTimestamp { path: String, raw: String },
        NonNumericMapKey { key: String },       // map keys must parse as integers
        IdKeyMismatch { map_key: String, embedded_id: u32 },
        CmpIdOutOfRange { id: u32 },            // CmpId is a 12-bit NONZERO
                                                // domain: 1..=4095 (matches the
                                                // TC string's 12-bit CmpId field)
    }
    ```
    Invariants (round-102 H9 — each REACHABLE and defined): root
    `lastUpdated` is `Option<String>` on `RawGcl` with an explicit
    `.ok_or(GclSchemaError::MissingLastUpdated)?` (a required `String`
    would surface as a serde error and make the variant unreachable);
    every `cmps` map key parses numerically AND equals its entry's
    embedded `id`; ids ∈ `1..=4095`; `deletedDate` parsed when
    present; unknown fields tolerated. `parse_rfc3339` and
    `check_sha256_format` are the SAME shared helpers
    `validate_manifest` already uses (one definition, schema crate).
    `GclRecord::expires_at()` uses CHECKED addition
    (`fetched_at.checked_add(Duration::seconds(i64::try_from(
cache_max_age_secs)…))` → `BadTimestamp` on overflow);
    `fetched_at > now` → `ManifestError::FutureTimestamp`; and
    `validate_manifest` CROSS-CHECKS `manifest.gcl.last_updated ==
validated_gcl.last_updated` (mismatch → a typed error — the
    manifest may not disagree with the blob it points at).
  - **Build gate + accessor (round-99 B1; names unified round-107
    H6):** `auctioneer-config`'s build.rs validates the GCL exactly like
    GVL entries (sha, schema, freshness via `validate_manifest`) and

  - **Runtime owner (round-105 B1 — the CONCRETE module):**
    `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/gcl.rs` (created by Task 4 Step 2c —
    a REAL numbered step as of round-106 B1 — declared
    `pub mod gcl;` in lib.rs):
    ```rust

    pub struct Gcl { pub cmps: BTreeMap<u16, CmpRecord>,
    ```

  **Refresh tool.** `crates/auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive/` is a
  standalone workspace crate — NOT a `auctioneer-config` feature
  or bin (the round-37 draft's `--features gen-manifest
--bin gen-gvl-manifest` shape referenced a feature and
  binary that were never declared). Layout:

  ```
  crates/auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive/
      Cargo.toml
      src/main.rs
  ```

  `Cargo.toml` (round-42 B9 canonical, retires round-38
  B2's shape which omitted `clap` despite the tool's
  Parser derive and had no `auctioneer-config` dep despite
  importing `gvl_schema`; round-42 B9 also BREAKS the
  bootstrap cycle by hosting the shared manifest
  validator in a NEW `auctioneer-gvl-schema` crate that
  neither `auctioneer-config` nor the tool depend on
  transitively):

  ```toml
  [package]
  name = "auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive"
  description = "Fetches IAB GVL archives and regenerates auctioneer-config's manifest."
  authors = { workspace = true }
  edition = { workspace = true }
  license = { workspace = true }
  publish = { workspace = true }
  version = { workspace = true }

  [dependencies]
  anyhow    = "1"
  chrono    = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["clock", "serde"] }
  clap      = { workspace = true, features = ["derive"] }   # round-42 B9
  fs2       = { workspace = true }   # round-61 B3: the exclusive refresh lock (round-60 H2)
  auctioneer-gvl-schema = { path = "../../crates/auctioneer-gvl-schema" }   # round-42 B9
  reqwest   = { version = "0.12", features = ["blocking", "json", "gzip"] }  # round-104 B4: without `gzip`, compressed bytes reach the JSON reader
  serde     = { workspace = true }
  serde_json = { workspace = true }
  sha2      = "0.10"
  ```

  **Round-61 B3 — declaring `fs2` in `[workspace.dependencies]` is
  NOT enough; each consuming crate must ALSO list `fs2 = { workspace
= true }` in its own `[dependencies]`** (a workspace dep is a
  version registry, not an implicit import). It appears here for the
  tool AND in `auctioneer-config`'s `[build-dependencies]` (round-60 H2)
  so `build.rs` can take the same lock.

  **Bootstrap cycle broken by extracting a new crate**
  (round-42 B9). Round-38 planned to have the refresh
  tool import `auctioneer_config::gvl_schema::validate_manifest`,
  but that dep cycle means: if the checked-in
  archive is broken, `auctioneer-config/build.rs` fails →
  can't build `auctioneer-config` → can't build the refresh
  tool → deployer can't repair the archive. Round-42 B9
  moves the shared validator into a new
  `crates/auctioneer-gvl-schema` crate that:
  - Has NO dependency on `auctioneer-config`.
  - Has NO `build.rs` that could break.
  - Contains only the pure Rust `validate_manifest`,
    `validate_gvl_json`, and the schema types.
    Both `auctioneer-config` (via its `build.rs` +
    library re-export) AND the refresh tool depend on
    `auctioneer-gvl-schema`. The refresh tool builds even when
    the archive is broken; running it repairs the archive
    so `auctioneer-config` builds next time.

  Spec §2.1 dep row for `auctioneer-config` gains
  `auctioneer-gvl-schema`; add `auctioneer-privacy` as well since
  the runtime lowering path already re-imports the
  schema types.
  Added to the workspace's `[workspace]` members list.
  **Round-66 B1 — the workspace-dep additions are done ONCE in Step
  0a-preflight above** (`serde_path_to_error` / `brotli` / `hex` /
  `sha2` / `fs2` + the `time` feature union). The tool's own manifest
  version-pins `chrono` / `reqwest` / `anyhow` / `sha2` DIRECTLY (they
  are not `{ workspace = true }`), so those need no workspace entry
  for the tool; `sha2` + `fs2` are in the table because
  `auctioneer-config`'s `[build-dependencies]` inherit them via
  `{ workspace = true }`. `auctioneer-config`'s `[build-dependencies]`
  gains `fs2` so `build.rs` can take the same lock before its
  `.old.* → live` recovery. `sha256` (the
  standalone crate) is NOT used — the plan uses `sha2` (the
  workspace standard) and computes SHA-256 via `sha2::Sha256::
digest(...)`.

  `src/main.rs` responsibilities (single binary — no
  `--features` gating needed because it lives in its own
  crate). **Round-58 H3 / round-59 H2 — build atomically with crash
  recovery: ALL writes go to a fresh temporary sibling directory
  the run's UNIQUE `$tx_dir` (`data/.gvl_refresh.<pid>.<n>/`, round-63 H1 — NOT a fixed `.tmp`), the ENTIRE result is validated, and only
  then does the tool swap it into place.**
  - **Failure safety (network/validation):** any failure before the
    swap leaves the checked-in `data/gvl_archive/` byte-for-byte
    untouched (the temp dir is discarded).
  - **Concurrency safety — a PERSISTENT advisory lock (round-60 H2 /
    round-61 B4).** The recovery-from-`.old` and the two-rename swap
    MUST be serialised, or they race: a `build.rs` that recovers
    `.old → live` in the gap between the refresh's two renames makes
    the refresh's second rename fail, and two concurrent refreshes
    clobber each other. Protocol:
    - **The lock is a PERSISTENT `fs2` advisory `flock` on a
      checked-in sentinel file `data/gvl_archive.lock` that is NEVER
      unlinked.** (Round-61 B4 — do NOT use an `O_EXCL` create-a-file
      lock: that leaves a STALE lockfile if the holder crashes, and
      the next process then can neither take the lock NOR recover.
      An `fs2` advisory `flock` is released automatically by the OS
      when the holding process dies, so a crash never wedges the
      next run.) The file is committed to the repo (0 bytes) so it
      always exists; a `.gitignore` entry is the alternative but a
      committed sentinel is simpler and can't go missing.
    - **EVERY archive read, recovery, and swap holds the lock**
      (round-61 B4 — the round-60 draft let `build.rs` read `live`
      WITHOUT the lock, which can observe the absent-`live` gap
      between the two renames). The refresh tool takes the lock
      **EXCLUSIVE** for the recovery + swap; `build.rs::
emit_gvl_archive` reads under a **SHARED** lock — and because
      **`fs2` has NO portable lock UPGRADE** (its docs warn lock
      behaviour varies by platform; a shared→exclusive upgrade is
      not guaranteed atomic and can deadlock), round-62 B2 replaces
      the round-61 "upgrade" with the explicit **drop-and-reacquire**
      dance. **The read ALWAYS happens under a HELD lock (round-63
      H2 — there is no unlocked read window):**
      (1) take the SHARED lock and inspect state.
      (2) **Common case — `live` present, no recovery:** READ the
      archive while STILL HOLDING the shared lock, then release. The
      read never leaves the shared lock.
      (3) **Recovery case — `live` missing:** release the shared
      lock; acquire the lock **EXCLUSIVE** (blocking); **re-check all
      state** (another process may have recovered/swapped in the
      gap); run the `.old → live` recovery only if still necessary;
      then READ the archive while STILL HOLDING the exclusive lock;
      only then release. (Round-63 H2 — the round-62 draft released
      the exclusive lock and THEN read, an unlocked window a
      concurrent refresh's swap could race; keeping the read under
      the held exclusive closes it.)
      build.rs never holds two locks and never relies on an upgrade
      primitive. A reader never sees a half-swapped tree because the
      refresh holds EXCLUSIVE across both renames AND build.rs holds
      a lock across its own read.
    - **TWO locks, one protocol (round-61 B4, REPLACED round-105
      B4):** the refresh tool holds the run-wide EXCLUSIVE
      `data/refresh.lock` for the WHOLE run (cache decisions,
      downloads, tx build — serializing concurrent refreshes so
      upstream cache periods see at most one request), while the
      ARCHIVE lock (`data/gvl_archive.lock`) is taken only for the
      fast recovery + swap window — so a normal BUILD (which takes
      only the archive lock) never waits through a network fetch.
      The refresh builds its **unique transaction directory**
      `data/.gvl_refresh.<pid>.<n>/` under `refresh.lock` but with
      NO archive lock held, and only THEN acquires the EXCLUSIVE
      archive lock for the recovery + swap (two renames) + cleanup.
      A second refresh that can't take
      the EXCLUSIVE lock at swap time exits with "refresh already
      running" and discards its transaction dir; it never touches
      `live`.
  - **Crash safety — ONE FIXED aside path (round-62 B3).** The swap
    uses a **single fixed `data/gvl_archive.old`** (NOT a per-pid
    `.old.<id>`), which is safe because the swap only ever runs under
    the EXCLUSIVE lock, so at most one aside dir exists at a time.
    (Round-62 B3 — unique `.old.*` names made recovery
    NONDETERMINISTIC: a crash after installing the new `live` but
    before deleting the old aside leaves a stale generation, and a
    later crash could leave TWO `.old.*` siblings with no way to know
    which is authoritative.) Under the lock:
    `rename(live → gvl_archive.old)` then `rename(tx → live)`;
    `sync_all` the parent after each; then delete `gvl_archive.old`.
    **Deterministic recovery** (run by the next EXCLUSIVE-lock
    holder), keyed only on `gvl_archive.old` existing:
    - `live` PRESENT + `gvl_archive.old` present → the crash was
      AFTER the second rename (new archive is already installed and
      complete); just **delete** the stale `gvl_archive.old`. Do NOT
      restore it.
    - `live` ABSENT + `gvl_archive.old` present → the crash was
      BETWEEN the renames; **`rename(gvl_archive.old → live)`**.
    - `live` present + no `gvl_archive.old` → nothing to do.
    - **`live` ABSENT + no `gvl_archive.old` → FIRST INSTALL / clean
      empty state (round-63 B2)** → nothing to recover; the swap
      (step 11) installs `tx_dir → live` DIRECTLY, skipping the
      `live → old` rename (there is no `live` to move aside — the
      repo ships no `gvl_archive/`, so the very first refresh hits
      exactly this state and the unconditional `live → old` rename
      would otherwise fail with `ENOENT`).
      A single fixed name means these FOUR cases are exhaustive and
      unambiguous. `File::open(parent_dir)?.sync_all()` after each
      rename makes the directory entry durable. Net: a crash at any
      point leaves EITHER the old or the new COMPLETE archive at
      `live`, never a half-written tree and never an ambiguous choice.
  - **Step 0 — acquire `data/refresh.lock` (EXCLUSIVE, round-105 B4
    — REPLACES the round-61 "no lock" reset), then reset:** take the
    run lock FIRST (fail "refresh already running" if held), then
    create this run's fresh unique transaction dir `$tx_dir =
data/.gvl_refresh.<pid>.<n>/` and use `$tx_dir` in EVERY step
    below (round-63 H1 — no step uses a fixed path). Every numbered
    step runs under `refresh.lock`; the ARCHIVE lock is taken only
    at step 11. The fixed
    `gvl_archive.old` is touched only under the archive lock at step 11,
    never here. **Own-tx-only cleanup (round-65 H3 — supersedes the
    round-63 H1 pid/mtime heuristic, which was unsafe on three counts:
    (a) `$tx_dir` carries THIS process's pid, so a "delete if `<pid>`
    matches" rule would delete the current transaction itself; (b)
    pid reuse means a stale dir's pid may belong to an unrelated live
    process; (c) nothing keeps a live refresh's `$tx_dir` mtime fresh
    during a multi-second download — the OS does not bump mtime just
    because a process is alive — so the "6h + live-pid" test could
    delete an in-flight concurrent refresh's tx dir).** The rule is
    now simply: **a refresh deletes ONLY its own `$tx_dir`, by exact
    path, and NEVER enumerates or removes any other `.gvl_refresh.*`
    sibling.** This run removes `$tx_dir` on BOTH exit paths — after a
    successful step-11 swap, and on any failure/discard (step 11's
    "discard `tx_dir`" arm). A crash before that leaves one orphaned
    `data/.gvl_refresh.<pid>.<n>/` behind; that is bounded (one per
    crashed run), git-ignored (`data/.gvl_refresh.*` is in
    `.gitignore` — round-65 H3), and harmless — no run ever touches
    another run's tx dir, so no PID-reuse, liveness-probe, or
    mtime-freshness assumption is relied on anywhere. Steps 1-10
    (fetch + validate) run WITHOUT the lock. The EXCLUSIVE lock is
    acquired only at step 11, wrapping recovery + swap + own-tx
    cleanup, so a concurrent `build.rs` (holding a SHARED lock) never
    waits through the network download.
  - **Notation:** in the numbered steps below, `.tmp/` is shorthand
    for THIS run's unique transaction dir
    (`data/.gvl_refresh.<pid>.<n>/`, written lock-free) and `.old/`
    for the SINGLE FIXED aside dir `data/gvl_archive.old/` (round-62
    B3 — one path, touched only inside the step-11 exclusive
    section).
  - **Deterministic recovery tests (round-60 H2 / round-61 B4 /
    round-62 B3 / round-63 B2):**
    `first_refresh_with_no_existing_archive_installs_directly()`
    (round-63 B2 — run against an EMPTY `data/` with no
    `gvl_archive/`; assert the swap installs `tx_dir → live`
    directly, never attempting the `live → old` rename, and `live`
    ends up complete), `recovery_restores_old_when_live_absent()`
    (round-88 H3 — leaves `.old` present + `live` absent, calls
    `auctioneer_gvl_schema::recover_gvl_archive` DIRECTLY, and asserts `live`
    is restored from `.old`; the direct unit test of the shared helper
    that build.rs's recovery branch and refresh step 11 both invoke),
    `crash_after_second_rename_deletes_stale_old_keeps_new_live()`
    (round-62 B3 — `live` present + `gvl_archive.old` present → the
    new archive is kept, the stale aside is deleted, NOT restored),
    `refresh_is_rejected_while_lock_held()`,
    `build_rs_drops_shared_then_takes_exclusive_to_recover()`
    (round-62 B2 — no lock upgrade),
    `build_rs_does_not_mutate_archive_while_refresh_lock_held()`, and
    `dead_holder_advisory_lock_does_not_wedge_next_run()` — each
    simulates the crash/interleaving by leaving the on-disk state a
    real run would and asserting the deterministic outcome. With the
    fixed `gvl_archive.old`, "two old generations" is
    unrepresentable, so there is no ambiguous-recovery case to test.
  0. **Round-104 B2: acquire `data/refresh.lock` (EXCLUSIVE) FIRST —
     before the tx dir is created, before any cache read, before any
     network access.** Every numbered step below runs under it; it is
     released only after step 11's swap completes (or on abort). The
     ARCHIVE lock (`gvl_archive.lock`) remains a separate, short
     recovery/swap-window lock — the "downloads happen outside the
     lock" rule refers to the ARCHIVE lock ONLY.
  1. Compute the target date window: `retain_from =
chrono::Utc::now() - Duration::days(max_age_days)`.
  2. Discover the current spec-3 version — **round-104 B3: reusing
     the recorded cache lifetime first.** `ManifestEntry` gains two
     OPTIONAL fields (serde-default `None` on `RawEntry`):
     `fetched_at: Option<OffsetDateTime>` + `cache_max_age_secs:
Option<u64>`, recorded on the CURRENT-list entry by this step.
     If the LIVE manifest's newest spec-3 entry has both and
     `now < fetched_at + lifetime`, REUSE it (no network — the IAB
     requires reusing the current GVL for its advertised max-age).
     Otherwise fetch `https://vendor-list.consensu.org/v3/vendor-list.
json` (gzip, bounded read) and record the RFC 9111 lifetime on
     its entry (same directive rules as step 2b).
     2b. **Round-99 B1 / round-100 B2 / round-102 H10 / round-103 B5:
     fetch the Global CMP List AT MOST ONCE PER CACHE PERIOD, under
     the REFRESH-RUN lock.** Round-103 B5 splits the locking: a NEW
     `data/refresh.lock` sentinel (exclusive, held by the TOOL for the
     WHOLE run — cache decisions, all downloads, tx build) serializes
     concurrent refresh runs WITHOUT blocking builds (builds never
     take `refresh.lock`); the existing `data/gvl_archive.lock` is
     held only for the recovery/swap window (and by build.rs readers)
     — the earlier "downloads happen outside the lock" rule refers to
     the ARCHIVE lock and still holds. Under `refresh.lock`: FIRST
     read the LIVE manifest's `gcl` record — if `now < expires_at`,
     REUSE the existing `gcl.json` (copy the blob into `$tx_dir`,
     carry the record forward unchanged; NO network request — the IAB
     permits only one request per cache period; the run lock makes
     concurrent duplicate fetches impossible). Only when the record is
     absent or expired, fetch from
     `https://cmplist.consensu.org/v2/cmp-list.json`. Capture the
     response's `Cache-Control`, `Age`, and `Date` headers. Enforce
     `GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES = 1 MiB` **on the DECODED stream via a
     bounded read (round-108 shared auction foundations — the cap must be
     allocation-bounded, not asserted after the fact): wrap the
     response reader (reqwest's gzip feature decodes transparently,
     so `take` applies post-decompression) in
     `.take(GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES + 1)`, read into a
     `Vec::with_capacity(GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES + 1)` (`read_to_end` on
     the capped reader cannot grow past it), and FAIL when
     `bytes.len() > GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES` — the DECODED OUTPUT buffer
     never materializes more than cap + 1 bytes (round-109 diagnostic qualification: that
     is the bound this design controls; HTTP transport buffers and
     the gzip decoder's internal state ride ON TOP as bounded
     library overhead, and the earlier "peak allocation ≤ cap + 1"
     wording overclaimed). Refresh-tool test (uncounted per the tool
     convention): `gcl_compressed_bomb_rejected_at_cap()` — a small
     gzip body inflating past 1 MiB is rejected; the test asserts
     (a) the decoded buffer's capacity stays exactly cap + 1, and
     (b) total allocation stays within an explicit BASELINE + FIXED
     DECODER ALLOWANCE, where the baseline is measured by running
     the same fetch path on a small (1 KiB decoded) response —
     bounding the overhead by MEASUREMENT rather than assertion**;
     run `validate_gcl_json`; write
     `$tx_dir/gcl.json`; record the manifest `gcl` object with
     `fetched_at` (tool clock) and the freshness lifetime computed
     STRICTLY per RFC 9111 from the upstream headers (round-100 B2 /
     round-101 H8 — NO floor, NO extension): `current_age` is computed
     per RFC 9111 §4.2.3 (the `Age` header plus response delay against
     `Date`), and `lifetime = max_age - current_age`. Directive
     pinning (round-101 H8 / round-103 B3 / round-106 shared auction foundations — corrected
     to RFC 9111 precedence, INCLUDING the shared-cache directive):
     the refresh tool behaves as a SHARED cache, so **`s-maxage` takes
     precedence over `max-age` when present** (lifetime = s-maxage −
     current_age); a duplicated, malformed, or conflicting `s-maxage`
     fails exactly like the `max-age` rules below; a DUPLICATED
     `max-age` directive → the refresh FAILS
     (fail-closed arm of RFC 9111's first-occurrence-or-stale rule);
     **`no-cache` → FAIL** (reuse requires successful revalidation,
     which a baked offline artifact cannot perform); **`no-store` →
     FAIL** (the response may not be persisted at all — bundling it
     would violate the directive); **an INVALID `max-age` value →
     FAIL** (round-104 H8 — invalid freshness information is stale
     per RFC 9111 §4.2.1, NOT "as if absent"); `Expires - Date` is
     consulted ONLY when `Cache-Control` carries no freshness
     directive AT ALL (max-age/s-maxage ABSENT, no
     `no-cache`/`no-store` — Expires is lower-precedence, never an
     override); otherwise-missing lifetime
     → the refresh FAILS telling the operator to verify upstream
     headers; `current_age >= max_age` at fetch (stale on arrival) →
     the refresh FAILS. Per the IAB GCL contract the tool sends
     `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (compressed retrieval), applies
     `GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES` to the DECODED bytes, and — because the
     recorded `expires_at` gates the next build — never re-fetches
     within a cache period (one request per period, satisfied by the
     weekly refresh cadence). `expires_at = fetched_at + lifetime`.
  3. **Round-90 B2: reserve the mandatory pair FIRST, then fill
     newest-first under a size budget — retention is size-bounded, not
     age-alone (see the Retention policy block below for why 180 days
     does NOT fit).** Establish the canonical raw cap. **Round-92 privacy enforcement —
     ONE source of truth: the refresh cap is `min(env, 24 MiB)` and an
     env value ABOVE 24 MiB is REJECTED with an error** (the GDPR enforcement shared
     archive feeds all four adapters and must fit the wasm hard max —
     round-91 privacy enforcement; honoring a larger env value here while the contract
     below says "always 24 MiB" was a contradiction). Concretely:
     `raw_cap = AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB` when set —
     but if it exceeds 24 MiB, print an error citing the round-91 privacy enforcement
     single-artifact rule and exit non-zero (an env value may only
     LOWER the cap); else the wasm default of 24 MiB. The budget
     subtraction (`raw_cap.checked_sub(GROWTH_MARGIN)`, default
     `GROWTH_MARGIN` = 4 MiB) happens INSIDE
     `select_retained_versions(candidates, reserved, raw_cap,
growth_margin, cutoff)` (round-92 GDPR enforcement — the tool passes the two
     values through UNCOMBINED so the helper's `BudgetUnderflow`
     variant is actually reachable and unit-testable). Then:
     a. **RESERVE the frozen spec-2 list** (the final TCF v2.2 GVL,
     `lastUpdated` 2023-11-16 — the only spec-2 version IAB will ever
     publish) fetched from `/v2/`, and **RESERVE the newest spec-3
     version** (the current `/v3/vendor-list.json` from step 2). Both
     are kept UNCONDITIONALLY so the corpus always satisfies step 10's
     mandatory spec-2 + spec-3 coverage. The frozen spec-2 list is
     **AGE-EXEMPT**: it is older than any `--max-age-days` window by
     design, so the age filter is NEVER applied to it
     (`validate_manifest` grants the same spec-2 exemption —
     round-90 B2).
     b. **Fail closed if the reserved pair ALONE exceeds the budget:**
     `select_retained_versions` returns
     `RetentionError::BudgetUnderflow` when `raw_cap < growth_margin`
     or `ReservedPairOverBudget` when `frozen_v2_bytes +
 newest_v3_bytes > raw_cap - growth_margin` (round-92 GDPR enforcement — both
     computed INSIDE the helper); on either error the tool prints it
     (naming both sizes, `GROWTH_MARGIN`, and
     `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB`), removes `$tx_dir`,
     and exits non-zero. This is a HARD build error — a mandatory
     version is NEVER silently dropped to fit.
     3c. **Round-103 B5 — GVL fetches honor caching too:** archived
     versions already present in the LIVE archive (same
     `(spec, version)` with a matching `sha256`) are REUSED (copied
     into `$tx_dir`) instead of refetched; all GVL requests send
     `Accept-Encoding: gzip` with the same bounded decoded read as the
     GCL; and the CURRENT `vendor-list.json` fetch records its
     `Cache-Control`-derived lifetime in the manifest entry metadata
     (same RFC 9111 rules as step 2b) so future tooling can observe
     upstream cache intent. All under `refresh.lock`.
  4. **Age-filter, then fill the ARCHIVED spec-3 candidates newest-first
     under the remaining budget.** Walk backwards through
     `/v3/archives/vendor-list-vN.json` (newest first, EXCLUDING the
     already-reserved newest v3). For each candidate, fetch it and read
     its `lastUpdated` FIRST: **if `lastUpdated < retain_from`, STOP —
     every older archive is out of the age window** (round-86 B4).
     Otherwise add the candidate ONLY while the running raw total
     (reserved pair + candidates accepted so far + this candidate) stays
     `<= size_budget`; the first candidate that would cross the budget
     ENDS the fill (versions are contiguous by recency, so there is no
     skip-and-continue). Persist each accepted candidate to
     **`$tx_dir/spec3/vendor-list-vN.json`** (this run's unique tx dir —
     round-63 H1, the temp dir, NOT the live archive). Because both the
     age filter and the size budget admit only versions with
     `lastUpdated >= retain_from`, every accepted spec-3 entry satisfies
     the validator's `age <= max_age_days` check.
  5. The keep set is exactly the reserved pair plus the accepted spec-3
     candidates now in the temp dir; there is no in-place deletion of the
     live archive (round-38 H2's "drop stale versions" is achieved by the
     temp dir containing ONLY the keep set — the atomic swap in step 11
     replaces the whole directory, so stale versions never carry over).
  6. Compute SHA-256 for every kept file via `sha2::Sha256`.
  7. Reject duplicates: iterate the kept-file list; two
     entries with the same `(spec, vendor_list_version)`
     pair → error. Reject `spec` not in `{2, 3}`. Reject
     zero or negative `vendor_list_version` (parse into
     `u32`, then check `> 0`).
  8. Constrain manifest `path` to `^spec[23]/vendor-list-
v\d+\.json$` (no directory traversal, no absolute
     paths — round-38 H2 hardening).
  9. Write `$tx_dir/manifest.json` with keys ordered
     as in the schema above (`manifest_version`, `generated_at`,
     `retention`, **the `gcl` object (round-105 B5 — path/sha256/
     last_updated/fetched_at/cache_max_age_secs from step 2b)**,
     `entries` sorted by `(spec asc, vendor_list_version desc)` —
     including each entry's OPTIONAL `fetched_at`/`cache_max_age_secs`
     cache metadata where recorded (step 2).
  10. **Round-58 H3 — validate the ENTIRE temp result BEFORE
      touching the live archive.** Run
      `auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_manifest(tmp_manifest, now)` and,
      for every entry, `validate_gvl_json(entry_bytes,
Some(entry.spec))` + SHA-256 re-check, **and (round-105 B5) the
      GCL leg: re-check `gcl.json`'s decoded size against
      `GCL_MAX_RAW_BYTES`, its SHA-256 against `manifest.gcl.sha256`,
      run `validate_gcl_json`, and run
      `check_gcl_consistency(&manifest, &validated_gcl)`** — ALL
      before swap. If ANY step 0–10 fails
      (network error, duplicate/out-of-range entry, schema/spec
      rejection, checksum mismatch, GCL failure), print the error,
      remove `$tx_dir`, and exit non-zero — the live
      `data/gvl_archive/` is unchanged.
  11. **Acquire the EXCLUSIVE lock, recover, swap (two renames +
      fsync — round-59 H2 / round-60 H2 / round-61 B4 / round-62
      B3).** Only after step 10 succeeds: take the EXCLUSIVE `fs2`
      lock on `data/gvl_archive.lock` (fail with "refresh already
      running" + discard `tx_dir` if it can't be taken). While
      holding it: first run the **fixed-`gvl_archive.old` recovery**
      (the four-case rule above — heals a prior crashed run). Then
      the swap, which is conditional on whether `live` exists
      (round-63 B2): **if `live` is present**,
      `fs::rename(live, "data/gvl_archive.old")` then
      `fs::rename(tx_dir, live)` then delete `data/gvl_archive.old`;
      **if `live` is ABSENT (first install / clean state)**, skip the
      aside rename and `fs::rename(tx_dir, live)` DIRECTLY — the
      unconditional `live → old` rename would fail with `ENOENT` on
      the very first refresh (the repo ships no `gvl_archive/`).
      `sync_all` the parent dir after each rename; release the lock.
      Each
      `rename` is individually atomic, but the PAIR is not — a crash
      between them leaves the data only at `gvl_archive.old`, which
      the next EXCLUSIVE-lock holder (a later refresh, or `build.rs`
      after its drop-and-reacquire, round-62 B2) heals via the same
      fixed-path recovery. The advisory lock is released by the OS on
      crash, so the next run is never wedged. Crash-SAFE (always
      recoverable to a complete archive), NOT a single atomic op — do
      not claim the two renames are jointly atomic.

  Retention policy (round-41 B8 canonical, retires
  round-39/40's split 180/400 defaults which contradicted
  each other across sections):

  **Round-89 H4 — retention is SIZE-BOUNDED, not age-alone, because 180
  days does NOT fit comfortably.** Measured: v3 versions 147–172 + the
  frozen v2 list = **23,617,656 bytes RAW against the 25,165,824-byte
  (24 MiB) raw cap — only ~1.55 MB headroom (~2 weekly versions).** Since
  IAB publishes a new GVL ~weekly (~900 KB raw each), a fixed 180-day
  retention would BLOW the raw cap within ~2 weeks and break every build.
  So the refresh tool retains **newest-first up to a SIZE budget =
  `raw_cap.checked_sub(GROWTH_MARGIN)` (default margin 4 MiB, ~4–5 weeks),
  AND at most `--max-age-days` old — whichever bound is hit first**, per
  the deterministic reserve-then-fill algorithm in refresh steps 3–5
  above (round-90 B2): the frozen spec-2 list and the newest spec-3
  version are reserved UNCONDITIONALLY (the frozen v2 is age-exempt), the
  archived spec-3 candidates are age-filtered then added newest-first
  while the running raw total stays `<= raw_cap.checked_sub(GROWTH_MARGIN)`,
  and if the reserved (v2 + newest v3) pair ALONE exceeds the budget the
  refresh FAILS with a hard error rather than dropping a mandatory
  version. The canonical `raw_cap` is the SAME
  `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB` build.rs enforces (unset →
  the most-constrained wasm default of 24 MiB). This keeps
  the build green through normal weekly growth without operator action;
  the age bound is the ceiling, the size budget is the sustainable floor.
  Dropped-but-referenced versions fall through to the empty-GVL
  fail-closed path (enforced-but-empty, round-51 B1/B2) with a
  `gvl_version_unavailable` warning + counter increment. IAB TCF allows
  TC strings up to ~13 months (~400 days); reaching that needs the
  oversize opt-in below. **The `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB`
  build gate stays HARD** — it is the backstop if the size-budget math is
  ever wrong.
  - **Build test (round-89 H4):** `generated_180d_corpus_under_raw_cap()`
    — generate the retention corpus at the default and assert the RAW
    bundle is `<= raw_cap − GROWTH_MARGIN` (proves the size-budget logic
    actually keeps margin, and catches the day the fixed weekly growth
    would otherwise cross the cap). Owned by Task 4's refresh-tool suite.

  **Executable opt-in for full-cadence retention:** the
  refresh tool accepts `--max-age-days N
--allow-oversize-bundle` where N > 180. Without
  `--allow-oversize-bundle`, `--max-age-days > 180`
  fails with a pointer to this section. With the flag
  set:
  - The tool writes `manifest.oversize_bundle_ack: true`.
    **Round-90 B3: the ack relaxes the AGE filter ONLY** — it
    records that the operator accepted spec-3 entries older
    than 180 days; it does NOT skip build.rs's raw-bundle cap.
    (The frozen spec-2 list is age-exempt regardless — round-90
    B2; older SPEC-3 entries are what the ack admits.)
  - **Round-91 privacy enforcement — the committed archive MUST fit the 24 MiB wasm
    hard max in GDPR enforcement; there is NO native-only extended-retention
    option.** All four adapters consume the SAME checked-in
    `data/gvl_archive/`, and Task 23's capability gate release-builds
    Axum AND all three wasm adapters — so an archive over 24 MiB
    cannot pass the capability regardless of a raised native cap. The
    round-90 "raise to 80 MiB, native-only, 400 days" pathway is
    therefore REMOVED from GDPR enforcement: the refresh tool's size budget is
    always computed against the 24 MiB wasm bound (round-92 privacy enforcement — the
    reserve-then-fill algorithm's step 3 ENFORCES it: an env cap above
    24 MiB is rejected with an error, the env can only LOWER the cap),
    and
    `--allow-oversize-bundle`'s practical effect in GDPR enforcement is admitting
    OLDER-but-still-fitting spec-3 entries (age > 180 within the same
    24 MiB budget), not a bigger bundle. Full-cadence ~400-day
    retention (~80 MiB) requires SEPARATE per-target archive
    artifacts — a deferred post-GDPR enforcement capability, recorded here so the
    single-artifact constraint is explicit. The compressed cap
    (`AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_MIB`) is likewise
    checked unconditionally — if the compressed bundle blows the
    platform's deploy ceiling, the build still fails.

  Refresh-tool CLI subtask:

  ```rust
  #[derive(clap::Parser)]
  struct Cli {
      /// Retain archive entries this many days back.
      /// Default 180. Values > 180 require
      /// --allow-oversize-bundle (round-41 B8).
      #[arg(long, default_value_t = 180)]
      max_age_days: u32,
      /// Round-41 B8: acknowledges retention past 180 days.
      /// Round-90 B3: records the acknowledgement in
      /// manifest.oversize_bundle_ack, which relaxes the AGE
      /// filter only — build.rs still enforces the raw-bundle
      /// cap on every build (and the wasm 24 MiB hard max).
      #[arg(long)]
      allow_oversize_bundle: bool,
  }
  ```

  New manifest field:

  ```json
  {
    ...,
    "oversize_bundle_ack": false
  }
  ```

  `validate_manifest` reads it; the refresh tool uses it to
  admit spec-3 entries older than 180 days. **Round-90 B3: it
  no longer gates the raw-cap check — `emit_gvl_archive`
  enforces the raw cap unconditionally.**
  Regression tests:
  - `refresh_tool_max_age_days_181_without_flag_errors()`.
  - `refresh_tool_max_age_days_400_with_flag_writes_ack_true()`.
  - **Round-91 H3 — the raw-cap enforcement tests live in
    `crates/auctioneer-gvl-schema/tests/schema.rs` (they exercise the pure
    `validate_bundle_limits`, NOT build.rs, which cannot host unit
    tests; the refresh crate cannot import a build script):**
    - `bundle_over_cap_rejected_even_when_ack_true()` (round-90 B3 —
      `validate_bundle_limits("x86_64", cap, cap + 1)` →
      `BundleOverCap`; the ack is not an input — the cap is
      unconditional).
    - `wasm_cap_above_24_mib_hard_max_rejected()` (round-90 B3 —
      `validate_bundle_limits("wasm32", 25 MiB, anything)` →
      `WasmCapAboveHardMax`; the same cap on `"x86_64"` is accepted).

  The build-script freshness gate (default 45 days on
  `generated_at`) is separate — it caps how stale the
  MANIFEST itself is, not how far back entries reach. A
  manifest that regenerates weekly with `--max-age-days
400` yields entries covering ~13 months + a very recent
  regeneration timestamp; both gates pass.

  **Archive DTO + generated API.** The runtime consumes the
  archive through a generated `gvl_archive()` function that
  returns a `&'static [BakedGvlEntry]`:

  ```rust
  // Round-38 B2: DTO exposed by auctioneer-config to
  // auctioneer-privacy. Lives in
  // `crates/auctioneer-config/src/gvl_archive.rs`. Includes
  // `generated_at` on every entry so /status (H1) can
  // report the manifest date without a second file read.
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct BakedGvlEntry {
      pub spec: u32,
      pub vendor_list_version: u32,
      pub tcf_policy_version: u32,
      /// Round-41 B7 canonical: raw bytes, embedded via
      /// `include_bytes!`. Runtime lowers via
      /// `Gvl::load_from_json_bytes` inside
      /// `GvlStore::get`. Round-38's `include_str!` +
      /// `&'static str` shape forced a UTF-8 revalidation
      /// on every boot AND clashed with round-39 B3's
      /// generated `include_bytes!` codegen path — the
      /// round-41 B7 sweep aligns type + codegen +
      /// consumers on `&'static [u8]`.
      pub raw: &'static [u8],
      /// SHA-256 from the manifest, verified at build
      /// time.
      pub sha256: &'static str,
      /// `last_updated` field copied from the archive JSON
      /// (RFC 3339 UTC string).
      pub last_updated: &'static str,
  }

  /// The manifest's `generated_at` (round-38 H1 addition
  /// — round-37's DTO didn't expose it, so the /status
  /// health block couldn't report the manifest date).
  pub fn gvl_archive_generated_at() -> &'static str;

  pub fn gvl_archive() -> &'static [BakedGvlEntry];
  ```

  Build script codegen (added to `emit_gvl_archive` in
  `build.rs`) emits this array as a static slice of
  literals, one per manifest entry, plus a static
  `GENERATED_AT` string constant behind
  `gvl_archive_generated_at()`.

  **Per-spec validation** (retires the round-36 hard pin to
  spec 3). `gvl_schema_shared.rs::validate_gvl_json` has
  ONE canonical signature (round-38 B2 — the round-37
  draft alternated between the one-arg legacy shape and
  the two-arg shape at different bullets):

  ```rust
  pub fn validate_gvl_json(
      raw: &str,
      spec_expected: Option<u32>,
  ) -> Result<ValidatedGvl, GvlSchemaError>;
  ```

  Round-56 B4 / round-88 H4: `spec_expected` is `Option<u32>`. build.rs
  (the authoritative archive gate) passes `Some(entry.spec)`; the
  runtime lowering loaders (`Gvl::load_from_json[_bytes]`) are driven by
  `GvlStore::get`, which — although it has ALREADY selected the blob by
  manifest `(spec, list)` — STILL passes `Some(slot_spec)` so a blob
  whose `gvlSpecificationVersion` disagrees is HARD-REJECTED with
  `UnsupportedSpecVersion` at runtime, exactly as strong as the build
  gate (round-57 B-k). Only hand-authored TEST FIXTURES pass `None`,
  skipping ONLY the redundant spec cross-check while every other schema /
  hostile-input invariant still runs; spec-check unit tests pass
  `Some(2)` / `Some(3)`. There is no zero-arg legacy signature retained.

  Historic `crates/auctioneer-config/data/gvl.json` +
  `gvl_raw()` are DELETED — the runtime iterates the
  archive.

  **Env-var override** (round-38 B2 canonical — the
  round-37 draft alternated between `AUCTIONEER__GVL__PATH_OVERRIDE`
  (single-file legacy) and `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__OVERRIDE`
  (directory). ONE name survives: `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__DIR`. The env var points at a
  directory containing its own `manifest.json` (same
  schema). Gated behind the existing `test-harness-
override` feature; production builds ignore it.
  Failure-harness fixtures live under
  `crates/auctioneer-config/tests/fixtures/gvl_archive_<name>/`
  and each carries a hand-authored `manifest.json`.

  **Fail-closed / missing-version warning** (round-43 B6
  canonical shape, round-51 B1/B2 semantics). Substituting
  `Gvl::empty()` + the accumulated-warning push (above)
  is the sole path when `store.get(spec, list)`
  returns `None`. It pushes the REAL openrtb warning type
  ([normalized.rs:43](../../../crates/auctioneer-openrtb/src/normalized.rs#L43))
  — earlier rounds wrote a struct-variant literal
  (`NonFatalWarning::gvl_version_unavailable { spec, list
}`) as if it were an enum variant, which it is not:

  ```rust
  // crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/context.rs
  fn gvl_version_unavailable(spec: u32, list: u32) -> NonFatalWarning {
      NonFatalWarning {
          code: WarningCode::GvlVersionUnavailable,   // 10018
          // Round-51 foundations: the message must NOT say "permissive" —
          // the behaviour is enforced-but-empty (IDs denied), and a
          // "permissive defaults" message would mislead an operator
          // into thinking identifiers still flow.
          message: format!(
              "GVL version (spec {spec}, list {list}) is not in the \
               bundled archive; applying enforced-but-empty defaults \
               (identifiers denied)"
          ),
          scope: Some("regs.gdpr".into()),
      }
  }
  ```

  `WarningCode::GvlVersionUnavailable` is a NEW variant on
  the existing enum at
  [normalized.rs:60](../../../crates/auctioneer-openrtb/src/normalized.rs#L60);
  its `as_u32()` arm returns `10018` (slotted after
  `10017 BidderBlockedByPrivacySettings` in Appendix G).
  `run_auction` converts to the exchange's `ErrorEntry`
  when draining `take_warnings()` — see bounded fanout Task Fanout-2's
  round-43 B6 taxonomy table for the exact conversion.
