  **Testable build support** (round-43 B4 canonical —
  supersedes the round-24 C2 `include!` +
  `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` workaround. That pattern existed
  because a package's `build.rs` cannot import its OWN
  library; it can, however, import a SIBLING crate as a
  `[build-dependencies]` entry. Extracting
  `auctioneer-gvl-schema` (round-42 B9) removes the need for
  `include!` entirely AND breaks the bootstrap cycle,
  since the sibling has no build.rs of its own):

  1. **Shared crate** (already created in Step 0a⁰ — round-65 B1;
     this item is its full definition, land it there, not here).
     `crates/auctioneer-gvl-schema/`
     (see the Files list above for its `Cargo.toml`). A
     normal library crate — NO `include!`, NO `#[path]`,
     NO build.rs. It defines `pub enum GvlSchemaError`,
     `pub struct RawGvl`, `pub struct ValidatedGvl`,
     `pub fn validate_gvl_json(raw: &str, spec_expected:
Option<u32>) -> Result<ValidatedGvl, GvlSchemaError>`
     (round-38 B2 two-arg canonical signature; round-56 B4
     optional spec), and
     `pub fn validate_manifest(...)` (round-39 B4).
     Depends only on `serde`, `serde_json`,
     `serde_path_to_error`, and `time`.

     ```rust
     // crates/auctioneer-gvl-schema/src/lib.rs
     use std::collections::BTreeMap;

     #[derive(Debug)]
     pub enum GvlSchemaError {
         InvalidJson(String),
         MissingRequiredField(&'static str),
         /// Round-35 foundations: table-generic malformed-entry variant
         /// (was `InvalidVendorEntry`, which only named the
         /// vendors table). Applies to any of the five
         /// indexed tables (vendors, purposes, special_
         /// purposes, features, special_features). `path` is
         /// the dotted field path produced by
         /// `serde_path_to_error::deserialize` — precise
         /// enough that operators can grep the offending row
         /// in the source JSON.
         MalformedEntry { table: &'static str, path: String, reason: String },
         /// Round-110 B1 / round-111 B2 / round-112 user sync: a timestamp
         /// field that fails RFC 3339 parsing during validation —
         /// the vendor `deletedDate` (`path` = the dotted vendor
         /// path) AND the root `lastUpdated` (`path` ==
         /// "lastUpdated" exactly). Distinct from MalformedEntry so
         /// operators can tell a shape error from a bad instant.
         BadTimestamp { path: String, raw: String },
         UnsupportedSpecVersion { got: u32, expected: u32 },
         /// Round-32 H2 generalised (was `VendorIdMismatch`) — one
         /// variant covers vendors, purposes, special purposes,
         /// features, and special features. `table` names the
         /// GVL table (`"vendors"`, `"purposes"`, …).
         IdKeyMismatch { table: &'static str, map_key: String, embedded_id: u64 },
         /// Round-32 H2: table-scoped zero-ID check. TCF IDs are
         /// positive integers per the technical spec; parsing a
         /// `u32` accepts `0` on the serde side, so validation
         /// rejects it explicitly.
         ZeroId { table: &'static str, map_key: String },
         VendorIdOutOfRange { vendor_id: u64 },
         PurposeIdOutOfRange { purpose_id: u64 },
         SpecialFeatureIdOutOfRange { special_feature_id: u64 },
         UnknownPurposeReference {
             vendor_id: u32,
             purpose_id: u32,
             field: &'static str,
         },
         // Round-89 B1 — flex-basis invariants (IAB vendor-list contract).
         /// A purpose id appears in BOTH `purposes` and `legIntPurposes`
         /// (a purpose has exactly one default basis).
         FlexBasisOverlap { vendor_id: u32, purpose_id: u8 },
         /// A purpose id in `flexiblePurposes` has no default basis in
         /// either `purposes` or `legIntPurposes`.
         FlexPurposeWithoutDefault { vendor_id: u32, purpose_id: u8 },
         /// Purpose 1 (storage/access) is consent-only and cannot be
         /// listed in `flexiblePurposes`.
         FlexiblePurposeOneForbidden { vendor_id: u32 },
     }

     /// Deserialised, validated GVL blob shared between build.rs
     /// (validator) and runtime (`Gvl` loader). Round-27 H1: the
     /// validator returns THIS DTO so the runtime does not
     /// re-parse or diverge. Round-47 H2: the type lives in the
     /// standalone **`auctioneer-gvl-schema`** crate (round-43 B4 —
     /// NOT the obsolete `auctioneer_config::gvl_schema`
     /// `include!(...)` module pattern); build.rs and the runtime
     /// both depend on that crate, so the type identity is
     /// genuinely shared without a build-order cycle.
     ///
     /// **Round-30 GDPR enforcement correction — raw parse uses `u32` widths;
     /// domain lowering happens INSIDE `validate_gvl_json`.**
     /// Earlier round-28 draft used `u8` map keys directly on
     /// `RawGvl`, which meant serde REJECTED any out-of-range
     /// id before `validate_gvl_json` could run — producing a
     /// generic serde error instead of the precise
     /// `PurposeIdOutOfRange { purpose_id }` diagnostic the
     /// invariant list promises. The correct flow:
     /// 1. Deserialise into `RawGvl` with `u32` keys / ids.
     /// 2. `validate_gvl_json` runs domain checks, producing
     ///    typed variants for each rejection.
     /// 3. On success, lower into `ValidatedGvl` (the shape
     ///    below with `u8` maps) — infallible because domain
     ///    validation just ran.
     ///
     /// **Round-47 H2: `features` has NO wire cap.** The
     /// superseded "features gets a 1..=24 cap" block is deleted —
     /// it contradicted the canonical `ValidatedGvl` shape below,
     /// where `special_purposes` and `features` stay `u32`
     /// precisely because they are GVL-declared tables with no
     /// wire-position limit (round-31 H6). Only `purposes` (≤ 24)
     /// and `special_features` (≤ 12) are wire-capped and lowered
     /// to `u8`.
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawGvl {
         pub gvl_specification_version: u32,
         pub tcf_policy_version: u32,
         pub vendor_list_version: u32,
         pub last_updated: String,
         pub purposes: BTreeMap<u32, RawPurpose>,
         pub special_purposes: BTreeMap<u32, RawSpecialPurpose>,
         pub features: BTreeMap<u32, RawFeature>,
         pub special_features: BTreeMap<u32, RawSpecialFeature>,
         // Round-57 B-f: plain deserialize — NO
         // `deserialize_with = "deserialize_vendor_map"` (that fn was
         // never defined). The vendors table needs no special
         // deserializer: `validate_gvl_json`'s Value-walk already
         // enforces map-key == embedded `id` for EVERY table
         // (invariant 2), so `vendors` uses the same plain
         // `BTreeMap<u32, RawVendor>` shape as the other five tables.
         pub vendors: BTreeMap<u32, RawVendor>,
     }

     /// Round-31 H6: post-validation shape. Only the wire-capped
     /// tables get lowered widths (purposes ≤ 24, special
     /// features ≤ 12 → `u8`); special purposes and features
     /// stay `u32` because they have no wire cap and can hold
     /// arbitrary positive integers from the GVL.
     /// `validate_gvl_json` returns `Result<ValidatedGvl, _>`;
     /// the runtime loader consumes this DTO directly.
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
     pub struct ValidatedGvl {
         pub gvl_specification_version: u32,
         pub tcf_policy_version: u32,
         pub vendor_list_version: u32,
         // Round-111 B2: PARSED at validation (the raw DTO keeps the
         // String) — malformed → GvlSchemaError::BadTimestamp
         // { path: "lastUpdated", .. }. The 5b flex-invariant
         // exemption compares vendor deleted_date against THIS
         // instant (tombstone iff deleted_date <= last_updated).
         pub last_updated: time::OffsetDateTime,
         pub purposes: BTreeMap<u8, RawPurpose>,           // 1..=24
         pub special_purposes: BTreeMap<u32, RawSpecialPurpose>,   // no wire cap
         pub features: BTreeMap<u32, RawFeature>,          // no wire cap
         pub special_features: BTreeMap<u8, RawSpecialFeature>,    // 1..=12
         // Round-110 B1: the VALIDATED side carries ValidatedVendor —
         // identical to RawVendor except `deleted_date` is the PARSED
         // Option<OffsetDateTime> (the raw serde DTO keeps
         // Option<String>; validation performs the one parse).
         pub vendors: BTreeMap<u16, ValidatedVendor>,
     }

     /// Round-110 B1: RawVendor after validation — the only field
     /// that changes shape is `deleted_date` (parsed RFC 3339; a
     /// malformed value fails validation with
     /// `GvlSchemaError::BadTimestamp`, build-gate and runtime
     /// alike). The runtime lowering (Task 4 Step 2) consumes THIS
     /// type, so `Vendor.deleted_date: Option<OffsetDateTime>` needs
     /// no second parse.
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
     pub struct ValidatedVendor {
         pub id: u32,
         pub name: String,
         pub purposes: Vec<u32>,
         pub leg_int_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         pub flexible_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         pub special_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         pub features: Vec<u32>,
         pub special_features: Vec<u32>,
         pub deleted_date: Option<time::OffsetDateTime>,
     }

     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawPurpose { pub id: u32, pub name: String }
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawSpecialPurpose { pub id: u32, pub name: String }
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawFeature { pub id: u32, pub name: String }
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawSpecialFeature { pub id: u32, pub name: String }
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Deserialize)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
     pub struct RawVendor {
         pub id: u32,
         pub name: String,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub purposes: Vec<u32>,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub leg_int_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub flexible_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub special_purposes: Vec<u32>,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub features: Vec<u32>,
         #[serde(default)]
         pub special_features: Vec<u32>,
         /// Present when the vendor was removed from the current
         /// GVL revision. Round-28 C1: previously omitted from the
         /// DTO, blocking the Task 4 `deleted_vendor_still_looks_
         /// up_but_has_deleted_date` regression from compiling.
         /// Round-90 B1 correction (supersedes round-28's "audit
         /// metadata only, still authorizes" answer), timestamp
         /// semantics per round-108 stored requests and accounts / round-110 B1: a deleted
         /// vendor is STILL looked up by id (the GVL map retains the
         /// record) BUT is EXCLUDED from authorization once the
         /// deletion instant has PASSED — validation parses this raw
         /// string onto `ValidatedVendor.deleted_date:
         /// Option<OffsetDateTime>` (malformed → `BadTimestamp`),
         /// and Task 9 Step 1 short-circuits `permissions()` to
         /// deny every gate when
         /// `is_deleted_at(authorization_now)` holds. The
         /// validator also TOLERATES legacy flex inconsistencies on
         /// TOMBSTONE rows only — round-111 B2: tombstone iff
         /// `deleted_date <= list.last_updated`; a FUTURE-dated
         /// vendor gets the full 5b flex invariants because it is
         /// still authorizable (invariant 5b). The
         /// Round-108 stored requests and accounts: this RAW serde field stays a `String`, but
         /// validation PARSES it (RFC 3339, shared helper — malformed
         /// fails the validator, build-gate and runtime alike) and
         /// the Validated/runtime `Vendor` carries
         /// `Option<OffsetDateTime>`; enforcement compares
         /// `is_deleted_at(now)` (deletion applies AFTER the
         /// instant), no longer field presence. Observability is a BUILD-TIME aggregate (`build.rs`
         /// emits one `cargo:warning` per archive entry with the deleted
         /// count), NOT a per-vendor runtime `log::warn!`: the deleted
         /// set is fixed at build time (the archive is `include_bytes!`),
         /// and a per-vendor runtime warn amplified hundreds of lines per
         /// cache rotation (round-90 H4). No per-request warning path
         /// exists — `resolve` has no auction Clock and `permissions`
         /// takes `&self`.
         #[serde(default)]
         pub deleted_date: Option<String>,
     }

     /// Round-37 B3 / round-56 B4: `spec_expected` is
     /// `Option<u32>` so the ONE validator serves both load
     /// modes without any caller having to fabricate a spec:
     /// - **`Some(n)` — spec-checked gate (round-57 B-k: BOTH build
     ///   AND runtime).** build.rs passes the manifest-declared spec
     ///   per archive entry (spec 2 for `spec2/`, spec 3 for
     ///   `spec3/`), AND `GvlStore::get` passes `Some(slot_spec)`
     ///   into the runtime loaders so a blob whose
     ///   `gvlSpecificationVersion != n` is rejected with
     ///   `UnsupportedSpecVersion` at BOTH layers — runtime
     ///   validation is as strong as the build gate, not a debug
     ///   assertion. Also the v2.4 refresh test.
     /// - **`None` — self-describing load, TEST FIXTURES ONLY.** A
     ///   hand-authored fixture that legitimately does not know /
     ///   care about a slot spec (e.g. the `load_from_json(&str)`
     ///   test path) passes `None` to skip ONLY the spec
     ///   cross-check; every other invariant (schema, id/key
     ///   equality, hostile-input caps) still runs. `None` is NOT
     ///   used on the runtime `get` path.
     pub fn validate_gvl_json(
         raw: &str,
         spec_expected: Option<u32>,
     ) -> Result<ValidatedGvl, GvlSchemaError> {
         // Round-33 H3 two-stage parse. A direct
         // `serde_json::from_str::<RawGvl>(raw)` returns a
         // single opaque serde error and cannot distinguish
         // "top-level field missing" from "one vendor entry is
         // malformed" — the derived `Deserialize` on `RawGvl`
         // gives up on the first error with no field-path
         // context. So the validator uses a two-stage parse:
         //
         // 1. Parse into `serde_json::Value` first. This
         //    always succeeds if the input is valid JSON;
         //    invalid JSON → `InvalidJson`.
         // 2. Walk the `Value` at top level to check each
         //    required field is present. Missing top-level
         //    field → `MissingRequiredField(&'static str)`
         //    with the exact field name (`"vendors"`,
         //    `"purposes"`, `"tcfPolicyVersion"`, …).
         // 3. For each indexed table, iterate `Value` entries
         //    and validate key/id equality + `>= 1` BEFORE
         //    handing the sub-value to the derived
         //    `RawGvl` deserializer. This is where
         //    `IdKeyMismatch` and `ZeroId` variants fire.
         // 4. Finally, per-table typed deserialise using
         //    `serde_path_to_error::deserialize::<RawGvl>` on
         //    the whole `Value` — the wrapper retains the
         //    dotted field path so residual serde errors
         //    become `MalformedEntry { table, path, reason }`
         //    with the offending element identifiable.
         //    (Round-35 foundations: `serde_json::Error` alone does NOT
         //    retain the nested path; without
         //    `serde_path_to_error` the path field would be
         //    forever empty.)
         //
         // Round-31 H5: single canonical signature. Parses into
         // `RawGvl` internally, then lowers into `ValidatedGvl`
         // (u8 / u16 keys where the wire caps allow, u32
         // otherwise per round-31 H6 + round-32 H2). Callers
         // consume only the lowered shape.
         //
         // Round-28 C1 tightens the invariants to match TCF v2.3.
         //
         // Invariants:
         // 1. Round-37 B3 / round-56 B4: IF `spec_expected` is
         //    `Some(n)`, gvlSpecificationVersion == n (per-entry
         //    manifest pin) — rejects a blob whose declared spec
         //    doesn't match the manifest slot it was fetched
         //    into. Both spec 2 (`spec2/` archive files) and
         //    spec 3 (`spec3/`) are accepted; the check is
         //    per-file, not workspace-wide. IF `None`, this
         //    single invariant is SKIPPED (self-describing
         //    load); every invariant below still runs.
         // 2. **Every** table (vendors, purposes, special_purposes,
         //    features, special_features) has its map key
         //    equal to the embedded `id` field. Mismatch =>
         //    `IdKeyMismatch { table, .. }`. Round-32 H2:
         //    round-31 only checked the vendors table; the
         //    other four went unchecked, so a GVL blob with
         //    map key `"5"` embedding `id = 7` would parse
         //    silently.
         // 3. Every vendor id is in [1, 65_535].
         // 3b. Round-32 H2: every id in every table is `>= 1` →
         //     `ZeroId { table, map_key }`. Serde `u32` accepts
         //     `0`; this check enforces the TCF-technical-spec
         //     positive-integer requirement.
         // 4. **All four ID spaces are SEPARATE tables** per
         //    IAB TCF v2.3. Round-31 H6: earlier drafts caps
         //    were partly correct (purposes 1..=24 matches the
         //    24-position wire bitfield; special features
         //    1..=12 matches the 12-position wire bitfield),
         //    but Features and Special Purposes have NO wire-
         //    format-imposed cap — they are GVL-declared vendor
         //    properties. Concretely:
         //     - `raw.purposes` keys in **1..=24** (the wire
         //       `PurposeConsent` / `PurposeLI` bitfields are
         //       exactly 24 bits each).
         //     - `raw.special_features` keys in **1..=12** (the
         //       wire `SpecialFeatureOptIns` bitfield is
         //       exactly 12 bits).
         //     - `raw.special_purposes` keys form a **SEPARATE
         //       id space**, positive integers with no wire
         //       cap (the segment doesn't reference them by
         //       position — the GVL cross-reference does).
         //       Validation is cross-reference-only.
         //     - `raw.features` keys form a **SEPARATE id
         //       space**, positive integers with no wire cap.
         //       Validation is cross-reference-only.
         //     - Keys outside the wire-capped ranges → typed
         //       rejection (`PurposeIdOutOfRange`,
         //       `SpecialFeatureIdOutOfRange`). Features /
         //       special purposes have no per-key cap; only
         //       the "must be positive u32" bound is enforced
         //       at parse time, and cross-references are
         //       enforced at validation time.
         // 5. Every vendor's `purposes`, `legIntPurposes`,
         //    `flexiblePurposes` reference must exist as a key in
         //    `raw.purposes`; `specialPurposes` reference must
         //    exist in `raw.specialPurposes`; `features` in
         //    `raw.features`; `specialFeatures` in
         //    `raw.specialFeatures`. Otherwise
         //    `UnknownPurposeReference { field: "purposes" |
         //    "specialPurposes" | "features" | "specialFeatures" }`.
         // 5b. **Flex-basis invariants per the IAB vendor-list
         //    contract (round-89 B1 — REQUIRED so the "default basis"
         //    the enforcement matrix relies on is well-defined; without
         //    these, a flex purpose with no default or a dual default
         //    would let GDPR enforcement grant under the WRONG basis).**
         //    **Round-90 B1 — ACTIVE vendors ONLY; round-111 B2 —
         //    "active" is TIMESTAMP-defined, not presence-defined.**
         //    The round-108/110 authorization rule treats a vendor
         //    with `deletedDate` in the FUTURE as still active — so a
         //    presence-based 5b skip would let an active vendor carry
         //    overlapping or missing flex defaults and still be
         //    authorized under a basis 5b exists to make well-defined.
         //    The validator therefore uses the LIST'S OWN instant as
         //    its reference (deterministic, content-derived — the
         //    validator has no request clock): a vendor is a
         //    TOMBSTONE for 5b purposes iff
         //    `deleted_date <= list.last_updated` (the parsed root
         //    `lastUpdated`, round-111 B2). Only tombstones are
         //    SKIPPED: the official IAB TCF v2 GVL ships DELETED
         //    records with legacy flex inconsistencies the current
         //    schema forbids — e.g. vendor 688 declares
         //    `flexiblePurposes: [7]` with 7 in NEITHER `purposes`
         //    NOR `legIntPurposes` (no default basis) — so applying
         //    5b to tombstones would make the real v224 vendor list
         //    fail validation and the whole archive unloadable.
         //    Tombstones are EXCLUDED from authorization anyway
         //    (their instant has passed for every request `now >=
         //    lastUpdated`, which build-gated archives satisfy by
         //    construction), so tolerating their legacy flex changes
         //    no grant decision. A FUTURE-dated vendor
         //    (`deleted_date > list.last_updated`) gets the FULL 5b
         //    block — it can still be authorized, so its flex
         //    defaults must be well-defined. For every such ACTIVE
         //    vendor (`deletedDate` absent OR future-dated):
         //    - **No overlap:** a purpose id in BOTH `purposes` AND
         //      `legIntPurposes` → `FlexBasisOverlap { vendor_id,
         //      purpose_id }`. A purpose has exactly ONE default basis.
         //    - **Flex requires a default:** every id in
         //      `flexiblePurposes` MUST also appear in `purposes` OR
         //      `legIntPurposes` (its default); a flex id in NEITHER →
         //      `FlexPurposeWithoutDefault { vendor_id, purpose_id }`.
         //    - **Purpose 1 cannot be flexible:** Purpose 1 (storage /
         //      access) is consent-only; `1 ∈ flexiblePurposes` →
         //      `FlexiblePurposeOneForbidden { vendor_id }`.
         //    These run at BUILD-time validation (`Some(spec)`) AND the
         //    runtime lowering path, so a malformed bundled GVL fails the
         //    build and a malformed runtime blob fails closed.
         // 6. **Auction enforcement still iterates purpose IDs
         //    `2..=10` intentionally.** Enforcement policy stays
         //    on the enforcement side; the validator accepts the
         //    full 1..=24 GVL namespace.
         // 7. tcfPolicyVersion, vendorListVersion, purposes,
         //    specialPurposes, features, specialFeatures, vendors
         //    all present.
     }
     ```

     **Runtime / validator schema equivalence.** Round-43
     B4: `auctioneer-gvl-schema` returns a `ValidatedGvl` DTO
     that BOTH `build.rs` (validation-only, discards
     value) and the runtime loader consume. Because the
     DTO is one type defined in one CRATE that both sides
     link against, the "same shape" invariant is a
     type-identity guarantee, not a hope — and unlike the
     round-26 `include!` pattern, the two sides genuinely
     share one compiled type rather than two structurally
     identical copies. Task 4 Step 5's
     `#[test] fn runtime_and_build_schema_agree_on_valid_gvl()`
     iterates `auctioneer_config::gvl_archive()` (round-37 B3 —
     the earlier `gvl_raw()` single-blob API is gone) and, per
     entry, validates ONCE the authoritative way —
     `validate_gvl_json(entry.raw, Some(entry.spec))` → the DTO —
     then lowers the SAME bytes through the runtime loader
     `Gvl::load_from_json(entry.raw, Some(entry.spec))` (round-57
     B-k — the runtime path passes the slot spec, mirroring
     `GvlStore::get`) and asserts the runtime `Gvl` matches the DTO
     (see the round-48 auction core body below for the exact field/content
     comparison). This proves the build gate and the runtime load —
     both `Some(spec)` — agree on every valid entry, the DEEPER
     equivalence,
     not the tautological "call the validator twice" the pre-
     round-48 draft had. A future refactor that tried to sneak a
     second parser in on the runtime side would have to break the
     shared-module structure to do so.

  2. **`build.rs` includes the shared module directly.**
     Round-39 B4 canonical shape (retires round-38 B2's
     draft which had `ManifestEntry` derive only
     `Deserialize` but then formatted `{e:?}` — needing
     `Debug`; failed to verify parsed `vendor_list_version`
     against the manifest entry's declared value; didn't
     parse `last_updated` for per-entry age enforcement;
     accepted future `generated_at` dates; and pointed at
     `scripts/auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive.sh` which was renamed to
     the `crates/auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive/` crate. ONE strict
     validator is shared by build.rs + refresh tool via
     the shared module).

     ```rust
     // crates/auctioneer-config/build.rs
     // Round-43 B4: a normal `use` against the sibling
     // crate declared in [build-dependencies]. The
     // round-38 `mod gvl_schema { include!(...) }`
     // workaround is GONE.
     use auctioneer_gvl_schema::{validate_gvl_json, validate_manifest, Manifest};
     use sha2::{Digest as _, Sha256};
     use fs2::FileExt; // round-87 H5: SHARED archive-read lock (§ Concurrency safety)

     // Round-47 auction core: returns `BuildResult` and uses `?` — matches
     // the existing build.rs (no bare `.expect()` / `panic!`);
     // `main` calls `emit_gvl_archive()?`.
     fn emit_gvl_archive() -> BuildResult {
         let manifest_dir = std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?;
         let default_dir = format!("{manifest_dir}/data/gvl_archive");
         let archive_dir = if std::env::var("CARGO_FEATURE_TEST_HARNESS_OVERRIDE").is_ok() {
             std::env::var("AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__DIR").unwrap_or(default_dir)
         } else {
             default_dir
         };
         let manifest_path = format!("{archive_dir}/manifest.json");

         // Round-87 H5 (round-61 B4 / round-63 H2): NO unlocked read
         // window. Every archive read below runs under the PERSISTENT
         // `fs2` advisory lock on the checked-in `data/gvl_archive.lock`
         // sentinel. Common case (`live` present): hold the SHARED lock
         // across all reads; `lock_file` stays in scope until this fn
         // returns, so its `Drop` releases the lock only after the last
         // read.
         let lock_path = format!("{manifest_dir}/data/gvl_archive.lock");
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={lock_path}");
         let lock_file = std::fs::File::open(&lock_path)
             .map_err(|e| format!("open archive lock {lock_path}: {e}"))?;
         lock_file.lock_shared()
             .map_err(|e| format!("lock_shared {lock_path}: {e}"))?;

         // Round-88 H3 (round-62 B2 / round-63 H2): recovery case — the
         // `live` manifest is ABSENT (a refresh swap caught mid-flight, or
         // a prior run crashed between its two swap renames, leaving the
         // archive only at `data/gvl_archive.old`). `fs2` has NO portable
         // shared→exclusive upgrade, so DROP the shared lock and
         // RE-ACQUIRE the lock EXCLUSIVE, heal, and READ while STILL
         // holding the exclusive (no unlocked window). The common case
         // leaves the shared lock untouched.
         let lock_file = if std::path::Path::new(&manifest_path).exists() {
             lock_file
         } else {
             drop(lock_file);
             let lock_file = std::fs::File::open(&lock_path)
                 .map_err(|e| format!("open archive lock {lock_path}: {e}"))?;
             lock_file.lock_exclusive()
                 .map_err(|e| format!("lock_exclusive {lock_path}: {e}"))?;
             // Re-check state under the EXCLUSIVE lock and run the
             // four-case `.old → live` recovery only if still necessary
             // (round-62 B3 fixed-`gvl_archive.old` rule); shared with the
             // refresh tool's step-11 pre-swap recovery.
             auctioneer_gvl_schema::recover_gvl_archive(std::path::Path::new(&archive_dir))
                 .map_err(|e| format!("recover_gvl_archive {archive_dir}: {e}"))?;
             lock_file
         };

         // The read ALWAYS runs under the HELD lock (shared in the common
         // case, exclusive after recovery); `lock_file` lives until this
         // fn returns, so `Drop` releases it only after the last read.
         let raw_manifest = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path)
             .map_err(|e| format!("read {manifest_path}: {e}"))?;

         // ONE strict validator shared by build.rs and the
         // refresh tool (round-39 B4). Returns a parsed
         // Manifest (all fields checked: manifest_version=1,
         // RFC 3339 timestamps, no future generated_at,
         // dedupe, path-safety, spec ∈ {2,3},
         // vendor_list_version >= 1) OR an explicit typed
         // error the caller propagates with `?`. `validate_manifest`
         // lives in the `auctioneer-gvl-schema` crate so both call
         // sites use bit-for-bit the same rules.
         let now = time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc();
         let manifest = validate_manifest(&raw_manifest, now)
             .map_err(|e| format!("manifest validation: {e}"))?;
         // `validate_manifest` already enforced `MissingGcl` +
         // `GclStale` (`now >= gcl.expires_at()`, round-100 B2 — the
         // GCL's OWN RFC 9111 lifetime, never the 45-day GVL window
         // below and never overrideable).

         // Round-100 B1: validate + EMIT the GCL alongside the GVL
         // entries. Same sha256 re-check pattern as the entries; then
         // codegen the baked accessors the runtime consumes:
         //   pub fn baked_gcl_json() -> &'static str      // include_str! of gcl.json
         //   pub fn gcl_expires_at_unix_secs() -> i64     // round-105 B3: the ONE
         //       // accessor form — unix seconds; the runtime converts
         let gcl_path = format!("{archive_dir}/{}", manifest.gcl.path);
         let gcl_raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&gcl_path)
             .map_err(|e| format!("read {gcl_path}: {e}"))?;
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={gcl_path}"); // round-105 B3
         verify_sha256(&gcl_raw, &manifest.gcl.sha256)
             .map_err(|e| format!("gcl sha mismatch: {e}"))?;
         // Round-105 B3: BIND the validated blob and EXECUTE the
         // manifest/blob cross-check (previously discarded/comment):
         let validated_gcl = auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_gcl_json(&gcl_raw)
             .map_err(|e| format!("gcl validation: {e}"))?;
         auctioneer_gvl_schema::check_gcl_consistency(&manifest, &validated_gcl)
             .map_err(|e| format!("gcl consistency: {e}"))?;
         // Round-103 B1: the GCL bytes are read + sha-checked +
         // schema-validated HERE (with the manifest), but the bundle
         // accounting and accessor EMISSION live in the executable
         // block AFTER the ENTRIES array below — where `bundle_bytes`
         // and the `codegen` String actually exist. See "GCL emission
         // (round-103 B1)" below.

         // Round-39 H1: freshness SLA on the manifest's
         // generated_at. Default 45 days — deployers can
         // override via env var. Kept separate from
         // validate_manifest because the cap is a build
         // policy, not a manifest-schema invariant.
         let max_days: u64 = std::env::var("AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__MAX_AGE_DAYS")
             .ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(45);
         let age_days = (now - manifest.generated_at).whole_days();
         // Round-47 auction core: `i64::try_from` (lint-clean) + `return Err`,
         // not `as i64` + `assert!`.
         let max_days_i64 = i64::try_from(max_days).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
         if age_days > max_days_i64 {
             return Err(format!(
                 "GVL archive is {age_days} days old (cap: {max_days}). \
                  Re-run: cargo run -p auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive"
             ).into());
         }

         // Round-40 B7 sweep: every env var read by the
         // build script gets a matching rerun-if-env-
         // changed. Missing lines silently cache stale
         // build output across env changes.
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__MAX_AGE_DAYS");
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__DIR");
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB");
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_MIB");
         println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={manifest_path}");

         // Round-40 B5: raw bundle-size gate.
         // Round-44 H1: per-target default. The wasm
         // adapters share a 128 MB isolate with code +
         // parse cache + fanout streams, so their GVL
         // budget is 24 MB — the figure bounded fanout's admission
         // proof reserves. Axum detects its ceiling at
         // boot and can afford 60 MB.
         let default_raw_mib: u64 =
             if std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").as_deref() == Ok("wasm32") {
                 24
             } else {
                 60
             };
         let bundle_max_raw: u64 = std::env::var("AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB")
             .ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(default_raw_mib) * 1024 * 1024;
         let mut bundle_bytes: u64 = 0;

         let mut codegen = String::new();
         codegen.push_str(
             "pub fn gvl_archive() -> &'static [BakedGvlEntry] { &ENTRIES }\n\
              pub fn gvl_archive_generated_at() -> &'static str { GENERATED_AT }\n\
              pub fn gvl_archive_max_age_days() -> u32 { MAX_AGE_DAYS }\n"
         );
         // Round-46 B2: the parsed cache is count-bounded
         // (`GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`), so there is no
         // byte-ceiling const or env override to codegen.
         // Round-47 auction core: the whole build script is subject to the
         // workspace restriction lints (the existing
         // `auctioneer-config/build.rs` clears them — `fn main() ->
         // BuildResult`, `?` throughout, NO bare `as` /
         // `.unwrap()` / `.expect()`). These snippets follow the
         // same contract: `u32::try_from(..)?` not `as`,
         // `?`/`.ok_or(..)?` not `.expect(..)`.
         codegen.push_str(&format!(
             "static GENERATED_AT: &str = \"{}\";\n\
              static MAX_AGE_DAYS: u32 = {};\n",
             manifest.generated_at_rfc3339,
             u32::try_from(max_days)?,
         ));
         codegen.push_str("static ENTRIES: &[BakedGvlEntry] = &[\n");
         for entry in &manifest.entries {
             let raw_path = format!("{archive_dir}/{}", entry.path);
             println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={raw_path}");
             let raw = std::fs::read(&raw_path)?;
             bundle_bytes = bundle_bytes
                 .checked_add(u64::try_from(raw.len())?)
                 .ok_or("bundle byte total overflowed u64")?;
             // SHA-256 pin. `sha2::Sha256::digest` returns a
             // GenericArray<u8, 32>; hex-encode via workspace
             // `hex` crate.
             // Round-47 auction core: SHA / cross-check failures `return
             // Err(..)` (the build.rs convention), never
             // `assert_eq!` / `panic!` under the denied
             // restriction lints.
             let observed = hex::encode(Sha256::digest(&raw));
             if observed != entry.sha256 {
                 return Err(format!(
                     "SHA mismatch for {}: manifest={}, on-disk={observed}",
                     entry.path, entry.sha256
                 ).into());
             }
             // The runtime uses lazy-parse — but build.rs
             // still validates every entry up-front so that a
             // malformed bundled blob fails the build, not
             // the first request that touches it.
             let raw_str = std::str::from_utf8(&raw)
                 .map_err(|e| format!("{} not UTF-8: {e}", entry.path))?;
             let validated = validate_gvl_json(raw_str, Some(entry.spec))
                 .map_err(|e| format!("{} failed schema: {e:?}", entry.path))?;
             // Round-39 B4: cross-check the parsed
             // vendor_list_version + tcf_policy_version
             // against the manifest entry. Round-38 verified
             // only tcf_policy_version.
             if validated.vendor_list_version != entry.vendor_list_version {
                 return Err(format!(
                     "manifest vendor_list_version {} disagrees with parsed {} in {}",
                     entry.vendor_list_version, validated.vendor_list_version, entry.path
                 ).into());
             }
             if validated.tcf_policy_version != entry.tcf_policy_version {
                 return Err(format!(
                     "manifest tcf_policy_version {} disagrees with parsed {} in {}",
                     entry.tcf_policy_version, validated.tcf_policy_version, entry.path
                 ).into());
             }
             // Round-90 H4: deleted-vendor observability as a BUILD-TIME
             // aggregate (one line per entry), replacing the removed
             // per-vendor runtime `log::warn!`. The deleted set is static
             // at build (the archive is `include_bytes!`), so this is the
             // non-amplifying place; the runtime lazy-parse path stays
             // silent. Deleted vendors are also EXCLUDED from
             // authorization at runtime (Task 9 Step 1 / `Vendor::is_deleted_at`).
             let deleted_count = validated
                 .vendors
                 .values()
                 .filter(|v| v.deleted_date.is_some())
                 .count();
             if deleted_count > 0 {
                 println!(
                     "cargo:warning=GVL (spec {}, list {}): {deleted_count} vendors marked deleted",
                     entry.spec, entry.vendor_list_version
                 );
             }
             // Round-39 B3: emit `include_bytes!` (was
             // `include_str!`). Runtime GvlStore holds
             // `&'static [u8]` raw slices; deferred UTF-8
             // check happens once on first parse via
             // `Gvl::load_from_json_bytes`.
             codegen.push_str(&format!(
                 "    BakedGvlEntry {{ spec: {}, vendor_list_version: {}, \
                  tcf_policy_version: {}, raw: include_bytes!(\"{raw_path}\"), \
                  sha256: \"{}\", last_updated: \"{}\" }},\n",
                 entry.spec, entry.vendor_list_version,
                 entry.tcf_policy_version, entry.sha256, entry.last_updated_rfc3339,
             ));
         }
         codegen.push_str("];\n");

         // ── GCL emission (round-103 B1 — EXECUTABLE, after the
         // entry loop so `bundle_bytes` + `codegen` are in scope;
         // `gcl_raw` was read + verified alongside the manifest) ──
         bundle_bytes = bundle_bytes
             .checked_add(
                 u64::try_from(gcl_raw.len())
                     .map_err(|_| "gcl size exceeds u64".to_string())?,
             )
             .ok_or("bundle size overflow")?;
         let gcl_expires_unix: i64 = manifest.gcl.expires_at()
             .map_err(|e| format!("gcl expiry: {e}"))?
             .unix_timestamp();
         // Round-104 B5 / round-105 B2: emit via plain line pushes —
         // no multi-line format-string escapes (the earlier
         // backslash-space continuation was not valid Rust). The
         // include_str! path is the RESOLVED gcl_path (honors
         // AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__DIR).
         codegen.push_str(&format!(
             "pub fn baked_gcl_json() -> &'static str {{ include_str!({gcl_path:?}) }}\n"
         ));
         codegen.push_str(
             "/// Unix seconds; the runtime Gcl boot init performs the\n"
         );
         codegen.push_str(
             "/// fallible OffsetDateTime conversion (round-102 B2).\n"
         );
         codegen.push_str(&format!(
             "pub fn gcl_expires_at_unix_secs() -> i64 {{ {gcl_expires_unix} }}\n"
         ));
         // (The compressed-bundle pass below includes gcl.json via
         // `blob_paths` — round-104 B5, executable.)

         // Round-90 B3: the raw bundle-size gate is ALWAYS
         // enforced. `oversize_bundle_ack` NO LONGER skips it —
         // the ack relaxes only the refresh tool's AGE filter
         // (--max-age-days > 180); the configured
         // `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_RAW_MIB` still
         // bounds the baked bytes on every build. (Skipping it
         // used to make the env value meaningless the moment an
         // operator acknowledged — even though the error message
         // below tells them to RAISE that same value.)
         // Round-90 B3: HARD PLATFORM MAXIMUM. On wasm targets
         // the GVL shares a 128 MB isolate (bounded fanout whole-isolate
         // proof reserves ≤ 24 MB raw GVL), so a raised env value
         // must NOT breach 24 MiB for a wasm build.
         // Round-87 H5: BuildResult-only contract — `return Err(..)`, not
         // `assert!`. Round-91 H3: the cap DECISION is the pure, shared
         // `auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_bundle_limits(target_arch,
         // configured_cap, bundle_bytes)` — build.rs cannot host unit
         // tests, so the logic lives in the schema crate where
         // `schema.rs` tests exercise every branch; build.rs only
         // gathers the inputs and surfaces the error string.
         auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_bundle_limits(
             std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").as_deref().unwrap_or(""),
             bundle_max_raw,
             bundle_bytes,
         )
         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

         // Round-40 B5: compressed bundle gate.
         // Compress every archive entry with brotli-11 and
         // sum. If the total exceeds the compressed cap,
         // the deployment won't fit in CF Workers' 10 MB
         // upload ceiling. Uses `brotli = "=8.0.4"` from
         // the workspace deps (added in bounded fanout H2).
         let bundle_max_compressed: u64 = std::env::var(
                 "AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_MIB")
             .ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(9) * 1024 * 1024;
         let mut compressed_bytes: u64 = 0;
         // Round-104 B5: the GCL blob is part of the compressed
         // bundle too — iterate entries PLUS gcl.json (executable,
         // not a comment):
         let mut blob_paths: Vec<String> = manifest.entries.iter()
             .map(|entry| format!("{archive_dir}/{}", entry.path))
             .collect();
         blob_paths.push(format!("{archive_dir}/{}", manifest.gcl.path));
         for raw_path in &blob_paths {
             let raw = std::fs::read(raw_path)?;
             let mut compressed = Vec::new();
             brotli::CompressorReader::new(&raw[..], 4096, 11, 22)
                 .read_to_end(&mut compressed)?;
             compressed_bytes = compressed_bytes
                 .checked_add(u64::try_from(compressed.len())?)
                 .ok_or("compressed byte total overflowed u64")?;
         }
         if compressed_bytes > bundle_max_compressed {
             return Err(format!(
                 "GVL bundle compressed size exceeds \
                  AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_MIB: \
                  {compressed_bytes} > {bundle_max_compressed} bytes"
             ).into());
         }

         let out_dir = std::env::var("OUT_DIR")?;
         std::fs::write(format!("{out_dir}/gvl_archive.rs"), codegen)?;
         Ok(())
     }
     ```

     (Round-47 auction core: the existing `auctioneer-config/build.rs` uses ZERO
     `assert!`/`assert_eq!`/`panic!` — its convention is to surface
     every build failure through the `?`/`Result` channel. These
     snippets follow suit: the size and SHA checks `return Err(..)`
     rather than assert, so they match the crate's established
     lint-clean shape.)

     **Shared `validate_manifest` in `auctioneer-gvl-schema`
     (round-43 B4 relocation; round-43 B5 type fixes —
     round-42's shape didn't compile: `Manifest` and the
     internal `Raw` both omitted `oversize_bundle_ack`
     while the return path read and initialised it, and
     `ManifestEntry` was `.clone()`d for the ordering
     check without deriving `Clone`)**:

     ```rust
     use time::OffsetDateTime;

     // Round-43 B5: `Manifest` is the VALIDATED output —
     // built by hand inside validate_manifest, never
     // deserialised directly. It therefore does NOT derive
     // Deserialize (the `#[serde(skip)]` + default-
     // OffsetDateTime dance round-42 used doesn't even
     // compile: OffsetDateTime has no Default). The
     // internal `Raw*` structs below own the serde derives.
     #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
     pub struct Manifest {
         pub manifest_version: u32,
         pub generated_at_rfc3339: String,
         pub generated_at: OffsetDateTime,
         pub retention: Retention,
         /// Round-43 B5: present on BOTH `Raw` and
         /// `Manifest`. Round-42's return path read
         /// `raw.oversize_bundle_ack` and initialised
         /// `Manifest.oversize_bundle_ack` while neither
         /// struct declared the field.
         pub oversize_bundle_ack: bool,
         /// Round-100 B1: the REQUIRED Global CMP List record —
         /// `validate_manifest` returns `ManifestError::MissingGcl`
         /// when absent, verifies `sha256` against the blob, and
         /// enforces freshness: `now >= expires_at` →
         /// `ManifestError::GclStale { expires_at }` (round-100 B2 —
         /// the `>=` comparator is used at BOTH build and runtime).
         pub gcl: GclRecord,
         pub entries: Vec<ManifestEntry>,
     }
     #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
     pub struct GclRecord {
         pub path: String,          // constrained to ^gcl\.json$
         pub sha256: String,
         pub last_updated: OffsetDateTime,  // upstream lastUpdated
         pub fetched_at: OffsetDateTime,    // tool fetch instant
         /// RFC 9111-derived lifetime the refresh tool recorded
         /// (Age/Date-corrected; round-100 B2 — no floor applied).
         pub cache_max_age_secs: u64,
     }
     // `GclRecord::expires_at() = fetched_at + cache_max_age_secs`.
     #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize)]
     pub struct Retention { pub max_age_days: u32 }

     /// Round-43 B5: derives `Clone` — the ordering check
     /// in validate_manifest clones the entry vec.
     #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
     pub struct ManifestEntry {
         pub spec: u32,
         pub vendor_list_version: u32,
         pub tcf_policy_version: u32,
         pub last_updated_rfc3339: String,
         pub last_updated: OffsetDateTime,
         pub path: String,
         pub sha256: String,
         /// Round-105 B5 (round-104 B3): recorded on the CURRENT-list
         /// entry so refresh runs can reuse it within its advertised
         /// max-age; `None` on archived entries.
         pub fetched_at: Option<OffsetDateTime>,
         pub cache_max_age_secs: Option<u64>,
     }

     // Round-57 B-f: enum now declares EVERY variant the body
     // constructs. The round-4x draft omitted FutureTimestamp,
     // PathVersionMismatch, RetentionExceeded, WrongEntryOrder,
     // MissingSpecCoverage, and declared `Sha256Length` while the
     // body constructs `Sha256Format` — both E0599/E0026.
     #[derive(Debug)]
     pub enum ManifestError {
         Json(String),
         UnsupportedVersion { got: u32 },
         BadTimestamp { field: &'static str, raw: String },
         FutureGeneratedAt { generated_at: String, now: String },
         FutureTimestamp { field: &'static str, raw: String },
         DuplicatePair { spec: u32, list: u32 },
         OutOfRangeSpec { spec: u32 },
         ZeroListVersion,
         BadPath { path: String, reason: &'static str },
         PathVersionMismatch { path: String, declared: u32 },
         Sha256Format { path: String, got: String },
         RetentionExceeded { path: String, age_days: i64, retention_days: u32 },
         WrongEntryOrder,
         MissingSpecCoverage { has_spec_2: bool, has_spec_3: bool },
         // Round-101 B1: the GCL contract variants (round-100 B1).
         MissingGcl,
         GclStale { expires_at: String, now: String },
         // Round-105 B2: declared in the CANONICAL enum (previously
         // only promised in the amendment prose).
         GclExpiryOverflow,
         GclLastUpdatedMismatch { manifest: String, blob: String },
         // Round-106 B3: per-ENTRY cache-metadata overflow gets its
         // own variant — it is a GVL-entry defect, not a GCL one.
         EntryExpiryOverflow { path: String },
     }

     // Round-105 B2: the shared helpers, DEFINED (one definition each;
     // used by validate_manifest above and check_gcl_consistency):
     fn parse_rfc3339(field: &'static str, raw: &str)
         -> Result<OffsetDateTime, ManifestError> {
         // Round-106 B3: module-scope helper — imports Rfc3339 itself
         // (the earlier draft leaned on validate_manifest's
         // function-local `use`, which is out of scope here).
         use time::format_description::well_known::Rfc3339;
         OffsetDateTime::parse(raw, &Rfc3339)
             .map_err(|_| ManifestError::BadTimestamp { field, raw: raw.to_owned() })
     }
     fn check_sha256_format(s: String) -> Result<String, ManifestError> {
         let ok = s.len() == 64
             && s.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !b.is_ascii_uppercase());
         if ok { Ok(s) } else {
             Err(ManifestError::Sha256Format { path: String::new(), got: s })
         }
     }
     impl GclRecord {
         /// CHECKED addition; overflow → GclExpiryOverflow.
         pub fn expires_at(&self) -> Result<OffsetDateTime, ManifestError> {
             i64::try_from(self.cache_max_age_secs).ok()
                 .and_then(|secs| self.fetched_at
                     .checked_add(time::Duration::seconds(secs)))
                 .ok_or(ManifestError::GclExpiryOverflow)
         }
     }
     /// Round-105 B3: the manifest/blob cross-check — EXECUTABLE, not
     /// a comment. Called by build.rs AND refresh step 10 after both
     /// `validate_manifest` + `validate_gcl_json` succeed.
     pub fn check_gcl_consistency(
         manifest: &Manifest,
         gcl: &ValidatedGcl,
     ) -> Result<(), ManifestError> {
         if manifest.gcl.last_updated == gcl.last_updated { Ok(()) } else {
             Err(ManifestError::GclLastUpdatedMismatch {
                 manifest: manifest.gcl.last_updated.to_string(),
                 blob: gcl.last_updated.to_string(),
             })
         }
     }

     pub fn validate_manifest(
         raw: &str,
         now: OffsetDateTime,
     ) -> Result<Manifest, ManifestError> {
         use time::format_description::well_known::Rfc3339;
         #[derive(Deserialize)]
         struct Raw {
             manifest_version: u32,
             generated_at: String,
             retention: Retention,
             /// Round-43 B5: the field the return path
             /// reads. Round-42 accessed
             /// `raw.oversize_bundle_ack` without
             /// declaring it here. `Option` + `default`
             /// so manifests written before round-41 B8
             /// still parse (absent → false).
             #[serde(default)]
             oversize_bundle_ack: Option<bool>,
             /// Round-101 B1: `Option` so the ABSENT case maps to the
             /// typed `ManifestError::MissingGcl` (not a serde error).
             #[serde(default)]
             gcl: Option<RawGclRecord>,
             entries: Vec<RawEntry>,
         }
         #[derive(Deserialize)]
         struct RawGclRecord {
             path: String,
             sha256: String,
             last_updated: String,
             fetched_at: String,
             cache_max_age_secs: u64,
         }
         #[derive(Deserialize)]
         #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
         struct RawEntry {
             spec: u32,
             vendor_list_version: u32,
             tcf_policy_version: u32,
             last_updated: String,
             path: String,
             sha256: String,
             // Round-105 B5: optional cache metadata (round-104 B3).
             #[serde(default)]
             fetched_at: Option<String>,
             #[serde(default)]
             cache_max_age_secs: Option<u64>,
         }
         let raw: Raw = serde_json::from_str(raw)
             .map_err(|e| ManifestError::Json(e.to_string()))?;
         if raw.manifest_version != 1 {
             return Err(ManifestError::UnsupportedVersion { got: raw.manifest_version });
         }
         let generated_at = OffsetDateTime::parse(&raw.generated_at, &Rfc3339)
             .map_err(|_| ManifestError::BadTimestamp {
                 field: "generated_at", raw: raw.generated_at.clone(),
             })?;
         // Round-39 B4: reject future dates (clock skew /
         // manual manifest edit).
         if generated_at > now {
             return Err(ManifestError::FutureGeneratedAt {
                 generated_at: raw.generated_at.clone(),
                 now: now.format(&Rfc3339).unwrap_or_default(),
             });
         }
         let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
         let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(raw.entries.len());
         for e in raw.entries {
             if !(e.spec == 2 || e.spec == 3) {
                 return Err(ManifestError::OutOfRangeSpec { spec: e.spec });
             }
             if e.vendor_list_version < 1 {
                 return Err(ManifestError::ZeroListVersion);
             }
             if !seen.insert((e.spec, e.vendor_list_version)) {
                 return Err(ManifestError::DuplicatePair {
                     spec: e.spec, list: e.vendor_list_version,
                 });
             }
             let expected_prefix = format!("spec{}/", e.spec);
             if !e.path.starts_with(&expected_prefix) {
                 return Err(ManifestError::BadPath {
                     path: e.path, reason: "missing spec{2,3}/ prefix",
                 });
             }
             if e.path.contains("..") || e.path.starts_with('/') {
                 return Err(ManifestError::BadPath {
                     path: e.path, reason: "contains .. or starts with /",
                 });
             }
             // Round-43 B5: enforce the promised regex
             // `^spec[23]/vendor-list-v\d+\.json$` inline.
             // Round-42's version accepted
             // `vendor-list-v.json` because `.all()` is
             // vacuously true on an EMPTY digit sequence —
             // `\d+` requires at least one. The digit run
             // is also cross-checked against the entry's
             // declared `vendor_list_version` so a
             // renamed file can't silently shadow another
             // version.
             let stem = e.path.strip_prefix(&expected_prefix).unwrap_or("");
             let digits = stem
                 .strip_prefix("vendor-list-v")
                 .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(".json"))
                 .filter(|d| !d.is_empty() && d.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()));
             let Some(digits) = digits else {
                 return Err(ManifestError::BadPath {
                     path: e.path,
                     reason: "does not match spec[23]/vendor-list-v<N>.json",
                 });
             };
             if digits.parse::<u32>().ok() != Some(e.vendor_list_version) {
                 return Err(ManifestError::PathVersionMismatch {
                     path: e.path.clone(),
                     declared: e.vendor_list_version,
                 });
             }
             // Round-41 B10: SHA-256 must be exactly 64
             // lowercase hex chars. Length check alone
             // accepted `"g" * 64`.
             if e.sha256.len() != 64
                 || !e.sha256.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !c.is_ascii_uppercase())
             {
                 return Err(ManifestError::Sha256Format {
                     path: e.path.clone(), got: e.sha256.clone(),
                 });
             }
             let last_updated = OffsetDateTime::parse(&e.last_updated, &Rfc3339)
                 .map_err(|_| ManifestError::BadTimestamp {
                     field: "last_updated", raw: e.last_updated.clone(),
                 })?;
             // Round-41 B10: last_updated must not be in
             // the future either.
             if last_updated > now {
                 return Err(ManifestError::FutureTimestamp {
                     field: "last_updated", raw: e.last_updated.clone(),
                 });
             }
             // Round-41 B10: retention enforcement is
             // executable, not just documented.
             // Round-90 B2: the frozen spec-2 list (final TCF
             // v2.2 GVL, lastUpdated 2023-11-16) is AGE-EXEMPT.
             // It is older than any --max-age-days window by
             // design, yet mandatory spec-2 coverage (below)
             // REQUIRES it, so the age gate applies to spec-3
             // entries ONLY. Without this exemption every build
             // fails RetentionExceeded on the one v2 list it is
             // required to carry.
             let age = (now - last_updated).whole_days();
             if e.spec != 2 && age > i64::from(raw.retention.max_age_days) {  // round-47 auction core: from, not `as`
                 // Retention exceeded — the manifest is stale,
                 // or was generated with a smaller
                 // --max-age-days than these spec-3 entries need.
                 return Err(ManifestError::RetentionExceeded {
                     path: e.path.clone(), age_days: age,
                     retention_days: raw.retention.max_age_days,
                 });
             }
             // Round-106 B3: the optional cache metadata is
             // validated AND initialized — the fields come in PAIRS
             // (one present without the other → BadTimestamp-class
             // error), fetched_at parses RFC 3339 and may not be in
             // the future, and the pair's checked expiry addition is
             // exercised so overflow fails here, not at reuse time.
             let fetched_at = match (&e.fetched_at, e.cache_max_age_secs) {
                 (None, None) => None,
                 (Some(raw_ts), Some(secs)) => {
                     let ts = parse_rfc3339("entry.fetched_at", raw_ts)?;
                     if ts > now {
                         return Err(ManifestError::FutureTimestamp {
                             field: "entry.fetched_at", raw: raw_ts.clone(),
                         });
                     }
                     // overflow probe (round-106 B3):
                     i64::try_from(secs).ok()
                         .and_then(|s| ts.checked_add(time::Duration::seconds(s)))
                         .ok_or(ManifestError::EntryExpiryOverflow {
                             path: e.path.clone(),
                         })?;
                     Some(ts)
                 }
                 _ => {
                     return Err(ManifestError::BadTimestamp {
                         field: "entry.fetched_at/cache_max_age_secs",
                         raw: "fields must be present together".into(),
                     });
                 }
             };
             entries.push(ManifestEntry {
                 spec: e.spec,
                 vendor_list_version: e.vendor_list_version,
                 tcf_policy_version: e.tcf_policy_version,
                 last_updated_rfc3339: e.last_updated,
                 last_updated,
                 path: e.path,
                 sha256: e.sha256,
                 fetched_at,
                 cache_max_age_secs: e.cache_max_age_secs,
             });
         }
         // Round-42 B10: manifest ordering must ALREADY be
         // `spec asc, vendor_list_version desc` — the
         // refresh tool writes it that way. Silently
         // sorting hides deployer edits that reordered
         // entries. Validate order; error on mismatch;
         // don't sort in-place.
         let expected_order = {
             let mut clone = entries.clone();
             clone.sort_by(|a, b| a.spec.cmp(&b.spec)
                 .then_with(|| b.vendor_list_version.cmp(&a.vendor_list_version)));
             clone
         };
         if entries.iter().zip(&expected_order).enumerate().any(|(_, (a, b))|
             (a.spec, a.vendor_list_version) != (b.spec, b.vendor_list_version)
         ) {
             return Err(ManifestError::WrongEntryOrder);
         }
         // Round-41 B10: spec-version coverage. Refuse a
         // manifest that has entries for only spec 2 or
         // only spec 3 — production traffic mixes both,
         // so a single-spec archive is a deployment bug.
         let has_spec_2 = entries.iter().any(|e| e.spec == 2);
         let has_spec_3 = entries.iter().any(|e| e.spec == 3);
         if !(has_spec_2 && has_spec_3) {
             return Err(ManifestError::MissingSpecCoverage {
                 has_spec_2, has_spec_3,
             });
         }
         // Round-101 B1: GCL — required, path-constrained, timestamp-
         // parsed, freshness-enforced (round-100 B2: `now >= expires_at`
         // → GclStale; the GCL's own RFC 9111 lifetime, never the
         // 45-day GVL window).
         let raw_gcl = raw.gcl.ok_or(ManifestError::MissingGcl)?;
         if raw_gcl.path != "gcl.json" {
             return Err(ManifestError::BadPath { path: raw_gcl.path, reason: "gcl path must be gcl.json" });
         }
         let gcl = GclRecord {
             last_updated: parse_rfc3339("gcl.last_updated", &raw_gcl.last_updated)?,
             fetched_at: parse_rfc3339("gcl.fetched_at", &raw_gcl.fetched_at)?,
             path: raw_gcl.path,
             sha256: check_sha256_format(raw_gcl.sha256)?,
             cache_max_age_secs: raw_gcl.cache_max_age_secs,
         };
         // Round-104 B1: `expires_at()` is FALLIBLE (checked addition
         // → GclExpiryOverflow); handle the Result here, and enforce
         // the future-fetched_at rejection:
         if gcl.fetched_at > now {
             return Err(ManifestError::FutureTimestamp {
                 field: "gcl.fetched_at", raw: gcl.fetched_at.to_string(),
             });
         }
         let gcl_expires = gcl.expires_at()?; // GclExpiryOverflow on overflow
         if now >= gcl_expires {
             return Err(ManifestError::GclStale {
                 expires_at: gcl_expires.to_string(),
                 now: now.to_string(),
             });
         }
         // (`parse_rfc3339` / `check_sha256_format` are THIS module's
         // shared helpers — bodies in the round-103 B2 block; one
         // definition each. Round-104 B1: build.rs KEEPS the
         // `ValidatedGcl` returned by `validate_gcl_json` and calls
         // `check_gcl_consistency(&manifest, &validated_gcl)?` so the
         // manifest/blob `last_updated` cross-check actually runs.)
         Ok(Manifest {
             manifest_version: raw.manifest_version,
             generated_at_rfc3339: raw.generated_at,
             generated_at,
             retention: raw.retention,
             // Round-43 B5: `Raw.oversize_bundle_ack` is
             // now declared, so this resolves.
             oversize_bundle_ack: raw.oversize_bundle_ack.unwrap_or(false),
             gcl,
             entries,
         })
     }

     /// Round-88 H3: heal a crashed or interrupted GVL-archive swap. The
     /// caller MUST already hold the EXCLUSIVE `fs2` advisory lock on
     /// `data/gvl_archive.lock` (see §Concurrency safety); this helper
     /// runs ONLY the pure `std::fs` four-case recovery decision, so it
     /// adds NO `fs2` dependency and stays wasm-clean (round-86 creative caching —
     /// `auctioneer-gvl-schema` cross-compiles to wasm32). `build.rs` (its
     /// missing-`live` read branch) and the refresh tool (step 11, before
     /// its swap) both call this under the held exclusive lock, then
     /// read/swap while STILL holding it (round-63 H2 — no unlocked
     /// window). `archive_dir` is the live archive dir
     /// (`data/gvl_archive`); the single fixed aside is its `.old`
     /// sibling (`data/gvl_archive.old`, round-62 B3). Keyed only on which
     /// of the two directories exists:
     /// - live present + `.old` present → crash AFTER the 2nd rename; the
     ///   new archive is already installed, so DELETE the stale `.old`.
     /// - live ABSENT + `.old` present → crash BETWEEN the renames;
     ///   `rename(.old → live)`.
     /// - live present + no `.old` → nothing to do.
     /// - live ABSENT + no `.old` → first install / clean state; nothing
     ///   to recover (the caller's swap installs `tx → live` directly).
     pub fn recover_gvl_archive(archive_dir: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
         let mut old_name = archive_dir
             .file_name()
             .map(std::ffi::OsStr::to_os_string)
             .unwrap_or_default();
         old_name.push(".old");
         let old_dir = archive_dir.with_file_name(old_name);
         match (archive_dir.exists(), old_dir.exists()) {
             // Crash after the 2nd rename: new `live` already complete.
             (true, true) => std::fs::remove_dir_all(&old_dir),
             // Crash between the renames: restore the aside, then fsync
             // the parent so the restored dir entry is durable.
             (false, true) => {
                 std::fs::rename(&old_dir, archive_dir)?;
                 if let Some(parent) = archive_dir.parent() {
                     std::fs::File::open(parent)?.sync_all()?;
                 }
                 Ok(())
             }
             // Steady state, or first-install/clean: nothing to do.
             (true, false) | (false, false) => Ok(()),
         }
     }
     ```

     Additional variants on `ManifestError`:

     ```rust
     /// Round-44 H3: derives `thiserror::Error`, which
     /// supplies the `Display` impl the build script's
     /// `panic!("manifest validation: {e}")` needs.
     /// Round-42 derived only `Debug`, so that format
     /// string would not compile.
     #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
     pub enum ManifestError {
         // ... existing variants, each with an #[error(..)]
         // attribute supplying its Display text ...
         /// Round-41 B10: hex format enforcement.
         #[error("{path}: sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex chars, got {got:?}")]
         Sha256Format { path: String, got: String },
         /// Round-41 B10: last_updated in future.
         FutureTimestamp { field: &'static str, raw: String },
         /// Round-41 B10: entry age exceeds retention cap.
         RetentionExceeded { path: String, age_days: i64, retention_days: u32 },
         /// Round-41 B10: manifest missing spec-2 or spec-3
         /// coverage.
         MissingSpecCoverage { has_spec_2: bool, has_spec_3: bool },
         /// Round-42 B10: entries not in canonical
         /// (spec asc, vendor_list_version desc) order.
         WrongEntryOrder,
         /// Round-43 B5: the `vendor-list-v<N>.json`
         /// filename's N disagrees with the entry's
         /// declared `vendor_list_version`.
         PathVersionMismatch { path: String, declared: u32 },
     }

     // Round-47 auction core: `?`/`ok_or` + `return Err`, not `.expect()` /
     // `assert_eq!` (build.rs lint contract).
     let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&raw)
         .map_err(|e| format!("{}: archive JSON parse: {e}", entry.path))?;
     let embedded_last_updated = parsed.get("lastUpdated")
         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
         .ok_or_else(|| format!("{}: archive JSON missing lastUpdated", entry.path))?;
     if embedded_last_updated != entry.last_updated_rfc3339 {
         return Err(format!(
             "manifest last_updated {} disagrees with archive JSON lastUpdated {} in {}",
             entry.last_updated_rfc3339, embedded_last_updated, entry.path
         ).into());
     }
     ```

     **Final-bundle proof — separate from the GVL cap**
     (round-43 H4 canonical). The compressed-cap check
     inside build.rs asserts the GVL archive ALONE fits
     under `GVL_BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_BYTES`, but
     Cloudflare's ceilings apply to the ENTIRE compiled
     artifact — all auctioneer-* crates + edgezero + the JS
     shim + the GVL. The CI gate therefore parses
     **wrangler's own reported figures** rather than
     measuring the output directory:

     `wrangler deploy --dry-run` prints
     `Total Upload: <X> KiB / gzip: <Y> KiB`. The gate
     extracts both and asserts:
     - `Y` (gzip) ≤ **9,000,000 bytes** — under CF's
       documented 10 MB _after compression_ ceiling with
       headroom. (Free-plan deploys must additionally
       fit 3 MB; the gate takes the target plan from a
       CI variable.)
     - `X` (total upload, uncompressed) ≤
       **60,000,000 bytes** — under CF's documented 64 MB
       _before compression_ ceiling.

     Round-43 H4 retires round-42's `du -sb out/cf`
     approach: `du` measures an uncompressed directory
     that may include files wrangler never uploads, and
     it cannot see the gzip figure that the 10 MB limit
     actually applies to. Both numbers are decimal MB per
     the Cloudflare docs — the plan's earlier binary-MiB
     constants (e.g. `10 * 1024 * 1024 = 10_485_760`)
     were LARGER than the real 10,000,000-byte limit and
     would have passed CI while failing deploy.

     Fastly's `fastly compute build` + `spin build`
     receive analogous gates reading each tool's own
     reported package size.

     **Round-92 user sync — OWNERSHIP: these packaged-artifact gates are
     bounded fanout Task Fanout-8 CI work, and GDPR fanout makes NO packaged-Worker size
     PROOF claim.** The workflows that run `wrangler deploy
--dry-run` / `fastly compute build` / `spin build` land with
     the (currently blocked) Fanout-8 CI matrix — Task 23's
     `cargo build --release` proves compilation, NOT that the
     packaged Worker fits Cloudflare's 10 MB-compressed / 64
     MB-uncompressed ceilings. What GDPR fanout DOES prove is the
     PROXY bound it owns: build.rs's unconditional
     compressed-cap gate (`GVL_BUNDLE_MAX_COMPRESSED_MIB`,
     sized with headroom against the 10 MB ceiling) plus the
     24 MiB raw cap — the GVL being the dominant artifact
     component. The definitive whole-package figures are
     deferred WITH Fanout-8; until then GDPR fanout's dev-complete label
     (Task 23 Step 0) is also what prevents anyone treating
     the proxy bound as a production packaging proof.

  WITHOUT breaking the "build.rs cannot import its own library"
  constraint.

  **Round-90 H4 — NO per-vendor runtime warn (amplification fix).**
  `Gvl::load_from_json` does NOT log per deleted vendor. With the
  4-entry evictable LRU (`GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`) and ~183 deleted
  vendors in the official v2 list, a per-vendor runtime warn re-emitted
  hundreds of lines on every cache miss as versions rotate through the
  cap — request-triggerable log amplification. Deleted-vendor
  observability instead lives as a BUILD-TIME aggregate: `build.rs`
  emits one `cargo:warning` per archive entry carrying the deleted-vendor
  COUNT. The deleted set is fixed at build (the archive is
  `include_bytes!`), so build time is the correct, non-amplifying place;
  the runtime lazy-parse path stays silent. `deleted_date` is still
  loaded onto each `Vendor` (it drives `Vendor::is_deleted_at(now)` and the
  Task 9 enforcement denial) — only the logging moves.
