  ```rust
  //! Runtime Global CMP List — lowered ONCE from the baked artifact.
  //!
  //! Single-parse-path rule: the ONLY JSON parse of the GCL at runtime
  //! goes through `auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_gcl_json`, the same
  //! validator the build gate ran. No independent serde call.

  use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  use std::sync::OnceLock;
  use time::OffsetDateTime;

  // Round-108 H7: module scope, so `is_baked()` can observe it.
  static BAKED: OnceLock<Gcl> = OnceLock::new();

  pub struct CmpRecord {
      pub id: u16,
      pub deleted_date: Option<OffsetDateTime>,
  }

  pub struct Gcl {
      pub cmps: BTreeMap<u16, CmpRecord>,
      pub expires_at: OffsetDateTime,
  }

  impl Gcl {
      /// Boot/baked constructor: lowers `auctioneer_config::baked_gcl_json()`
      /// once into a process-static. Called at boot alongside the
      /// host-primitives install, so its heap sits inside the measured
      /// baseline (round-100 B3 — no separate budget term).
      pub fn baked() -> &'static Gcl {
          BAKED.get_or_init(|| {
              let expires_at = OffsetDateTime::from_unix_timestamp(
                  auctioneer_config::gcl_expires_at_unix_secs(),
              )
              // Fail-closed: an unconvertible expiry reads as already
              // stale, never as never-expiring.
              .unwrap_or(OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH);
              match auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_gcl_json(
                  auctioneer_config::baked_gcl_json(),
              ) {
                  Ok(validated) => Gcl {
                      cmps: validated
                          .cmps
                          .into_iter()
                          .map(|(id, cmp)| {
                              (id, CmpRecord { id, deleted_date: cmp.deleted_date })
                          })
                          .collect(),
                      expires_at,
                  },
                  // Unreachable for a build-gate-validated artifact, but
                  // defined anyway (round-106 B1): an EMPTY list with a
                  // PAST expiry — every TCF request then takes the
                  // stale-GCL fail-closed path and emits warning 10019,
                  // which is the observable signal; non-TCF traffic is
                  // unaffected, and this crate stays log-free (the
                  // round-90 H4 silent-runtime rule).
                  Err(_) => Gcl {
                      cmps: BTreeMap::new(),
                      expires_at: OffsetDateTime::UNIX_EPOCH,
                  },
              }
          })
      }

      /// Round-108 H7: boot-order probe — true once `baked()` has
      /// initialized the static. Used by the Task 11
      /// `bootstrap_adapter_initializes_gcl()` test (a plain pub fn:
      /// cross-crate tests cannot see `#[cfg(test)]` items).
      pub fn is_baked() -> bool { BAKED.get().is_some() }

      /// Test constructor — direct fields, no JSON.
      #[cfg(test)]
      pub fn for_test(cmps: Vec<CmpRecord>, expires_at: OffsetDateTime) -> Gcl {
          Gcl {
              cmps: cmps.into_iter().map(|c| (c.id, c)).collect(),
              expires_at,
          }
      }
  }
  ```

  No LRU — one current GCL. Consumers: `PrivacyContext::resolve`
  takes `gcl: &Gcl` (Task 8 Step 2b uses `cmps` for authenticity +
  deletion and `expires_at` for staleness); the handler passes
  `Gcl::baked()` into the `AuctionContext` (Task 13). Unit tests
  (in `gcl.rs`, +2 to the Task 4 count — round-106 B1):
  `baked_gcl_lowering_is_fresh_and_nonempty()` (calls `Gcl::baked()`
  against the real baked artifact: nonempty `cmps`, `expires_at >
UNIX_EPOCH`, and a known official CMP id present) and
  `gcl_for_test_maps_ids_and_deleted_dates()` (two records in, keyed
  lookup + `deleted_date` round-trip out).

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `GvlStore::baked()`** — round-39
      B3 lazy-parse shape (retires round-37 B2's eager parse
      which was uncompilable at the CF isolate memory limit).
      Boot cost is O(N) `HashMap::insert`s of `&'static [u8]`
      pointers; parse latency is deferred to first
      `get(spec, list)` per pair. `BakedGvlEntry.raw` is
      `&'static [u8]` (round-39 B3: changed from `&'static
str`; `include_bytes!` yields byte slices).

  ```rust
  use lru::LruCache;
  use std::num::NonZeroUsize;
  use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};
  use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;

  impl GvlStore {
      pub fn baked() -> &'static GvlStore {
          static STORE: OnceLock<GvlStore> = OnceLock::new();
          STORE.get_or_init(|| {
              let mut raw_index = std::collections::HashMap::new();
              for entry in auctioneer_config::gvl_archive() {
                  raw_index.insert(
                      (entry.spec, entry.vendor_list_version),
                      entry.raw,
                  );
              }
              // Round-47 auction core: `.unwrap_or(NonZeroUsize::MIN)`, not
              // `.expect()` — `expect_used` is denied in production.
              // The const is a nonzero literal, so the fallback is
              // unreachable; MIN (1) is a safe floor regardless.
              let entries_nz = NonZeroUsize::new(GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES)
                  .unwrap_or(NonZeroUsize::MIN);
              GvlStore {
                  raw_index,
                  cache: Mutex::new(LruCache::new(entries_nz)),
              }
          })
      }

      /// Parse-on-demand, singleflight-within-cell, entry-count
      /// bounded (round-46 B2 — no byte accounting).
      pub fn get(&self, spec: u32, list: u32) -> Option<Gvl> {
          let key = (spec, list);

          // Round-44 H2: check raw_index FIRST so unknown
          // versions never touch the cache (an attacker
          // walking (3,1),(3,2)… could otherwise evict the
          // hot set).
          let raw = *self.raw_index.get(&key)?;

          // Take-or-create the shared cell under the lock;
          // parse runs outside it. `get_or_insert` here also
          // marks the entry most-recently-used and performs any
          // count-based eviction atomically (round-46 B2: no
          // separate byte pass that could double-count or leak).
          let cell = {
              let mut cache = self.cache.lock().ok()?;
              Arc::clone(cache.get_or_insert(key, || Arc::new(OnceCell::new())))
          };

          let parsed = cell.get_or_init(|| {
              // Round-57 B-k: pass the slot spec INTO runtime
              // lowering — `Some(spec)` — so `validate_gvl_json`
              // HARD-REJECTS a blob whose declared
              // `gvlSpecificationVersion` doesn't match the slot it
              // was fetched into (or is an unsupported version).
              // Runtime validation is now as strong as the build
              // gate, not a debug-only assertion. A reject → parse
              // error → the empty sentinel below → fail-closed miss.
              Gvl::load_from_json_bytes(raw, Some(spec)).unwrap_or_else(|err| {
                  log::error!(target: "auctioneer::gvl",
                      "baked GVL entry ({spec}, {list}) failed schema/spec check: {err:?}");
                  Gvl::empty()
              })
          });

          if parsed.vendor_list_version() == 0 {
              return None;   // parse/spec-failure sentinel → miss
          }

          Some(parsed.clone())
      }
  }
  ```

  `LruCache::get_or_insert` returns the existing cell or
  inserts a fresh one and evicts the least-recently-used key
  when the map is already at `GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` —
  count-bounded eviction with no byte bookkeeping to get wrong
  (round-46 B2). There is **no `Gvl::heap_bytes()`** (round-46
  B3: `BTreeMap` has no capacity API and a hand-rolled sum
  cannot bound tree nodes, the six nested per-vendor
  `BTreeSet`s, `deleted_date`, or allocator overhead — so no
  honest byte figure exists to evict on). Resident parsed-GVL
  memory is `≤ GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES × max_gvl_heap` plus
  the Arcs still held by in-flight `PrivacyContext`s — an
  envelope GDPR fanout documents but does not prove; the byte-exact
  reservation lands in bounded fanout with admission.

  **Round-46 B4 — the Arc-retention reality (why GDPR fanout does NOT
  claim a hard GVL byte bound).** An evicted `Gvl` is not freed
  while any live `PrivacyContext` still holds its `Arc<GvlInner>`
  (each `resolve` clones the Arc into the context and holds it
  for the auction's lifetime). Worse, privacy resolution runs
  BEFORE any stream-admission gate, so the number of
  simultaneously-retained Arcs is bounded by in-flight auctions,
  not by `max_active_body_streams` — arbitrarily many queued
  auctions can each retain a `Gvl`. A memory proof of the form
  `cache + max_active_body_streams × max_gvl_heap` is therefore
  UNSOUND (round-46 B4), and the round-45 draft that asserted it
  is withdrawn. Bounding retained GVLs requires one of the two
  bounded fanout options — admit auctions BEFORE privacy resolution, or
  materialize compact permissions and drop the `Arc<GvlInner>`
  before fanout — both of which land with the admission gate in
  bounded fanout. GDPR fanout's cache is count-bounded and its GVL memory is an
  UNPROVEN envelope; the whole-isolate byte proof is an bounded fanout
  deliverable, not an GDPR fanout claim.

  Round-46 B2/B3/B4 regressions (replacing the withdrawn

    `GVL_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + 1` distinct versions; assert

  - `gvl_cache_singleflights_concurrent_misses()` — two

    round-48 auction core rewrite. The old
    `runtime_and_build_schema_agree_on_valid_gvl()` called
    `validate_gvl_json` TWICE and asserted `a == b` — tautological
    (the validator is deterministic; it proved nothing about the
    runtime). The real agreement to check is that the runtime
    `Gvl` lowering preserves what the validated DTO says. Validate
    ONCE via the standalone crate, then compare the runtime `Gvl`
    against that DTO:
    **Round-49 B4 — written against the API the plan actually
    defines.** `Gvl` exposes `vendor(id: u16) -> Option<&Vendor>`
    (there is no `vendor_count()` and no version accessors — the
    version fields are `pub` on `GvlInner`), and `Vendor.purposes`
    is a `BTreeSet<u8>` **field**, not a method. The DTO side
    carries `Vec<u32>`, so the comparison must NORMALIZE rather
    than compare two different types:
    ```rust
    /// DTO `Vec<u32>` → the runtime's `BTreeSet<u8>` domain.
    /// Ids outside 1..=24 cannot survive lowering, so they are
    /// dropped here exactly as the lowering drops them.
    fn to_purpose_set(raw: &[u32]) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<u8> {
        raw.iter().filter_map(|&p| u8::try_from(p).ok()).collect()
    }

    for entry in auctioneer_config::gvl_archive() {
        let raw_str = std::str::from_utf8(entry.raw)
            .expect("build.rs validated UTF-8 for every archive entry");
        // ONE authoritative validation, via the standalone crate.
        let dto = auctioneer_gvl_schema::validate_gvl_json(raw_str, Some(entry.spec)).unwrap();
        // Runtime lowering of the SAME bytes.
        let gvl = Gvl::load_from_json(raw_str, Some(entry.spec)).unwrap();
        // Identity agreement (pub fields on the inner shape).
        assert_eq!(gvl.vendor_list_version(), dto.vendor_list_version);
        assert_eq!(gvl.tcf_policy_version(), dto.tcf_policy_version);
        // Content agreement: EVERY DTO vendor survives lowering
        // with the same purpose set. This is the assertion that
        // actually proves runtime == validator (the old test
        // compared the validator against itself).
        for (&dto_id, dto_vendor) in &dto.vendors {
            let Ok(id) = u16::try_from(dto_id) else { continue };  // >u16 rejected upstream
            let lowered = gvl.vendor(id)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("vendor {id} lost in lowering"));
            assert_eq!(lowered.purposes, to_purpose_set(&dto_vendor.purposes));
            assert_eq!(lowered.leg_int_purposes, to_purpose_set(&dto_vendor.leg_int_purposes));
        }
    }
    ```
    The `load_from_json_bytes(&[u8])` variant used
    inside `GvlStore::get` performs the same UTF-8
    validation once and short-circuits on failure; the
    test uses the `&str` variant because both parse
    paths must agree, and the `&str` API is the
    canonical validator entry point.

− the deleted `gvl_raw_parses_as_json` smoke − the ignored latency
row; exact-name sweep confirmed all 66 schema + 26 privacy + 7
config roster names; `auctioneer-gvl-schema` cross-compiles to
wasm32-unknown-unknown). Archive fetched LIVE: frozen spec-2 v224
(440,614 B) + spec-3 v153–v174 (22 versions, current v174 925,444 B,
retention walk stopped at v148 on the 180-day window, budget kept 21
of 25 eligible) + `gcl.json` (29,500 B; 265 CMPs, 75 deleted); raw
sum 20,292,875 B ≤ 20,971,520 B. **Operational deadlines (by
design):** the GCL freshness gate FAILS BUILDS after
2026-09-03T16:01:13Z and the 45-day manifest gate after mid-October
— rerun `cargo run -p auctioneer-refresh-gvl-archive` before then.
Reconciliations:

1. The tool's single run-start `now` was unexecutable — the
   current-list `fetched_at` postdates it and the validator rejects
   it as a future timestamp; `generated_at` is stamped AFTER the
   fetches and step 10 validates with a fresh clock reading (same
   call build.rs makes).
2. `serde_json` was NOT in auctioneer-config's build-dependencies
   despite the plan's claim (added); the tool needs `time` as a
   direct dependency (schema API is `time`-typed; chrono stays for
   HTTP-date parsing as planned); `lru` entered the workspace table
   at preflight.
3. `GclSchemaError` has no over-cap variant, so
   `gcl_over_raw_cap_rejected` asserts `InvalidJson` with a message
   naming the cap (candidate future amendment: a dedicated
   variant).
4. Calendar-proofing: the harness's archive runner raises
   `AUCTIONEER__GVL__ARCHIVE__MAX_AGE_DAYS`, and checked-in fixtures use
   36,500-day retention + a 100-year GCL lifetime so freshness gates
   don't fire before the validators under test.
5. The gzip-bomb test drives the bounded-read helper over an
   in-memory flate2 stream with a test-scoped counting allocator
   (one scoped `#[expect(unsafe_code)]` — a measured allocation
   bound cannot be built otherwise).
6. Smaller: the emitted accessor returns `ENTRIES` (not the plan's
   double-reference `&ENTRIES`); `Gvl` gained
   `special_purpose()`/`feature()` accessors (dead-code deny; Task 6
   needs them); the parse-counter test hook is STORE-scoped (a

### Task 4a: GVL health endpoint + unavailable-lookup counter

Round-38 H1 owner task, round-39 B1+B2 rewrite. Round-38's
sketch (a) declared a handler "next to /status" but never
registered the route in `edgezero.toml` or the ingress
`body_caps::RouteTable`, so the endpoint wasn't actually
reachable; (b) tried to thread the counter through
`AuctionContext.metrics`, but the canonical §7.6 shape has

**Route + exposure policy (round-41 H2 canonical,
retires round-39 B1's shape which claimed K8s
NetworkPolicy could restrict an HTTP path):**

- Path: `/internal/health/gvl` (GET). The `/internal/*`
  prefix is a AUCTIONEER CONVENTION for operational access. Round-48
  H1: the route is **fail-closed** (401) unless an explicit
  `HealthAccessPolicy` is installed at boot — it is NOT open by
  default.
- **Round-41 H2 CORRECTION:** Kubernetes NetworkPolicy
  operates at L3/L4 (IP + port) and CANNOT restrict by
  HTTP path. The round-40 H2 snippet promising a
  NetworkPolicy path filter was wrong. The correct
  ingress-level restrictions are:
  - **Cloudflare Workers:** `[[triggers.http]]` route
    guard with a Cloudflare Access Application over
    `/internal/*` (auth at L7).
  - **Fastly Compute:** VCL prefix match + require
    signed request or edge-network policy.
  - **Kubernetes:** an L7 proxy (nginx-ingress,
    istio) with a `HTTPRoute` matching `/internal/*`
    and pointing at an `AuthorizationPolicy` or
    external auth service. `NetworkPolicy` alone
    does NOT satisfy this.
  - **Standalone Axum**: run behind an ingress that
    terminates auth (nginx `auth_request`, envoy
    `ext_authz`).
- **Round-48 H1 — auctioneer ships the handler FAIL-CLOSED by
  default.** The round-47 "None = open + WARN" model was not
  fail-closed: an operator who simply forgot to install a token
  got an open endpoint. Now the endpoint is CLOSED (401) unless
  the boot EXPLICITLY installs one of two policies:
  - a token authenticator (`Token`), OR
  - an explicit unauthenticated acknowledgement
    (`UnauthenticatedAcknowledged`), which the adapter installs
    ONLY when the deploy config sets `allow_unauthenticated_health
= true` (a machine-checkable opt-in, not a silent default).
    If NEITHER is installed — the default `OnceLock` state — the
    handler returns **401** (a missing install is a
    misconfiguration, and fail-closed is the safe reading). The
    token is resolved BY THE ADAPTER from its own host API and
    installed as a typed primitive — portable core never reads
    `std::env` (empty on Workers anyway):

  ```rust
  // crates/auctioneer-core/src/host_primitives/registry.rs
  pub trait HealthAuth: Send + Sync {
      /// Constant-time compare against the configured
      /// token. Implementations MUST NOT short-circuit
      /// on first byte mismatch.
      fn verify(&self, presented: &str) -> bool;
      /// Round-50 H4: stable identity for the idempotent-reinstall
      /// check (the 32-byte digest for `BearerToken`). Compared
      /// instead of the `Arc` pointer so two authenticators built
      /// from the same secret are equal.
      fn identity(&self) -> [u8; 32];
  }

  /// Round-48 H1: an EXPLICIT policy — there is no implicit
  /// "open" state. Absence of an installed policy is fail-closed.
  /// Round-50 H4: hand-written `PartialEq` (a `dyn` trait object
  /// can't derive it) compares `Token` by `identity()`.
  pub enum HealthAccessPolicy {
      /// Bearer token required (the common production case).
      Token(Arc<dyn HealthAuth>),
      /// Endpoint served WITHOUT auth — installed only when the
      /// deploy set `allow_unauthenticated_health = true` and is
      /// relying on an ingress guard. The explicit variant makes
      /// "open" a deliberate, greppable choice.
      UnauthenticatedAcknowledged,
      /// Round-51 H1: FROZEN fail-closed. Installed at boot when the
      /// adapter resolved no token and no opt-in, so a LATER request
      /// (Cloudflare/Fastly/Spin install from request entrypoints)
      /// cannot flip the endpoint open — the `OnceLock` is already
      /// set, so any conflicting reinstall is a `ConflictingPolicy`
      /// error. `Closed` authorizes as `Deny`, same as never-set.
      Closed,
  }
  impl PartialEq for HealthAccessPolicy {
      fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
          use HealthAccessPolicy::{Closed, Token, UnauthenticatedAcknowledged};
          match (self, other) {
              (UnauthenticatedAcknowledged, UnauthenticatedAcknowledged) => true,
              (Closed, Closed) => true,
              (Token(a), Token(b)) => a.identity() == b.identity(),
              _ => false,
          }
      }
  }

  static HEALTH_POLICY: OnceLock<HealthAccessPolicy> = OnceLock::new();

  /// `None` (never installed) OR `Some(Closed)` → handler
  /// fail-closes to 401. The two differ only in mutability: once
  /// `Closed` is installed the cell is frozen (round-51 H1).
  pub fn health_policy_handle() -> Option<&'static HealthAccessPolicy> {
      HEALTH_POLICY.get()
  }

  /// Round-43 H3: the adapter's declared counter scope.
  static COUNTER_SCOPE: OnceLock<&'static str> = OnceLock::new();
  pub fn counter_scope_handle() -> &'static str {
      COUNTER_SCOPE.get().copied().unwrap_or("unknown")
  }

  /// Round-50 B5/H4: a dedicated GDPR fanout error type — `AuctioneerBootError`
  /// belongs to bounded fanout's (upstream-gated) admission stack, and GDPR fanout
  /// must not depend on it.
  #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
  pub enum HealthBootError {
      #[error("a conflicting health policy or counter scope was already installed")]
      ConflictingPolicy,
      #[error("health config value {key} is not a strict boolean (got {value:?})")]
      NonBooleanFlag { key: &'static str, value: String },
  }
  // Round-52 H2: the `InstallRace` variant is REMOVED — a lost
  // `set` race with an IDENTICAL policy is now success (idempotent),
  // and a lost race with a DIFFERENT policy is `ConflictingPolicy`;
  // there is no distinct race error.

  /// Round-50 H4: returns a `Result` and does NOT silently
  /// discard `OnceLock::set` errors. A second install is
  /// idempotent ONLY when the policy is byte-identical; a
  /// CONFLICTING second policy fails boot. (`HealthAccessPolicy`
  /// implements `PartialEq`; `Token` compares by the stored digest,
  /// not the `Arc` pointer, so two `BearerToken`s built from the
  /// same secret compare equal.)
  pub fn install_health_primitives(
      policy: HealthAccessPolicy,
      counter_scope: &'static str,
  ) -> Result<(), HealthBootError> {
      set_policy(policy)?;
      set_counter_scope(counter_scope)
  }

  /// Round-52 H2: race-IDEMPOTENT. `OnceLock::set` returns the
  /// rejected value on a lost race; two THREADS installing the
  /// identical policy must BOTH succeed, so on `set` failure we
  /// compare the value that actually won against ours. Only a
  /// genuinely different installed policy is `ConflictingPolicy`.
  /// (The round-51 draft returned `InstallRace` to the loser even
  /// when the policies were identical — a false boot failure under
  /// the concurrent-install path the integration tests exercise.)
  fn set_policy(policy: HealthAccessPolicy) -> Result<(), HealthBootError> {
      match HEALTH_POLICY.get() {
          Some(existing) if *existing == policy => Ok(()),
          Some(_) => Err(HealthBootError::ConflictingPolicy),
          None => match HEALTH_POLICY.set(policy) {
              Ok(()) => Ok(()),
              // Lost the race: whoever won is now present. Identical
              // → fine (idempotent); different → conflict. `set`
              // hands the rejected value back; compare against the
              // winner.
              Err(rejected) => match HEALTH_POLICY.get() {
                  Some(winner) if *winner == rejected => Ok(()),
                  _ => Err(HealthBootError::ConflictingPolicy),
              },
          },
      }
  }

  /// Round-51 H1 / round-52 H2: fail-loud AND race-idempotent —
  /// same pattern as `set_policy`.
  fn set_counter_scope(counter_scope: &'static str) -> Result<(), HealthBootError> {
      match COUNTER_SCOPE.get() {
          Some(existing) if *existing == counter_scope => Ok(()),
          Some(_) => Err(HealthBootError::ConflictingPolicy),
          None => match COUNTER_SCOPE.set(counter_scope) {
              Ok(()) => Ok(()),
              Err(rejected) => match COUNTER_SCOPE.get() {
                  Some(winner) if *winner == rejected => Ok(()),
                  _ => Err(HealthBootError::ConflictingPolicy),
              },
          },
      }
  }

  /// Round-51 H1: install the FROZEN `Closed` policy — the
  /// fail-closed default. Used by an adapter that resolved no token
  /// and no opt-in. Unlike the round-50 draft (which left
  /// `HEALTH_POLICY` UNSET, so a later request-entrypoint install
  /// could still open the endpoint), this SETS the cell to `Closed`,
  /// freezing it: any later conflicting install fails boot.
  pub fn install_health_primitives_without_policy(
      counter_scope: &'static str,
  ) -> Result<(), HealthBootError> {
      install_health_primitives(HealthAccessPolicy::Closed, counter_scope)
  }

  /// Round-48 H1: the handler's authorization decision, computed
  /// from the INSTALLED policy. Not installed OR `Closed` → 401
  /// (fail-closed). The handler returns early on `Deny` before
  /// touching the counter or building the payload.
  pub fn health_authorize(presented_bearer: Option<&str>) -> HealthAuthz {
      match health_policy_handle() {
          None | Some(HealthAccessPolicy::Closed) => HealthAuthz::Deny,  // fail-closed
          Some(HealthAccessPolicy::UnauthenticatedAcknowledged) => HealthAuthz::Allow,
          Some(HealthAccessPolicy::Token(auth)) => match presented_bearer {
              Some(tok) if auth.verify(tok) => HealthAuthz::Allow,
              _ => HealthAuthz::Deny,                       // missing/wrong → 401
          },
      }
  }

  pub enum HealthAuthz { Allow, Deny }

  /// Round-47 H5: the CONCRETE production authenticator (the
  /// only prior impl was a test double). Constant-time so a
  /// timing side-channel can't recover the token byte by byte.
  /// This adds `subtle`, `sha2`, AND `thiserror` to `auctioneer-core`'s
  /// `[dependencies]` (round-51 B5 — `HealthBootError` derives
  /// `thiserror::Error`, and `auctioneer-core` did not previously
  /// depend on `thiserror`; all three are wasm-compatible; `sha2`
  /// was previously only a build-dep for GVL pinning). Hashing
  /// both sides to a fixed 32 bytes before the constant-time
  /// compare removes length as a side channel.
  // Round-48 B3: the `Digest` trait must be in scope for
  // `Sha256::digest` (otherwise the method does not resolve).
  use sha2::{Digest as _, Sha256};

  pub struct BearerToken {
      digest: [u8; 32],
  }

  impl BearerToken {
      /// Round-50 H3: rejects an EMPTY token. An empty configured
      /// secret is a misconfiguration (a caller sending `Bearer `
      /// or an empty header would otherwise authenticate). The
      /// adapter maps `None` here to "no token configured".
      pub fn new(token: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Option<Self> {
          if token.as_ref().is_empty() {
              return None;
          }
          Some(Self { digest: Sha256::digest(token.as_ref()).into() })
      }
  }

  impl HealthAuth for BearerToken {
      fn verify(&self, presented: &str) -> bool {
          use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
          let presented_digest: [u8; 32] =
              Sha256::digest(presented.as_bytes()).into();
          presented_digest.ct_eq(&self.digest).into()
      }
      // Round-50 H4: the digest IS the stable identity.
      fn identity(&self) -> [u8; 32] { self.digest }
  }
  ```

  **Round-48 H1 — genuinely fail-closed, and the adapter MUST wire
  it.** There is no implicit "open" state: a NOT-installed policy
  returns 401 (`health_authorize` → `Deny`). Each adapter's boot
  passes `HealthAccessPolicy::Token(...)` when its host surface
  yields a token, or `HealthAccessPolicy::UnauthenticatedAcknowledged`
  **only** when the deploy config sets `allow_unauthenticated_health
= true` — an explicit, greppable, machine-checkable opt-in, not a
  silent default, and it still logs a `WARN health_gvl endpoint is
OPEN — relying on ingress restriction`. A deploy that provides no
  token and does NOT set the flag gets a closed (401) endpoint, so
  a forgotten token can never silently expose it. The per-adapter
  `install_health_primitives(...)` call is REQUIRED wiring (see the
  Files list).
  Per-adapter resolution — each reads its OWN config surface and
  declares its OWN scope. **Round-49 auction core: the Cloudflare secret name
  is `AUCTIONEER__RUNTIME__HEALTH_GVL_TOKEN`** — the single-underscore
  `AUCTIONEER_HEALTH_GVL_TOKEN` violated the plan's own `__`
  section-separation rule (Global Constraints). All four now use the
  same dotted-path spelling:

  | Adapter    | token source                                                | `allow_unauthenticated_health` source                                       | `counter_scope`                     |
  | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
  | Cloudflare | `env.secret("AUCTIONEER__RUNTIME__HEALTH_GVL_TOKEN")`           | `env.var("AUCTIONEER__RUNTIME__ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HEALTH")`                  | `"isolate"`                         |
  | Fastly     | `SecretStore::open("auctioneer")?.try_get("health_gvl_token")?` | `ConfigStore::try_open("auctioneer")?.try_get("allow_unauthenticated_health")?` | `"request"` (fresh-sandbox default) |
  | Spin       | `spin_sdk::variables::get("health_gvl_token")`              | `spin_sdk::variables::get("allow_unauthenticated_health")`                  | `"instance"`                        |
  | Axum       | `std::env::var("AUCTIONEER__RUNTIME__HEALTH_GVL_TOKEN")`        | `std::env::var("AUCTIONEER__RUNTIME__ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HEALTH")`            | `"process"`                         |

  **Round-50 H3 / round-51 H2 — the Fastly bearer is a SECRET, and
  EVERY Fastly call is the fallible variant.** Verified against
  fastly 0.12.1: `ConfigStore::open` and `Secret::plaintext` BOTH
  panic on failure, so the plan uses `ConfigStore::try_open(..)?`
  and `Secret::try_plaintext()?` (and `SecretStore::open` is already
  `Result`, `try_get` is the fallible lookup). A bearer token is a
  credential → `SecretStore` (encrypted at rest); the non-secret
  `allow_unauthenticated_health` flag stays in `ConfigStore`. Flow:

  ```rust
  let secret = SecretStore::open("auctioneer")?          // Result
      .try_get("health_gvl_token")?;                 // Result<Option<Secret>>
  let token_bytes = match secret {
      Some(s) => Some(s.try_plaintext()?),           // NOT .plaintext() (panics)
      None => None,
  };
  // token_bytes → BearerToken::new (returns None on empty — H3).
  ```

  A missing/broken store or a decrypt failure fails boot cleanly
  instead of panicking.

  **Round-50 B5 — the health policy is BOOT-scoped, resolved from
  adapter secrets, NOT from per-request `RuntimeConfig`.** The
  round-49 draft put `allow_unauthenticated_health` on
  `RuntimeConfig`, but that is loaded PER REQUEST
  ([auction.rs](../../../crates/auctioneer-core/src/handlers/auction.rs)),
  while `HEALTH_POLICY` is a process-global installed ONCE at
  adapter boot — the two lifecycles cannot meet. So BOTH inputs
  (the token and the unauthenticated opt-in) come from the
  adapter's boot surface in the table above, are read once before
  serving, and are frozen into the policy `OnceLock`. There is no
  `RuntimeConfig` field. Each adapter's boot code:

  ```rust
  // Runs ONCE at adapter boot, before the server accepts requests.
  // `read_bool_flag` parses "true"/"false" strictly and returns
  // `Err(HealthBootError::NonBooleanFlag { .. })` on anything else
  // (never a silent false). Absent → false.
  let allow_unauth = read_bool_flag(
      "ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HEALTH", raw_flag)?;      // Option<&str> → bool
  let token: Option<BearerToken> =
      resolved_token.and_then(BearerToken::new);       // empty secret → None (H3)

  match (token, allow_unauth) {
      // Conflicting intent — fail boot, don't guess.
      (Some(_), true) => return Err(HealthBootError::ConflictingPolicy),
      (Some(tok), false) =>
          install_health_primitives(
              HealthAccessPolicy::Token(Arc::new(tok)), counter_scope)?,
      (None, true) => {
          log::warn!(target: "auctioneer::health",
              "health_gvl endpoint is OPEN — relying on ingress restriction");
          install_health_primitives(
              HealthAccessPolicy::UnauthenticatedAcknowledged, counter_scope)?;
      }
      // No token, no opt-in → install NOTHING; `health_authorize`
      // fail-closes to 401 (attributable, not a hidden bad token).
      (None, false) => install_health_primitives_without_policy(counter_scope)?,
  }
  ```

  Regressions: `health_gvl_returns_401_when_token_set_and_missing()`
  and `allow_unauthenticated_health_true_installs_acknowledged()`.

- **Counter caveat** (round-43 H3). The rolling counter is
  process-local, and "process" means something different
  per platform — see the table above. Round-42 B12
  hardcoded `"isolate"` in the payload even though the
  plan's own text described Axum as process-scoped and
  Fastly as request-scoped; the adapter now declares the
  truth. Reads reflect only the isolate/sandbox/process
  that serviced the health check, NEVER deployment-wide
  state. On Fastly's default fresh-sandbox model the
  counter is effectively always near-zero, which is why
  the scope label matters. Deployers who need
  deployment-wide metrics aggregate via external
  observability (Cloudflare Analytics Engine, Fastly log
  tailing, Prometheus).
- `edgezero.toml` registration:
  ```toml
  [[triggers.http]]
  id      = "health_gvl"
  path    = "/internal/health/gvl"
  methods = ["GET"]
  handler = "crate::handlers::health_gvl"
  adapters = ["axum", "cloudflare", "fastly", "spin"]
  description = "GVL archive health (GDPR enforcement Task 4a; operator-only, restrict at ingress)"
  ```
- `body_caps.rs` RouteTable entry: `Route { id:
"health_gvl", method: Method::GET, path: "/internal/
health/gvl", cap_bytes: HEALTH_GVL_CAP_BYTES }` (4 KiB —
  no body).
- Spec §2.2 route table gains a row for the endpoint
  (see round-39 H3 spec-side follow-up below).

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `GET /internal/health/gvl` → 200 JSON (503
  when stale, round-40 H2). `counter_scope` is the
  ADAPTER's declared scope (round-43 H3), not a hardcoded
  `"isolate"`:
  ```json
  {
    "status": "ok",
    "generated_at": "2026-06-25T00:00:00Z",
    "age_days": 15,
    "max_age_days": 45,
    "spec3_versions": [341, 342, 343, 344, 345, 346, 347, 348],
    "spec2_versions": [79, 80, 81, 82],
    "unavailable_lookups_last_hour": 3,
    "counter_scope": "isolate"
  }
  ```
  **Execution amendment (post-review round 2): the shipped endpoint
  gates on BOTH clocks and carries three more fields.** The GCL's own
  RFC 9111 lifetime (~7 days) expires far inside the archive's
  `max_age_days` window, and runtime privacy resolution fails closed the
  moment it does — so archive age alone let an instance report `ok` for
  months while every enforced auction returned unusable-consent
  defaults. Shipped behavior: `status` is `"stale"` (and the response 503) when EITHER the archive age exceeds `max_age_days` OR
  `now >= gcl_expires_at`. Three response fields join the example
  above: `"gcl_expires_at"` (RFC 3339), `"gcl_expired"` (bool), and
  `"gcl_stale_lookups_last_hour"` — the `GclStale` (10019) rolling
  counter, deliberately separate from `unavailable_lookups_last_hour`
  (10018): stale-CMP-list and missing-vendor-list are different
  deployment faults with different fixes, and one number cannot tell
  them apart. Monitoring should page on `status != "ok"` and can use
  `gcl_expires_at` to pre-stage the weekly refresh.
  (`counter_scope` shown for a Cloudflare deploy; Fastly
  reports `"request"`, Spin `"instance"`, Axum
  `"process"`.)

  ```rust
  // crates/auctioneer-core/src/handlers/health_gvl.rs
  use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};
  use time::OffsetDateTime;

  pub struct GvlUnavailableCounter {
      // Ring of (unix_timestamp_seconds, count) per-minute
      // buckets covering the trailing 60 minutes. Mutex is
      // uncontended in practice; the counter is read at
      // request time (rare) and written at auction time
      // (frequent but bucketed).
      buckets: Mutex<[(i64, u32); 60]>,
  }

  // Round-48 B3: `new()` needs a matching `Default` impl or
  // `clippy::new_without_default` fires.
  impl Default for GvlUnavailableCounter {
      fn default() -> Self {
          Self::new()
      }
  }

  impl GvlUnavailableCounter {
      #[must_use]
      pub fn new() -> Self {
          Self { buckets: Mutex::new([(0, 0); 60]) }
      }

      pub fn record(&self, now: OffsetDateTime) {
          // Round-55 H2: `div_euclid` not `/` (avoids the
          // `integer_division` / `arithmetic_side_effects`
          // restriction lints) and pairs with the `rem_euclid`
          // below so the minute/bucket derivation is consistent for
          // pre-epoch timestamps.
          let minute = now.unix_timestamp().div_euclid(60);
          // Round-48 B3: `usize::try_from` not `as usize`
          // (`as_conversions` denied); `rem_euclid` keeps the index
          // in 0..60 even for a pre-epoch timestamp.
          let bucket = usize::try_from(minute.rem_euclid(60)).unwrap_or(0);
          // Round-48 B3: recover a poisoned guard instead of
          // `.expect(..)` (denied) — the bucket data is fine, only
          // the guard was contaminated by an unrelated test panic.
          let mut b = self.buckets.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
          // Round-55 H2: `.get_mut` not `b[bucket]` (avoids
          // `indexing_slicing`). bucket ∈ 0..60 == array len, so this
          // is always `Some`; the `if let` is fail-safe.
          if let Some((bucket_start, count)) = b.get_mut(bucket) {
              if *bucket_start != minute {
                  *bucket_start = minute;
                  *count = 0;
              }
              *count = count.saturating_add(1);
          }
      }

      #[must_use]
      pub fn count_last_hour(&self, now: OffsetDateTime) -> u32 {
          // Round-55 H2: `div_euclid` not `/` (restriction lints).
          let now_bucket = now.unix_timestamp().div_euclid(60);
          let b = self.buckets.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
          b.iter()
              // Round-41 H2 fix: earlier `now_bucket -
              // start < 60` accepted NEGATIVE deltas (i.e.
              // future-labelled buckets) because signed
              // negatives compare less than 60. Restrict
              // to the trailing hour with `0..60`.
              // Round-55 H2: `checked_sub` not `-` (avoids
              // `arithmetic_side_effects`); a wrapped/absent delta
              // is treated as out-of-window.
              .filter(|(start, _)| {
                  now_bucket
                      .checked_sub(*start)
                      .is_some_and(|delta| (0..60).contains(&delta))
              })
              .map(|(_, count)| *count)
              .fold(0_u32, |a, c| a.saturating_add(c))
      }
  }

  pub fn counter() -> &'static GvlUnavailableCounter {
      static C: OnceLock<GvlUnavailableCounter> = OnceLock::new();
      C.get_or_init(GvlUnavailableCounter::new)
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  use edgezero_core::action;
  use edgezero_core::body::Body;
  use edgezero_core::context::RequestContext;
  use edgezero_core::error::EdgeError;
  use edgezero_core::http::{Response, StatusCode, response_builder};
  use time::format_description::well_known::Rfc3339;
  use time::OffsetDateTime;

  #[action]
  pub async fn health_gvl(ctx: RequestContext) -> Result<Response, EdgeError> {
      // Round-49 B2: authorize through `health_authorize`, which
      // FAIL-CLOSES when no policy was installed. The round-48
      // revision replaced the API but left this body calling the
      // deleted `health_auth_handle()` inside `if let Some(..)` —
      // that both fails to compile AND, if "fixed" naively, would
      // reinstate the fail-open hole (no policy ⇒ served).
      // Round-43 H3: the token comes from the ADAPTER-installed
      // policy, never `std::env` (empty on Workers).
      // Round-52 foundations / round-93 auction core: the `Bearer` scheme name is
      // CASE-INSENSITIVE (RFC 9110 §11.1) and may be followed by more
      // than one SPACE. Match the scheme token case-insensitively and
      // trim leading SPACES off the credential rather than requiring
      // an exact `"Bearer "` prefix (which would wrongly reject
      // `bearer` and `BEARER`). A TAB after the scheme is NOT valid
      // RFC-9110 auth whitespace — only SP is. Round-93 auction core: that means
      // `trim_start_matches(' ')` (SP ONLY), NOT `trim_start()` —
      // `trim_start()` strips tabs and Unicode whitespace, so
      // `Bearer \t<tok>` (space, then tab) would have AUTHENTICATED
      // with the tab silently eaten. With SP-only trimming, a
      // credential that still begins with a tab/Unicode-space simply
      // fails the exact token comparison below → 401.
      let presented = ctx.request().headers()
          .get("authorization")
          .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
          .and_then(|v| {
              let (scheme, rest) = v.split_once(' ')?;
              scheme.eq_ignore_ascii_case("bearer")
                  .then(|| rest.trim_start_matches(' '))
          });
      if matches!(
          crate::host_primitives::health_authorize(presented),
          crate::host_primitives::HealthAuthz::Deny
      ) {
          // Covers all three deny paths: no policy installed
          // (fail-closed default), Token policy with a missing or
          // wrong bearer. Round-52 foundations: a 401 MUST carry a
          // `WWW-Authenticate` challenge (RFC 9110 §11.6.1).
          return response_builder()
              .status(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
              .header("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer")
              .body(Body::from_bytes(b"unauthorized".to_vec()))
              .map_err(EdgeError::internal);
      }
      let clock = crate::host_primitives::clock_handle();
      let now = clock.now();
      let generated_at_raw = auctioneer_config::gvl_archive_generated_at();
      let generated_dt = OffsetDateTime::parse(generated_at_raw, &Rfc3339)
          .map_err(|e| EdgeError::internal(anyhow::anyhow!(
              "manifest.generated_at parse: {e}"
          )))?;
      let age_days = ((now - generated_dt).whole_days()).max(0);
      let max_age_days = auctioneer_config::gvl_archive_max_age_days();
      let (mut s2, mut s3) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
      for entry in auctioneer_config::gvl_archive() {
          match entry.spec {
              2 => s2.push(entry.vendor_list_version),
              3 => s3.push(entry.vendor_list_version),
              _ => {}
          }
      }
      s2.sort_unstable();
      s3.sort_unstable();
      let unavailable = crate::handlers::health_gvl::counter().count_last_hour(now);
      // Round-48 B3: compare in i64 via `i64::from` — no `as u32`
      // (denied, and lossy on a negative/huge `age_days`).
      let status_flag = if age_days > i64::from(max_age_days) { "stale" } else { "ok" };
      let payload = serde_json::json!({
          "status": status_flag,
          // Round-43 H3: the ADAPTER declares its real
          // scope — round-42 B12 hardcoded "isolate" even
          // though the plan itself describes Axum as
          // process-scoped and Fastly as request-sandbox-
          // scoped. `counter_scope_handle()` returns the
          // adapter's installed &'static str:
          //   CF     → "isolate"
          //   Fastly → "request"   (fresh sandbox default)
          //   Spin   → "instance"
          //   Axum   → "process"
          "counter_scope": crate::host_primitives::counter_scope_handle(),
          "generated_at": generated_at_raw,
          "age_days": age_days,
          "max_age_days": max_age_days,
          "spec2_versions": s2,
          "spec3_versions": s3,
          "unavailable_lookups_last_hour": unavailable,
      });
      let status_code = if status_flag == "stale" {
          StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
      } else {
          StatusCode::OK
      };
      let body_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&payload)
          .map_err(|e| EdgeError::internal(anyhow::anyhow!("payload serialise: {e}")))?;
      response_builder()
          .status(status_code)
          .header("content-type", "application/json")
          .body(Body::from_bytes(body_bytes))
          .map_err(EdgeError::internal)
  }
  ```

  [lib.rs:13](../../../crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/lib.rs#L13) is

  symbols Task 13's NSP branch + Task 13 Step 0 reach for by
  re-exporting at the crate root (round-68 B3 — the export set MUST
  include `PrivacyError`, which Task 13's handler names in
  `HandlerError::from_privacy_error`):
  ```rust
  mod error;
  pub use error::PrivacyError;
  pub use signal::{resolve_wire_signal, validate_wire_signal_input, WireSignalInput};
  ```
  Task 13's snippets call them at the crate root
  (`auctioneer_privacy::resolve_wire_signal(...)`,
  `auctioneer_privacy::validate_wire_signal_input(...)`,
  `auctioneer_privacy::PrivacyError`), NOT through the private module path.

**Interfaces:**

**⚠ Round-44 B1 — the error type. `auctioneer-privacy` CANNOT
return `AuctionError`.** Every prior round wrote
`-> Result<_, AuctionError>` on privacy-crate functions, but
`AuctionError` lives in `auctioneer-exchange`, and
`auctioneer-exchange` ALREADY depends on `auctioneer-privacy`
([Cargo.toml:20](../../../crates/auctioneer-exchange/Cargo.toml#L20)).
Adding the reverse edge is a Cargo cycle — it would not
compile. Round-44 B1 introduces a privacy-owned error and
maps it at the boundary:

```rust
// crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/error.rs  (NEW, round-44 B1)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum PrivacyError {
    /// `regs.gdpr` carried a value other than 0 or 1
    /// (§7.1 rule 2). The ONLY fatal privacy input.
    #[error("regs.gdpr must be 0 or 1, got {got}")]
    InvalidRegsGdpr { got: i32 },
}
```

```rust
// crates/auctioneer-exchange/src/error.rs  (round-44 B1)
// Exchange depends on privacy, so the From impl lives
// HERE — the direction the graph already allows.
impl From<PrivacyError> for AuctionError {
    fn from(e: PrivacyError) -> Self {
        match e {
            PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr { .. } => {
                AuctionError::BadInput(e.to_string())
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Call sites (round-68 B3 — two DISTINCT boundaries):

- **Inside `run_auction`** (which returns `AuctionError`): the NSP
  branch's `resolve_wire_signal(...)?` uses this
  `From<PrivacyError> for AuctionError` impl automatically. The
  mapping is exhaustive today (one variant); adding a variant forces
  the match to be updated, which is the point.
- **In the auction handler** (`auction_inner`, which returns
  `HandlerError`, NOT `AuctionError`): the Step-0
  `validate_wire_signal_input(&normalized)` is mapped EXPLICITLY via
  `.map_err(HandlerError::from_privacy_error)?` (round-67 B1) — there
  is no `From<PrivacyError> for HandlerError`, so a bare `?` would not
  compile. This `From` impl does NOT cover the handler path.

`auctioneer-privacy` gains `thiserror = { workspace = true }` in
`[dependencies]` (already a workspace dep, used by auctioneer-exchange).

- Produces:
  - `pub enum Signal { Yes, No, Ambiguous }`
  - `pub struct WireSignalInput<'a> { pub regs_gdpr: Option<i32>, pub gpp_sid: Option<&'a [i32]> }`
    — narrow input covering only the wire-visible request fields.
    No geo, no host default. Renamed from the earlier `SignalInput`
    to prevent test call sites from accidentally locking in
    resolve_signal-as-decision semantics.
  - `pub fn resolve_wire_signal(input: &WireSignalInput<'_>) ->
Result<(Signal, Vec<NonFatalWarning>), PrivacyError>` —
    round-44 B1 corrects the error type (was `AuctionError`,
    a cycle). `Ok((Signal::Ambiguous, warnings))` when both
    fields absent is a legitimate terminal output.
    `Err(PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr { got })`
    short-circuits when `regs.gdpr` carries a value other
    than 0 or 1 (round-34 H4); the exchange boundary maps it
    to `AuctionError::BadInput` → HTTP 400. Task 8
    destructures the tuple inside the `Ok` arm and combines
    with `auction_geo_signal` to derive `enforcement_active`.
  - **`pub fn validate_wire_signal_input(req:
&NormalizedBidRequest) -> Result<(), PrivacyError>`** —
    round-45 B1 canonical (retires round-43 H1's
    `validate_regs_gdpr`, which checked `regs.gdpr ∈ {0,1}`
    UNCONDITIONALLY and so rejected `{gpp_sid:[2],
gdpr:2}` at HTTP even though §7.1 rule 1 says a
    non-empty `gpp_sid` overrides `regs.gdpr` ENTIRELY —
    the invalid `regs.gdpr` is never consulted, so it must
    not 400). **Precedence-aware by construction**: it is
    a thin wrapper that calls the SAME `resolve_wire_signal`
    the resolver uses, discarding the `Ok` value and
    surfacing only the `Err`. One function, one precedence,
    both paths:
    ```rust
    // crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/signal.rs
    pub fn validate_wire_signal_input(
        req: &NormalizedBidRequest,
    ) -> Result<(), PrivacyError> {
        // Build the same narrow input the resolver takes,
        // then run it purely for its Err side-effect.
        // Because resolve_wire_signal checks gpp_sid FIRST
        // (§7.1 rule 1), an invalid regs.gdpr with a
        // non-empty gpp_sid yields Ok here — exactly as it
        // does in the resolver.
        let input = WireSignalInput {
            regs_gdpr: req.regs.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.gdpr),
            gpp_sid:   req.regs.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.gpp_sid.as_deref()),
        };
        resolve_wire_signal(&input).map(|_| ())
    }
    ```
    `resolve_wire_signal` itself (Step 1 below) is where the
    `Err(PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr { got })` decision
    lives, gated on gpp_sid absence. The handler's `?`
    converts to `AuctionError::BadInput` → 400 via the
    round-44 B1 `From` impl on the exchange side.
    **Still does NOT inspect** `regs.gpp` or `user.consent`
    as fatal input — malformed TCF/GPP is §7.7
    warn-and-continue (code 10001 + permissive/denial),
    never a 400. Running it early makes the ordering
    guarantee explicit; the resolver runs it again inside
    `resolve` so direct callers (tests, trusted-server)
    stay correct.
  - Round-45 B1 test:
    `wire_signal_input_gpp_sid_overrides_invalid_gdpr()`
    — `{gpp_sid:[2], regs.gdpr:2}` returns `Ok(())` from
    both `validate_wire_signal_input` AND
    `resolve_wire_signal`, and drives the handler to a
    normal auction (NOT 400). The companion
    `invalid_gdpr_without_gpp_sid_returns_400()` keeps the
    §7.1-rule-2 path.
  - **Round-86 B1 — the input MUST carry geo-OBJECT presence, not just
    the country string.** A bare `Option<&str> country` collapses two
    cases the algorithm must distinguish: (i) the `user.geo` object is
    ABSENT, versus (ii) the object is PRESENT but its `country` is
    absent/malformed. Per pinned upstream the whole `Geo` handle being
    non-null is what makes user-geo "selected" and blocks the device-geo
    fallback (see Step 2), so the two cases resolve differently
    (device-geo may decide vs. host default decides) and can flip GDPR
    enforcement. Model presence with the OUTER `Option`:
    ```rust
    pub struct GeoView<'a> { pub country: Option<&'a str> }
    pub struct AuctionGeoInput<'a> {
        /// `None` = the `user.geo` OBJECT is absent; `Some(view)` = the
        /// object is present (its `country` may still be `None`/malformed).
        pub user_geo: Option<GeoView<'a>>,
        /// `None` = the `device.geo` OBJECT is absent.
        pub device_geo: Option<GeoView<'a>>,
        pub host_default_value: &'a str,
        pub eea_countries: &'a [&'a str],
    }
    ```

  1. **Conflict detection first (warn only, semantics unchanged).**
     If `regs.gdpr.is_some() && gpp_sid.is_some()` — regardless of
     whether the `gpp_sid` slice is empty or non-empty — emit a
     `InvalidPrivacyConsent` warning ("regs.gdpr set together with
     regs.gpp_sid; gpp_sid presence disambiguates when non-empty,
     else regs.gdpr wins") via `warnings::regs_gpp_conflict()`.
     Then continue with the rules below. The warning is diagnostic;
     it does NOT change the resolution order.
     **Round-58 GDPR enforcement — do NOT conflate this with the invalid-VALUE
     case.** This CONFLICT warning uses `InvalidPrivacyConsent` (code 10001) per spec §7.1 line 2725 and fires when BOTH fields are
     present (any `regs.gdpr` value, including a legal 0/1). It is
     entirely separate from an invalid `regs.gdpr` _value_ (∉ {0,1})
     WITH empty/absent `gpp_sid`, which is a HARD
     `Err(PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr)` → 400 and emits NO warning.
     (A `regs.gdpr = 2` alongside a non-empty `gpp_sid` is NOT an
     error — `gpp_sid` wins, and only this conflict warning fires.)
  2. `gpp_sid` present AND non-empty: `Yes` when section 2 (TCFEU2)
     is in the slice, else `No`. **GPP SID overrides `regs.gdpr`
     entirely only when non-empty**, per spec Section 7.1 line
     2269 (present-empty is warning-only; regs.gdpr still wins).
  3. Else `regs.gdpr` is `Some(0)`: `No`.
  4. Else `regs.gdpr` is `Some(1)`: `Yes`.
  5. Else `regs.gdpr` is `Some(other)`: **round-45 H1 —
     return `Err(PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr { got })`.**
     Reached ONLY when gpp_sid is absent/empty (rule 2 above
     consumed the non-empty-gpp_sid case first, so an invalid
     regs.gdpr under a non-empty gpp_sid never reaches here —
     that is the §7.1-rule-1 override, round-45 B1). The
     exchange boundary maps the error to
     `AuctionError::BadInput` → 400. **Round-74 L1 — the COMPLETE 400
     wire body, exact bytes:** `Invalid request: regs.gdpr must be 0 or
1, got {got}\n`. It is built as the executable `PrivacyError`
     Display (`#[error("regs.gdpr must be 0 or 1, got {got}")]` above —
     COMMA form) wrapped by BOTH mapping paths with the same
     `"Invalid request: "` prefix (`from_privacy_error` on the handler
     Step-0 path, auction.rs:118; `from_auction_error` on the
     run_auction NSP path, auction.rs:154) and the trailing `\n` that
     `HandlerError::BadRequest::into_parts` appends — so both paths
     produce identical bytes. Never emits a warning. Test:
     `regs_gdpr_out_of_range_without_gpp_sid` asserts that exact byte
     sequence (prefix + comma-form message + newline), not just the
     inner `PrivacyError` string.
  6. Else (both absent): `Ambiguous` per spec Section 7.1 line 2202. **Do NOT apply the geo-aware default here.** The
     geo-aware default is `auction_geo_signal` (Task 8) and lives
     alongside `resolve_wire_signal`, not inside it.

### Task 6: Per-purpose enforcement matrix + Appendix A.2 / A.3 legal-basis

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/purposes.rs`
- Modify: `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/auction_context.rs` (Step 0 lands
  the GDPR enforcement `PrivacyContext` struct skeleton — see below)
- Modify: `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/lib.rs`

**Interfaces:**

**Round-21 → Round-22 rework: single decision context.** Earlier
drafts defined a separate `PurposeContext<'a>` here alongside
Task 8's `PrivacyContext`. That created a compile-break (Task 9
passes `&PrivacyContext` into functions the previous draft typed
as `&PurposeContext`) and forced the decision functions to
duplicate state Task 8 already caches. **There is ONE decision
context**: the `PrivacyContext`. Every function below takes
`&PrivacyContext`; Task 6 owns the decision algorithms, Task 8
owns the `resolve()` population logic.

**Round-57 B-g — break the Task 6↔8 cycle: land the struct skeleton
in Task 6 Step 0, not Task 8.** Task 6's functions read
`&PrivacyContext` FIELDS, so the struct must exist before Task 6
compiles — but the full definition previously lived in Task 8 Step
4 (which runs _after_ Task 6). Resolution: **Task 6 Step 0** REPLACES the auction core stub in
[`auction_context.rs:24`](../../../crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/auction_context.rs#L24)
with the GDPR enforcement struct + a test builder. Concretely, Step 0 must
(round-58 B1 — the auction core stub is not merely "extended"):

- **Drop `#[derive(Debug, Default)]` → `#[derive(Debug)]`.** The
  struct now owns a `gvl: Gvl` field, which has no `Default`, so a
  derived `Default` no longer compiles — and a defaultable
  "permissive empty" `PrivacyContext` is exactly the fail-OPEN shape
  GDPR enforcement must not have.
- **KEEP `pub fn allow_all_no_scrub() -> Self` — reimplement its
  body, do NOT delete it (round-59 C2 — the round-58 "delete it"
  instruction was wrong).** It is NOT single-call-site: production
  calls it at
  [run.rs:56](../../../crates/auctioneer-exchange/src/run.rs#L56) AND
  the integration tests in
  [`tests/stub_invariants.rs`](../../../crates/auctioneer-privacy/tests/stub_invariants.rs)
  call it — and integration tests compile the library **without
  `--cfg test`**, so a `#[cfg(test)]`-only replacement would NOT be
  visible to them and would break the normal library build. Instead:
  keep the constructor **public and always-compiled**, and change
  its body from `Self {}` to build the COMPLETE **permissive** GDPR enforcement
  context — every field initialised to the "GDPR does not apply"
  shape so `permissions(..)` grants everything (`AllowAll`) and
  `take_warnings` is empty, exactly matching the auction core stub's observable
  behaviour. The **production** use at `run.rs:56` is replaced by
  `PrivacyContext::resolve(...)` in **Task 13** (which OWNS `run.rs`
  — Task 8 does not); the tests keep calling `allow_all_no_scrub`.
- **`permissions_for` / `activity_allow` / `ccpa_should_enforce` /
  `apply_scrub` auction core stubs:** `permissions_for` is superseded by Task
  9's real `permissions(core, bidder)`; `activity_allow` /
  `ccpa_should_enforce` / `apply_scrub` keep their auction core
  `&self`-ignore-fields bodies (their real impls are privacy enforcement) — they
  still compile with the new fields present.
- **Add the `#[cfg(test)] fn for_test(...)`** field builder so Task
  6/7 unit tests construct a context directly (no dependency on
  Task 8's `resolve`).
- **Field visibility — declare every GDPR enforcement field `pub(crate)` (round-77
  B1).** `PrivacyContext` lives in `auction_context.rs`, but the
  decision algorithms that read its fields live in the sibling module
  `purposes.rs` (Task 6) and the constructor that writes them lives in
  the sibling module `resolve.rs` (Task 8). Rust field privacy is
  _module_-scoped, so plain-private fields are unreachable from
  siblings and Tasks 6/8 would not compile. Fields are therefore
  `pub(crate)` — readable/writable within `auctioneer-privacy` (the
  decision fns, the resolver, and the crate's own unit tests that
  inspect `consent_usable`), and invisible outside the crate (
  `auctioneer-exchange` only ever sees `permissions()` / `resolve()` /
  `take_warnings()`, never a raw field). The `for_test` builder and
  crate tests set/read `consent_usable` directly through this
  crate-visibility. The fail-closed invariant is preserved because no
  code _outside_ `auctioneer-privacy` can flip `consent_usable`, and the
  only in-crate writer is `resolve()` (the `#[cfg(test)]` builder is
  test-only).
  Task 8 Step 4 then implements ONLY `resolve()` + the
  field-population against this already-defined struct — it does not
  re-declare it. Task 7's `warnings` field is part of the same
  skeleton.

      `declares_purpose_for_consent` / `_for_li` call), but it **does**
      consult the TCF `VendorConsent` bit in the final A.3 row per
      spec line 5047 — that's why the signature takes `vendor_id: u16`
      alongside the flag pair. `flags` carries the same `EnforceFlags`
      shape as full enforcement. **A.3 rows** (spec lines 5034–5047):

  Row order below is the exact spec Appendix A.3 order (lines
  5034-5047) — do not reorder. First match wins.

  1. **Everything unenforced** (spec row 1): if
     `!flags.enforce_purpose && !flags.enforce_vendors → true`.
  2. **`vendor_exceptions`** (spec row 2): if `core_name` (CORE
     bidder only — the alias name is NEVER consulted per round-87 B3)
     appears in the purpose's `vendor_exceptions` list → `true`.
  3. **Basic-enforcement vendor — purpose unenforced** (spec row
     3): if `!flags.enforce_purpose && core_name ∈
basic_enforcement_vendors → true` (CORE bidder only — round-87 B3).
     Reaching this row means
     row 1 did not match (i.e. `flags.enforce_vendors == true`) —
     a basic bidder bypasses vendor consent when the purpose
     itself is not enforced.
  4. **Basic-enforcement vendor — purpose enforced and permitted**
     (spec row 4): if `flags.enforce_purpose &&
tcf.purposes_consent.contains(&purpose_id) && core_name ∈
basic_enforcement_vendors → true` (CORE bidder only — round-87 B3).
     Basic bidders skip the
     vendor-consent bit lookup when the purpose bit is set.
  5. **LI transparency via the `allow_li_transparency` invocation
     override** (spec row 5): if `flags.enforce_purpose &&
tcf.purposes_li_transparency.contains(&purpose_id) &&
allow_li_transparency` → `true`, where `allow_li_transparency`
     is the `bool` PARAMETER passed into this call — never config.
     Per spec Appendix A.3 line 5933 this is an "allowLITransparency
     override", and upstream enables it ONLY on the basic Purpose-2 path.
     Callers pass `allow_li_transparency = (purpose_id == 2)`: the
     auction `AllowBidRequest` P2 call passes `true`, the PassID walk
     over `p ∈ 2..=10` passes `p == 2`. **Round-87 B2 fix:** P3–P10 can
     NEVER be satisfied by LI transparency under basic enforcement, so an
     LI-transparency bit can no longer grant `PassID` for purposes 3–10
     without vendor consent. There is no per-purpose config field and no
     host/account fallthrough to resolve — the earlier account-only
     `allow_li_transparency` model diverged from spec §7.3 (which lists
     only `enforce_algo` / `enforce_purpose` / `enforce_vendors` /
     `vendor_exceptions`) and spec A.3 (which names it an override).
  6. **Purpose enforced but not permitted** (spec row 6): if
     `flags.enforce_purpose &&
!tcf.purposes_consent.contains(&purpose_id) → false`.
  7. **Vendor enforcement disabled** (spec row 7): if
     `!flags.enforce_vendors → true`. Reached only when
     `flags.enforce_purpose == true` AND the purpose consent bit IS
     present (row 6 wouldn't have matched) AND the bidder is NOT in
     `basic_enforcement_vendors` (rows 3-4 wouldn't have matched).
  8. **Default vendor consent** (spec row 8): if
     `tcf.vendor_consent.contains(&vendor_id_or_zero) → true`.
     Basic enforcement DOES consult vendor consent as the last row
     (spec Appendix A.3 line 5065); it just never consults the GVL
     declaration set. `vendor_id_or_zero` is 0 when the bidder has
     no configured GVL id — the vendor-consent bit is looked up
     against 0, which is always absent, so this row returns `false`
     for no-GVL-id bidders. That matches upstream's basic behavior.
  9. If no row matched, return `false`.

  **Signature guard (round-87 B2)**: this task fails to compile until
  Task 2 has REMOVED `allow_li_transparency` from `PurposeEnforcement` —
  row 5 now reads the `allow_li_transparency: bool` parameter, not a
  struct field. Task 9's two call sites (Step 2) must pass the P2-only
  override (`true` for the AllowBidRequest P2 call, `p == 2` in the
  PassID walk).

**Task 6 execution notes (implementation, post-GO):** landed as
`794a894`; gates green (514 passed / 1 ignored, 515 insecure — the
named roster and the metrics row AGREE at 33 for the first time in
this plan; an exact-name diff of rostered vs. executed confirmed
it). Reconciliations:

1. **`PrivacyContext.tcf` MUST be `Option<Box<TcfString>>`, not
   by-value.** `TcfString` embeds two fixed 8 KiB `VendorBitSet`s,
   so the by-value field made the context ~16.5 KB, and
   `run_auction` holds one across await points — pushing seven
   auctioneer-exchange/auctioneer-core futures past `clippy::large_futures`
   (21,248–29,952 B vs. the 16,384 threshold). Verified by `git
stash` that the lint does NOT fire on the baseline, so it was
   introduced here. Fixed at the root (boxing the field, inside
   Task 6's own Files list) rather than `Box::pin`-ing seven call
   sites in other crates or relaxing `clippy.toml`. **Tasks 8/9 must
   write `Some(Box::new(parsed))` and read via `as_deref()`.**
   Residual: any future by-value `TcfString` held across an await
   re-triggers this; the durable fix is boxing the bitsets inside
   `TcfString` (Task 3's file).
2. **`pub mod purposes;` with `pub fn` items** (user-directed
   override of the Interfaces block's `pub(crate) fn`): the private
   module + `pub(crate)` items forced a
   `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, ...))]` on the module,
   because the restriction wall denies `allow_attributes` and a bare
   `#[expect]` would be unfulfilled in test builds. Public items are
   never dead code, so the attribute disappears in BOTH
   configurations; matches the sibling `pub mod tcf/gvl/gcl`. Only
   fallout was `must_use_candidate` (`#[must_use]` added).
3. **The fixture `core_vendor_li_bit_unset.txt` never existed** —
   its name appears exactly once in the whole plan (Task 6) and Task
   3 never created it. Generated via Task 3's encoder through a
   throwaway test and committed as a fifth file beyond the Files
   list. It carries SEMANTIC assertions rather than Task 3's
   byte-equality anti-drift check (the encoder is `#[path]`-included
   privately by `tcf.rs`; a second instance in `purposes.rs` would
   be mostly-unused code).
4. **Task 7 Step 1 becomes a verification no-op** — it claims "the
   drain method is in place"; it was not. `take_warnings` now really
   drains via `mem::take`.
5. `allow_all_no_scrub` sets `consent_usable = true`, which reads
   oddly against that field's doc, but Task 9 Step 2 short-circuits
   to `{PassID: false}` when the flag is false while Step 3 requires
   this constructor to yield `AllowAll` — `false` would put
   out-of-scope traffic on the fail-closed row. **Tasks 8/9 must not
   "correct" it**; the constructor carries a comment saying so.
6. Six fields have no reader until Task 9 and carry
   `#[expect(dead_code, ...)]`; each becomes a HARD BUILD ERROR the
   moment its reader lands, so **Task 9 must delete them as it wires
   each field**.
7. `field_scoped_visibility_modifiers` (restriction, denied) fires
   on all eleven `pub(crate)` fields mandated by round-77 B1;
   resolved with a struct-scoped `#[expect(..., reason = ...)]`
   rather than editing workspace lint policy (Cargo.toml is not in
   the Files list) or writing eleven getter pairs.
8. `for_test`'s signature was unspecified; an eleven-arg version
   trips `too_many_arguments`, so it takes the four fields the plan
   names as "the fields the Task 6 functions read" over the
   permissive base. A.2's `vendor_id == 0` guard is hoisted above
   rows 4–6 (outcome-identical; matches the spec's blanket "vendor
   id 0 / absent → both fail").

### Task 7: Warnings buffer

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/warnings.rs`
- Modify: `crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/lib.rs`

**Interfaces:**

- **Warnings use `NonFatalWarning`, the existing shared type.**
  `auctioneer_openrtb::NonFatalWarning` is already defined at
  [normalized.rs:45](../../../crates/auctioneer-openrtb/src/normalized.rs#L45)
  and re-exported by `auctioneer-privacy` (via
  [lib.rs:19](../../../crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/lib.rs#L19)).
  `PrivacyContext::take_warnings` already returns
  `Vec<NonFatalWarning>` at
  [auction_context.rs:64](../../../crates/auctioneer-privacy/src/auction_context.rs#L64).
  Do NOT create a new `TcfSyntaxWarning` type — the auction core stub already
  returns the shared type; GDPR enforcement just populates the buffer with real
  entries.
- `NonFatalWarning` carries `scope: Option<String>` alongside `code`
  and `message` per spec Section 7.6 line 2445. TCF-syntax warnings
  populate `scope: Some("user.consent".into())`; GDPR signal
  conflicts populate `scope: Some("regs.gpp_sid".into())` or
  `scope: Some("regs".into())` per spec Section 7.6 line 2463.
- Produces: a `warnings.rs` module that centralises the constructor
  functions (`fn malformed_tcf(err: &str) -> NonFatalWarning`,
  `fn regs_gpp_conflict() -> NonFatalWarning`) so scope + code +
  message live in one place. **Round-47 H1: do NOT ship a
  `regs_gdpr_ambiguous(raw: i32)` constructor.** An invalid
  `regs.gdpr` value (with empty `gpp_sid`) is now a HARD ERROR —
  `PrivacyError::InvalidRegsGdpr` → `AuctionError::BadInput` → 400
  (spec §7.1, round-46 foundations) — NOT a non-fatal warning; the Task 5
  tests that asserted the warning path are already removed (Step 5
  below). A legitimately-absent `regs.gdpr` yields `Signal::Ambiguous`
  with no warning. **Do NOT ship a `missing_consent()`
  constructor.** Spec Section 7.2 line 2302 says empty consent
  under an enforced GDPR path becomes `default_permissions()` (the
  enforced-but-empty branch from Task 9); it is NOT a request
  error and does NOT emit a warning. Only _malformed_ consent
  strings surface a warning (spec Section 7.6 line 2454). If
  future spec revisions add a missing-consent warning code, add
  the constructor then.

NonFatalWarning>` and NOT a new type.

     was a GDPR-BYPASS: an `app` request could set
     `ext.prebid.channel.name = "web"` and select a `channel_enabled.web
= disabled` path to dodge `app` enforcement). upstream derives this
     policy key from its trusted request TYPE, not the request body's
     channel extension.**
     - **Inventory-shape derivation** (the ONLY source on the
       `/openrtb2/auction` route): `req.dooh` present → `Dooh`; else
       `req.app` present → `App`; else → `Web` (`req.site`-or-neither).
       `Channel = { Web, App, Dooh }` for GDPR fanout — these three are the only
       channels reachable on the auction route, so there is no "unknown"
       branch (which the round-86 five-variant enum could not represent
       anyway).
     - **`amp` / `video` are ROUTE-derived, NOT request-derived.** They
       are selected by dedicated endpoints (`/openrtb2/amp`,
       `/openrtb2/video`) that do NOT exist in GDPR fanout, so they are
       unreachable here; when those routes land (user sync) the handler for
       that route sets the channel from the route, never from
       `ext.prebid.channel.name`. The `account.gdpr.channel_enabled`
       map still carries `amp`/`video` keys for that future use.
     - **Conflicting inventory** (more than one of `site`/`app`/`dooh`):
       cannot reach here — OpenRTB + `prepare()` validation rejects a
       request carrying more than one distribution channel object with a
       400 before `resolve` runs (spec §3.2). Defensively the derivation
       above still resolves deterministically (`dooh` > `app` > `web`),
       but that arm is unreachable in a validated request.

     Then resolve the tri-state ladder for the classified channel:
     `account.gdpr.channel_enabled.<channel>` (tri-state) →
     `account.gdpr.enabled` (tri-state) → `host.gdpr.tcf2.enabled`
     (bool). The account-level `enabled` MUST be checked BEFORE
     falling through to the host default, per spec Section 7.1 line 2277.

  5. **`enforcement_active` per spec Section 7.1 line 2214 +
     Appendix E line 5009:**
     - `wire_signal == Signal::Yes` + `channel_enabled` → enforce.
     - `wire_signal == Signal::No` → do NOT enforce.
     - `wire_signal == Signal::Ambiguous` + `channel_enabled` +
       `geo_signal == Signal::Yes` → enforce. Ambiguous alone is NOT
       a green light; a request whose wire is ambiguous but whose
       geo says No must NOT enforce, per Appendix E line 5009. The
       `InvalidPrivacyConsent` warning was already emitted by
       `resolve_wire_signal` (step 1 above — round-83 L1, wire signal is
       step 1 after the round-82 renumber).
  6. **Permissive early return.** Only when `enforcement_active == false`
     does the resolver return the auction core-permissive purpose table.
