  ```rust
  // iteration in Task 8 and the overlay doc comments); special
  // features are the 12-slot wire bitfield (spec §GVL: SF ids 1..=12).
  // Key 0 is never valid. **These MUST match the build-time constants
  // in `build_codegen.rs` (round-55 foundations build path).**
  const PURPOSE_ID_RANGE: core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> = 1..=10;
  const SPECIAL_FEATURE_ID_RANGE: core::ops::RangeInclusive<u8> = 1..=12;

  // Generic over the map VALUE type so the one function serves both
  // the host (`HostPurposeEnforcementOverride`) and account
  // (`PurposeEnforcementOverride`) maps — the KEYS are `u8` in both.
  fn validate_purpose_id_keys<V>(
      m: &std::collections::BTreeMap<u8, V>,
  ) -> Result<(), validator::ValidationError> {
      if m.keys().any(|id| !PURPOSE_ID_RANGE.contains(id)) {
          return Err(validator::ValidationError::new("purpose_id_out_of_range"));
      }
      Ok(())
  }
  fn validate_special_feature_id_keys<V>(
      m: &std::collections::BTreeMap<u8, V>,
  ) -> Result<(), validator::ValidationError> {
      if m.keys().any(|id| !SPECIAL_FEATURE_ID_RANGE.contains(id)) {
          return Err(validator::ValidationError::new("special_feature_id_out_of_range"));
      }
      Ok(())
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, Validate)]
  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
  pub struct HostTcf2Override {
      #[serde(default)]
      pub enabled: Option<bool>,
      /// Per-purpose enforcement overrides. **Round-87 B2 — host and
      /// account per-purpose overrides are now FIELD-IDENTICAL** (the
      /// round-24 H3 split existed ONLY to keep `allow_li_transparency`
      /// off the host side; that field is removed, so
      /// `HostPurposeEnforcementOverride` and the account
      /// `PurposeEnforcementOverride` now have the same four fields).
      /// The distinct host type is retained for structural stability;
      /// it may be collapsed to the shared type in a later cleanup.
      // Round-55 foundations: reject out-of-range enforcement-map keys. The
      // `validator` crate does not inspect BTreeMap keys, so a custom
      // validator does it (skipped when the field is `None`).
      #[serde(default)]
      #[validate(custom(function = "validate_purpose_id_keys"))]
      pub purposes: Option<BTreeMap<u8, HostPurposeEnforcementOverride>>,
      #[serde(default)]
      #[validate(custom(function = "validate_special_feature_id_keys"))]
      pub special_features: Option<BTreeMap<u8, SpecialFeatureEnforcementOverride>>,
  }

      #[serde(default)]

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, Validate)]
  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
  pub struct AccountOverride {
      // -- Base AccountConfig fields (mirror the shape at

      #[serde(default)]
      pub disabled: Option<bool>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub debug_allow: Option<bool>,
      #[serde(default)]
      #[validate(length(min = 1_u64, max = 32_u64))]

      #[serde(default)]
      #[validate(length(min = 1_u64, max = 8_u64))]

      #[serde(default)]

      /// without disturbing the other; `merge` applies present
      /// values over the baked `AccountPrivacyConfig`.
      #[serde(default)]
      #[validate(nested)]
      pub privacy: Option<AccountPrivacyOverride>,

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, Validate)]

  pub struct AccountGdprOverride {
      /// `TriState::Unset` / `Enabled` / `Disabled` — the account-side
      /// master switch. `Unset` falls through to `host.tcf2.enabled`.
      #[serde(default)]

      /// Per-channel enablement fallback (see Task 5 Step 4). `Unset`

      /// Per-purpose enforcement overrides. Keys 1..=10. Absent

      /// runtime per §9:3889)"; `Some(empty map)` = "declared, but
      /// no purposes overridden — same effective behaviour"; a

      /// `PurposeEnforcementOverride` onto the baked account entry

      #[serde(default)]

      #[serde(default)]

  }

  /// `Option<Vec<String>>` because a whole-list replace matches
  /// RFC 7396's whole-array semantics; there is no per-entry
  /// exception merge in GDPR enforcement. **Runtime host fall-through happens

  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]

      #[serde(default)]

      #[serde(default)]

      #[serde(default)]
      pub enforce_vendors: Option<TriState>,
      // round-87 B2: no `allow_li_transparency` field.
      #[serde(default)]
      pub vendor_exceptions: Option<Vec<String>>,
  }

  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
  pub struct SpecialFeatureEnforcementOverride {
      #[serde(default)]
      pub enforce: Option<TriState>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub vendor_exceptions: Option<Vec<String>>,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, Validate)]
  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
  pub struct ChannelEnabledOverride {
      #[serde(default)]
      pub web: Option<TriState>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub app: Option<TriState>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub video: Option<TriState>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub amp: Option<TriState>,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub dooh: Option<TriState>,
  }
  ```

  **Overlay semantics — two-step, boot-time overlay + runtime
  merge.** The plan uses different shapes at the two layers, and
  they never mix:

  **Boot-time (Task 15 Step 3):** overlay
  `AccountOverride.gdpr.purposes: Option<BTreeMap<u8,
PurposeEnforcementOverride>>` onto the baked
  `AccountConfig.gdpr.purposes: BTreeMap<u8, PurposeEnforcement>`
  (concrete, per Task 2). For each entry key in the override
  map, materialise a `PurposeEnforcement` by starting from the
  baked account entry (or `PurposeEnforcement::default()` if
  absent) and applying each `Some` field on the override to the
  corresponding field: tri-state fields become
  `Enabled`/`Disabled`; other fields (`enforce_algo`,
  `vendor_exceptions`) are set to the override value. Fields the
  override left as `None` retain the baked value; **crucially,
  `TriState::Unset` on a resolved account entry is legal and
  meaningful** — it signals to the runtime merge that the account
  has NO opinion for that field on this purpose, and the runtime
  should fall back to host.

  **Runtime (Task 8 Step 3):** the effective `PurposeEnforcement`
  for a purpose id is computed per §9:3889's cross-layer rule.
  ONLY `enforce_purpose` and `enforce_vendors` fall back to host
  when the account value is `TriState::Unset` (those are the two
  tri-state fields on §9:3889's exhaustive list). `enforce_algo`
  and `vendor_exceptions` are account-only. (Round-87 B2:
  `allow_li_transparency` is no longer a config field at all — it is a
  per-call A.3 row-5 override, so it does not participate in this
  overlay.) See Task 8 Step 3's `effective_purpose(host, acct)`
  pseudocode.

  This shape means a partial `[accounts.<id>.gdpr.purposes.3]`
  TOML block — say, `enforce_purpose = "disabled"` alone —
  produces an account `PurposeEnforcement` with
  `enforce_purpose = Disabled`, `enforce_vendors = Unset`,
  plus whatever `enforce_algo` / `vendor_exceptions` the baked account
  default carries (usually `Full` / empty). At runtime, purpose 3
  resolves: `enforce_purpose = Disabled` (account wins over host),
  `enforce_vendors = host.enforce_vendors` (Unset falls through).

  **Privacy (IP-anon) overlay merge (round-50 H1).** The same
  boot-time overlay handles `AccountOverride.privacy`. For each of
  `ipv4` / `ipv6`, if the override carries `Some(anon_keep_bits)`
  it replaces the baked `AccountPrivacyConfig` value for that
  family; `None` (family absent, or `anon_keep_bits` absent within
  it) retains the baked default (24 / 56). There is no runtime
  host fall-through for IP-anon (it is account-scoped, like
  `vendor_exceptions`), so `AccountConfig.privacy` is fully
  resolved at boot and `ip_keep_bits()` reads it directly. A
  regression `account_privacy_overlay_sets_ipv4_only()` asserts a
  `[accounts.acme.privacy.ipv4] anon_keep_bits = 16` block yields
  `v4 = 16, v6 = 56` (baked) — and is ACCEPTED, not rejected by
  `deny_unknown_fields`.

  `PurposeEnforcement`, `SpecialFeatureEnforcement`, and `TriState`
  are the concrete types Task 2 introduces at
  `crates/auctioneer-config/src/types.rs`.
  `PurposeEnforcementOverride` / `SpecialFeatureEnforcementOverride`
  are the boot-time overlay shapes defined above; the
  `AccountConfig` handed to `run_auction` never carries them.
  Add `validate_account_map` alongside `validate_bidder_map` at
  [config.rs:63](../../../crates/auctioneer-core/src/config.rs#L63)
  using the same recursion pattern. Round-55 foundations: that pattern calls
  `value.validate()` on each `AccountOverride`, so the nested
  `gdpr.tcf2`/`gdpr` key-range custom validators
  (`validate_purpose_id_keys` / `validate_special_feature_id_keys`)
  fire per account — an out-of-range account enforcement key fails
  `AuctioneerAppConfig::validate()`.

  1. `/app/publisher/ext/prebid/parentAccount`
  2. `/app/publisher/id`
  3. `/site/publisher/ext/prebid/parentAccount`

     `ResolvedAccountOwned { id: "unknown", source: AccountSource::
DefaultFallback, config: default.clone() }` per spec Section 9's

- [ ] **Step 3: Three-layer account overlay** (round-19 foundations fix
      — earlier draft skipped the existing deployment-wide overlay
      that `resolved_account(&app, &baked)` at
      [resolve.rs:51](../../../crates/auctioneer-core/src/config/resolve.rs#L51)
      already applies from `[targeting]`, `[features]`, etc.). Correct
      order:

  1. Start with the baked `AccountConfig` default.
  2. Apply the **deployment-wide overlay** — the existing
     `resolved_account(&app, &baked)` call. This folds in
     `AuctioneerAppConfig.targeting` / `.features` / etc., which
     already applies to every account before per-account
     overrides.
  3. Look up `app.accounts.get(&id)`. If absent → return the
     step-2 result with `source: AccountSource::DefaultFallback`.
     If present, apply the `AccountOverride` on top of the step-2
     result per the same `Option::override_field` pattern
     `resolved_account` uses: every present field on
     `AccountOverride` writes onto the corresponding
     `AccountConfig` field; absent fields leave the deployment-
     wide value in place. Nested `gdpr` maps merge on top of the
     baked account gdpr map (per-purpose entries override
     individually; absent entries pass through).
  4. Return `source: AccountSource::Configured`.

  Overlay failures are compile-time impossible (both sides are
  typed structs); no `MalformedAcct` from this step. (The taxonomy

- [ ] **Step 3b: `resolve_host` body — host `[gdpr]` + `[aliases]`

      Add alongside `resolved_host` in
      `crates/auctioneer-core/src/config/resolve.rs`. It EXTENDS, never
      replaces, `resolved_host` (round-21 H2): call it FIRST for the base,
      then layer the GDPR enforcement `[gdpr]` overlay + host `[aliases]` on top. Every
      baked field the override does not name — resource limits, status
      body, cookies, ccpa, lmt, and any gdpr sub-entry absent from the
      override — passes through untouched. The overlay mirrors the
      `AccountOverride` Some-field-wins pattern of Step 3, with PER-ENTRY
      recursive map merge (not whole-map replace). (`channel_enabled` is
      ACCOUNT-only, not on `HostConfig`, so it is not a `resolve_host`
      concern.)

  ```rust
  #[must_use]
  pub fn resolve_host(app: &AuctioneerAppConfig, baked: &HostConfig) -> HostConfig {
      // 1. Base = existing auction core overlay (auction.* + status.*). Never bypass.
      let mut host = resolved_host(app, baked);

      // 2. Host `[gdpr]` overlay. Absent → baked gdpr passes through whole.
      if let Some(g) = app.gdpr.as_ref() {
          if let Some(v) = g.enabled { host.gdpr.enabled = v; }
          if let Some(v) = g.host_vendor_id { host.gdpr.host_vendor_id = Some(v); }
          if let Some(v) = g.default_value.as_ref() {
              host.gdpr.default_value.clone_from(v);
          }
          // Whole-array replace (RFC 7396 array semantics).
          if let Some(v) = g.non_standard_publishers.as_ref() {
              host.gdpr.non_standard_publishers.clone_from(v);
          }
          if let Some(t) = g.tcf2.as_ref() {
              if let Some(v) = t.enabled { host.gdpr.tcf2.enabled = v; }
              // Per-ENTRY recursive merge — a keyed override touches ONLY
              // that id; sibling baked entries survive.
              if let Some(over) = t.purposes.as_ref() {
                  for (&id, po) in over {
                      let base = host.gdpr.tcf2.purposes.entry(id).or_default();
                      if let Some(v) = po.enforce_algo { base.enforce_algo = v; }
                      if let Some(v) = po.enforce_purpose { base.enforce_purpose = v; }
                      if let Some(v) = po.enforce_vendors { base.enforce_vendors = v; }
                      if let Some(v) = po.vendor_exceptions.as_ref() {
                          base.vendor_exceptions.clone_from(v);
                      }
                  }
              }
              if let Some(over) = t.special_features.as_ref() {
                  for (&id, so) in over {
                      let base = host.gdpr.tcf2.special_features.entry(id).or_default();
                      if let Some(v) = so.enforce { base.enforce = v; }
                      if let Some(v) = so.vendor_exceptions.as_ref() {
                          base.vendor_exceptions.clone_from(v);
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      }

      // 3. Host `[aliases]` overlay: per-KEY object merge (RFC 7396) —
      //    baked aliases the override does not name survive; a named key
      //    replaces its base bidder.
      if let Some(over) = app.aliases.as_ref() {
          for (alias, base_bidder) in over {
              host.aliases.insert(alias.clone(), base_bidder.clone());
          }
      }

      host
  }
  ```

  `.entry(id).or_default()` is sound: `PurposeEnforcement` and
  `SpecialFeatureEnforcement` both `#[derive(Default)]` (Task 2);
  `TriState`/`EnforceAlgo` are `Copy`. A missing baked entry the override
  names is CREATED from `default()` then overlaid (matches Step 3's
  account rule).

      stays in the taxonomy for Task 14 forward-compat — future work
      that ships remote account fetch can plug into it — but GDPR enforcement's
      single-TOML resolver never emits it.)

      `HandlerError::from_auction_error(..).into_parts()` directly).**
      Handler-path tests (the `10018` observer, the disabled-account
      ordering test, the GDPR snapshots Task 19, the account-resolution
      snapshots Task 21) all need a way to install NON-DEFAULT runtime config
      so `resolve_runtime_config` returns the fixture instead of silently
      degrading to `AuctioneerAppConfig::default()`. Without this seam every
      such test would see baked defaults (GDPR disabled) and could not
      exercise the code paths under test. Create ONE shared helper in
      `crates/auctioneer-core/tests/support/mod.rs` (included by each
      integration-test binary via `mod support;`) that drives the REAL
      handler loader — it does NOT introduce a second config path:

  ```rust
  // crates/auctioneer-core/tests/support/mod.rs
  // Round-83 H1 — the four API spellings below are verified against the
  // pinned EdgeZero (`9e661ae`; re-verified unchanged at the round-112
  // v0.0.6 pin, `c8d6e414`): `BlobEnvelope::new` (NOT `from_data`),
  // `PathParams` under `edgezero_core::params`, `ConfigRegistry =
  // StoreRegistry<ConfigStoreBinding>` built via `StoreRegistry::single_id`,
  // and the integration-test crate path `auctioneer_core::config::…` (NOT
  // `crate::…`, since integration tests are external to the crate).
  use edgezero_core::blob_envelope::BlobEnvelope;
  use edgezero_core::config_store::{ConfigStore, ConfigStoreError, ConfigStoreHandle};
  use edgezero_core::context::RequestContext;
  use edgezero_core::params::PathParams;                                 // NOT edgezero_core::http
  use edgezero_core::store_registry::{ConfigRegistry, ConfigStoreBinding, StoreRegistry};
  use auctioneer_core::config::AuctioneerAppConfig;                              // external crate path
  use std::sync::Arc;

  /// A fixed in-memory `ConfigStore` returning one blob for any key.
  struct FixedStore(String);
  #[async_trait::async_trait(?Send)]
  impl ConfigStore for FixedStore {
      async fn get(&self, _key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, ConfigStoreError> {
          Ok(Some(self.0.clone()))
      }
  }

  /// Parse fixture TOML into `AuctioneerAppConfig`, wrap it in an EdgeZero
  /// `BlobEnvelope` (`new` computes the canonical sha256 so the
  /// extractor's integrity check passes), and install it as the
  /// `"auctioneer_runtime"` config store on the request. `from_store(ctx,
  /// "auctioneer_runtime", None)` — the SAME call the real handler makes —
  /// then reads exactly this blob. `request` is the EdgeZero request type
  /// (confirm its exact path — `edgezero_core::http::Request` in the
  /// pinned tree — when wiring).
  pub fn ctx_with_config(toml_src: &str, request: edgezero_core::http::Request) -> RequestContext {
      let cfg: AuctioneerAppConfig =
          toml::from_str(toml_src).expect("fixture TOML parses");
      let data = serde_json::to_value(&cfg).expect("config → json");
      // `BlobEnvelope::new(data, generated_at)` — a fixed timestamp is
      // fine for tests; the extractor verifies the sha, not the time.
      let envelope = BlobEnvelope::new(data, "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z".to_owned());
      let blob = serde_json::to_string(&envelope).expect("envelope → string");

      // `ConfigRegistry = StoreRegistry<ConfigStoreBinding>`; the
      // single-id constructor registers the one `"auctioneer_runtime"` store.
      let registry: ConfigRegistry = StoreRegistry::single_id(
          "auctioneer_runtime".to_owned(),
          ConfigStoreBinding {
              default_key: "auctioneer_runtime".to_owned(),
              handle: ConfigStoreHandle::new(Arc::new(FixedStore(blob))),
          },
      );
      let mut request = request;
      request.extensions_mut().insert(registry);
      RequestContext::new(request, PathParams::default())
  }
  ```

  spellings above are verified against the pinned EdgeZero `9e661ae`

  ```rust
  #[validate(custom(function = "validate_sample_rate"))]
  pub sample_rate: Option<f64>,

  fn validate_sample_rate(v: &f64) -> Result<(), validator::ValidationError> {
      if v.is_finite() && (0.0..=1.0).contains(v) {
          Ok(())
      } else {
          Err(validator::ValidationError::new(
              "sample_rate_must_be_finite_and_in_0_1",
          ))
      }
  }
  ```
  The runtime sampler treats the value as trusted (post-validate)
  and does not defensively clamp — `f64` boundary handling
  (`>= 1.0` short-circuit, `<= 0.0` short-circuit) exists only to
  keep the RNG conversion well-defined at the exact endpoints.

      participates:

  ```rust
  fn apply_sampling(
      per_bidder: Vec<PerBidderRequest>,
      overrides: &BTreeMap<BidderName, f64>,
      rng: &dyn Rng,
      bundles: &mut BTreeMap<BidderName, BidderResultBundle>,
  ) -> Vec<PerBidderRequest>
  ```

  Sampling formula (boundary-safe — the naive
  `next_u64 as f64 / u64::MAX as f64` can return exactly `1.0`
  when `next_u64()` yields `u64::MAX`, which would then fail the
  `sample_rate = 1.0` "always keep" invariant):

  ```rust
  // The workspace `restriction` group denies `as_conversions` and
  // `float_arithmetic`, and `-D warnings` (Task 23) promotes the
  // pedantic `cast_precision_loss` to an error. The [0, 1) sampler
  // genuinely needs all three: `u64 -> f64` has NO `From` impl (only
  // `u32`/`i32`/`f32` do), so the mantissa cast MUST use `as`, and the
  // scale-down is float multiplication by construction. This is the
  // one place the conversion is correct and unavoidable, so scope an
  // `#[expect]` (not blanket `#[allow]`) to the single fn — `expect`
  // also fails the build if a future refactor removes the need,
  // keeping the escape hatch honest. Round-64 H3.
  #[expect(
      clippy::as_conversions,
      clippy::cast_precision_loss,
      clippy::float_arithmetic,
      reason = "u64->f64 [0,1) sampler: no From<u64> for f64; the \
                53-bit mantissa cast and scale are the correct, \
                bounded conversion (raw <= 2^53 - 1 is exact in f64)"
  )]
  fn should_keep(rate: f64, rng: &dyn Rng) -> bool {
      // Boundary short-circuits: rate == 1.0 keeps every bidder,
      // rate == 0.0 drops every bidder. Neither branch consults the
      // RNG so the endpoints are deterministic. Config-side
      // validation guarantees rate is in [0.0, 1.0]. (`<`/`>=` float
      // comparisons are fine — `float_cmp` only fires on `==`/`!=`.)
      if rate >= 1.0 { return true; }
      if rate <= 0.0 { return false; }
      // Half-open [0, 1) conversion: shift the u64 into the
      // 53-bit mantissa so the maximum representable f64 is
      // strictly less than 1.0. Same bit-level cast rand's
      // `f64::from_bits` uses. `raw <= 2^53 - 1`, so `raw as f64`
      // is EXACT (no precision actually lost despite the lint name);
      // `9_007_199_254_740_992.0` is `2^53` as an f64 literal, so the
      // divisor needs no cast of its own.
      let raw = rng.next_u64() >> 11;
      let u01 = raw as f64 / 9_007_199_254_740_992.0_f64;
      u01 < rate
  }
  ```

  **Per-bidder rate resolution — observable → base → none (round-67
  H3).** `PerBidderRequest` carries BOTH the observable name
  (`p.bidder`, which may be a request- or host-declared alias) AND the
  base bidder (`p.base`) — split.rs:12. Looking the rate up by
  `p.bidder` ALONE lets a request-defined alias dodge its base
  bidder's load-control `sample_rate`. So `apply_sampling` resolves
  each request's rate with the SAME precedence the per-bidder timeout
  already uses (observable override wins, else the base's setting):

  ```rust
  // Inside apply_sampling, per PerBidderRequest `p`:
  let rate = overrides
      .get(&p.bidder)          // 1. observable (alias) override
      .or_else(|| overrides.get(&p.base))  // 2. base bidder override
      .copied();
  match rate {
      Some(r) if !should_keep(r, rng) => { /* sample OUT: sentinel bundle */ }
      _ => { /* keep: no override on alias OR base -> not sampled */ }
  }
  ```

  A bidder/alias with no override on EITHER the observable name or the
  base bypasses the sampler (kept). This mirrors run.rs's timeout
  resolution (`[bidders.<observable>]` then `[bidders.<base>]`).
  **Sentinel bundle.** When a bidder is sampled OUT, write
  `bundles.entry(bidder).or_insert_with(BidderResultBundle::default)`
  with `dispatched = false` and no warning code / no seatnonbid row.
  The presence of the entry (a) keeps the "no live bidders" nbr
  branch reachable in the response builder and (b) makes it
  observable in tests without inventing a warning code the operator
  never asked for.

    ```rust
    // crates/auctioneer-core/src/config/runtime.rs (GDPR fanout shape)
    use crate::config::AuctioneerAppConfig;
    use edgezero_core::context::RequestContext;
    use edgezero_core::extractor::AppConfig;

    /// Round-30 H2: core-owned error type. Do NOT return
    /// `EdgeError` (the pinned EdgeZero serialises it as JSON
    /// and provides no `Retry-After` configuration, contrary to
    /// bounded fanout's plain-text 500 / 503 + `Retry-After: {n}s` contract
    /// at `bounded fanout.md` §Prereq 1 mapping table). Every
    /// config-consuming route calls `resolve_runtime_config`
    /// and then `RuntimeConfigError::into_response(err)` — the
    /// shared route response mapper below — to produce the
    /// exact wire bytes bounded fanout requires.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum RuntimeConfigError {
        /// Round-30 H2: GDPR fanout always returns `Ok(_)`; this
        /// variant is populated only under bounded fanout's fail-loud
        /// tightening. The GDPR fanout shape below never constructs it.
        MalformedHost { detail: String },
        /// Round-30 H2: same story — GDPR fanout never populates.
        ConfigStoreUnavailable {
            detail: String,
            retry_after: std::time::Duration,
        },
    }

    /// Round-31 B1 shared response builder. The round-30 sketch
    /// called nonexistent `EdgeError::from_response`, referenced
    /// `tracing` without a dep, and used `.expect(...)` inside a
    /// module the workspace's restriction lint gate rejects.
    ///
    /// Correct shape: build a `Response` directly. Handlers get
    /// `Ok(error_response)` back and return it verbatim; there is
    /// no need to route through `EdgeError`. `?` still short-
    /// circuits inside the handler because the caller pattern is
    /// `let response = match resolve_runtime_config(&ctx).await {
    ///     Ok(cfg) => run_handler(cfg, ctx).await?,
    ///     Err(err) => err.into_response()?,
    /// };`
    ///
    /// Body-build errors surface via the `?` on
    /// `response_builder().body(...)` — no `.expect(...)`.
    /// Logging uses `log::error!` / `log::warn!` because
    /// `auctioneer-core` already depends on `log` (round-30 H5
    /// added the same dep on `auctioneer-privacy`).
    impl RuntimeConfigError {
        pub fn into_response(
            self,
        ) -> Result<edgezero_core::http::Response, edgezero_core::error::EdgeError> {
            use edgezero_core::http::{response_builder, StatusCode};
            use edgezero_core::body::Body;
            match self {
                Self::MalformedHost { detail } => {
                    log::error!("malformed host config: {detail}");
                    response_builder()
                        .status(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
                        .header("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
                        .body(Body::from_bytes(b"Malformed host configuration".to_vec()))
                        .map_err(edgezero_core::error::EdgeError::internal)
                }
                Self::ConfigStoreUnavailable { detail, retry_after } => {
                    log::warn!("config store unavailable: {detail}");
                    let secs = retry_after.as_secs();
                    let body = format!(
                        "Config store unavailable, retry after {secs}s"
                    );
                    response_builder()
                        .status(StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)
                        .header("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
                        .header("retry-after", secs.to_string())
                        .body(Body::from_bytes(body.into_bytes()))
                        .map_err(edgezero_core::error::EdgeError::internal)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Resolve the runtime app-config for a request.
    ///
    /// **GDPR fanout shape (DEV-ONLY — round-45 B4):** any extractor
    /// error degrades to `AuctioneerAppConfig::default()` with a
    /// WARN log. This is acceptable ONLY because GDPR fanout is the
    /// dev-complete, non-production capability (see the
    /// deployability banner at the top of this plan). In
    /// production this path is a privacy hole: a malformed host
    /// config would silently disable GDPR enforcement. GDPR fanout
    /// cannot close it because distinguishing "key absent"
    /// (legitimate default) from "malformed" (must 500) needs
    /// the typed `StoreAppConfigError` from EdgeZero Prereq 1.
    /// The WARN log line therefore also names the capability so
    /// an operator grepping logs sees WHY it degraded:
    ///   `"[GDPR fanout dev-only] auctioneer_runtime config unavailable ..."`.
    ///
    /// **bounded fanout supersession:** bounded fanout Task Fanout-1 replaces the body
    /// with the fail-loud match over `StoreAppConfigError`
    /// variants (round-28 H5, round-30 H2 typed via the
    /// `RuntimeConfigError` shape above). Signature stays
    /// `Result<AuctioneerAppConfig, RuntimeConfigError>` so every
    /// caller (`auction`, `status`, `info_bidders`,
    /// `info_bidder`) automatically inherits the tightened
    /// behaviour without an edit.
    pub async fn resolve_runtime_config(
        ctx: &RequestContext,
    ) -> Result<AuctioneerAppConfig, RuntimeConfigError> {
        match AppConfig::<AuctioneerAppConfig>::from_store(ctx, "auctioneer_runtime", None).await {
            Ok(cfg) => Ok(cfg),
            Err(err) => {
                log::warn!(
                    "[GDPR fanout dev-only] auctioneer_runtime config unavailable: {err}. \
                     Using AuctioneerAppConfig::default(). This path is NOT \
                     production-safe — bounded fanout Prereq 1 makes malformed config \
                     fail loud (500)."
                );
                Ok(AuctioneerAppConfig::default())
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    `Result<_, RuntimeConfigError>` (NOT `EdgeError`). Callers

    ```rust
        Ok(cfg) => cfg,
        Err(err) => return err.into_response(),  // returns Result<Response, EdgeError>
    };
    ```

    ```rust
    // crates/auctioneer-core/src/handlers/auction.rs
    pub(crate) fn effective_host_aliases(
        host_aliases: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
        registry: &[&'static BidderInfo],
    ) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        host_aliases
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, base)| registry.iter().any(|b| b.name == **base))
            .map(|(a, b)| (a.clone(), b.clone()))
            .collect()
    }
    ```

    advertising an alias that `detail` would 404 (info_bidders.rs:88 vs
    :135). The auction path already drops unknown-base host aliases
    inside `resolve_aliases` (round-67 H2), so the two surfaces stay
    consistent.

     ```rust
     // crates/auctioneer-core/src/capability.rs
     #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
     pub enum Capability { DevComplete, BehaviorComplete, ProductionComplete }
     /// The capability this build is certified for. Flipped ONLY by the
     /// completion commit of the capability that earns it (Fanout-8 flips
     /// to BehaviorComplete; Fanout-10's acceptance flips to
     /// ProductionComplete). Deploy tooling gates on this value.
     pub const Capability: Capability = Capability::DevComplete;

     impl Capability {
         #[must_use]
         pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
             match self {
                 Self::DevComplete => "dev-complete",
                 Self::BehaviorComplete => "behavior-complete",
                 Self::ProductionComplete => "production-complete",
             }
         }
     }
     ```
  2. **Surfaced on the wire:** the `/status` handler adds an
     `x-auctioneer-capability: dev-complete` response header
     (config-independent — emitted regardless of `status_response`
     content), so ANY deployed instance mechanically self-reports its
     certification and a deploy pipeline / probe can assert it.
  3. **Gate assertions:**
     - Workspace test `development_status_is_dev_complete()` — asserts
       `Capability == Capability::DevComplete`; the Fanout-8/Fanout-10
       completion commits UPDATE this test alongside the constant, so
       flipping the label without passing those capabilities' own gates
       is a visible, reviewable diff, never a silent promotion.
     - Handler test `status_carries_development_header()` — asserts the
       header value equals `Capability.as_str()`.

       boundary): a PRODUCTION deploy of any adapter REQUIRES
       `x-auctioneer-capability: production-complete` from the deployed
       candidate (or `Capability == ProductionComplete` at build time).

## Explicit non-goals for GDPR enforcement

- **CCPA / GPP full parsing (sections 3, 6, 7-12) / activity model
  / the NON-GDPR scrub rows.** All privacy enforcement. **Round-48 B1 correction:
  the two GDPR-driven Appendix C.2 scrubs — `scrub_gdpr_id` on
  `PassID=false` and `scrub_geo_and_device_ip` on `PassGeo=false` —
  are IN GDPR enforcement** (Task 13 Step 3b); GDPR enforcement is the GDPR gate and must
  actually strip IDs / round geo when it denies them, not merely
  decide. What stays privacy enforcement is the rest of the matrix: `scrub_user_fpd`,
  the CCPA `scrub_device_ids_ips_user_demo_ext`, LMT/COPPA, and
  `scrub_tid`, plus the activity model that drives them. GDPR enforcement does
  honor `regs.gpp_sid` section 2 for the GDPR-in-scope Signal decision
  (spec §7.1 line 2202), but does NOT decode the section-2 (TCFEU2)
  CONSENT — so **GDPR enforcement treats section-2 consent as UNUSABLE
  (`consent_usable = false` → the `default_permissions()` row: `PassID:
false` always, bid/geo denied where P2/SF1 are enforced), on the
  enforcement path**, rather than reading the legacy `user.consent` an
  authoritative GPP section-2 could override (round-75 B1 / round-76 B2
  — Task 8 Step 2.0; this is NOT "deny all section-2 traffic" — out-of-
  scope requests are still allow-all). It also does NOT decode / enforce
  section 6 (USPV1 → US-Privacy) — that's privacy enforcement per spec §7.4 line 2358.
  The GPP section-2 extractor + `user.consent`-vs-GPP conflict handling
  that would let GDPR enforcement HONOUR (not just nullify) section-2 consent is privacy enforcement.
- **Sync endpoints (`/cookie_sync`, `/setuid`, `/getuids`).** All user sync.
- **Debug surface (`ext.debug`).** diagnostic qualification.
- **`SkipWhen.gpp_sid` matching, per-syncer `BidderSyncAllowed`.** user sync.
- **Host-cookie GDPR-only gate for `/setuid`.** user sync.

## Explicit deferrals to future review rounds

- **EdgeZero ingress hook** (spec §14 production-complete prereq).
  Production-complete-only; not in GDPR fanout's dev-complete scope. **Round-71
  H2 — the canonical owner is bounded fanout Task Fanout-10** (blocked on EdgeZero
  Prereq 5), NOT privacy enforcement/user sync. The earlier "privacy enforcement/user sync owns wiring" note is
  superseded: Fanout-10 carries the full ingress decision table +
  adapter wiring, and the spec §13 registration note points there too.
- **Full RFC 7396 JSON merge (JSON-value form).** The GDPR enforcement account
  overlay is a typed-struct `Option::Some/None` overlay that
  preserves RFC 7396's structural semantics (see Task 15's
  "Overlay semantics" block) but does NOT accept a raw JSON
  `null` as "remove this key" because TOML has no `null`. The
  full JSON-value RFC 7396 merge (including null-removes-key)
  ships with the future config-store account path — that capability
  reintroduces `resolve_account_from_store(raw_body, config_store,
default)` and applies the merge against a `serde_json::Value`
  before deserialising into `AccountConfig`.
- **GPP-derived GDPR consent (spec Appendix D.1 GPP section 2).**
  Spec D.1 line 5369 makes GPP section 2 the winning GDPR consent
  source when present. **GDPR enforcement does NOT parse GPP, and it does NOT read
  `user.consent` when GPP section 2 is in scope (round-76 B1 / round-77
  H2 — corrects the earlier "GDPR enforcement reads `user.consent` only / misclassifies
  section-2 as no-consent" wording, which described a fail-OPEN bug).**
  Because GDPR enforcement has no GPP decoder, it cannot honour the authoritative
  section-2 consent, so it FAILS CLOSED: any request whose
  `regs.gpp_sid` includes section 2 makes GDPR consent UNUSABLE
  (`consent_usable = false` → `default_permissions()`, `PassID` always
  false; Task 8 Step 2.0), rather than falling back to a possibly-stale
  `user.consent`. The GPP wire-signal (whether GDPR applies at all)
  already consults `regs.gpp_sid` via `resolve_wire_signal`
  (Task 5 Step 1). The DEFERRED piece is honouring section-2 consent
  affirmatively: a post-GDPR enforcement (privacy enforcement) capability will add (a) a GPP parser,
  (b) a section-2 extractor that produces the same `TcfString` shape
  Task 4 loads today, and (c) the "consent conflict" warning path from
  D.1's "Both present and differ" row. Until privacy enforcement lands those, a valid
  `regs.gpp` section 2 that WOULD grant consent is treated as unusable
  (denied ID, enforced-but-empty defaults) — documented and observable,
  a fail-CLOSED gap, not a fail-open one.
  **Round-57 B-l — the `regs.gpp` well-formedness warning is part of
  this same GPP deferral.** The spec's `NonFatalWarning { code:
10001, scope: "regs.gpp" }` on a malformed GPP string requires GPP
  section-parsing, so it lands with the privacy enforcement GPP parser (the spec
  bullet is annotated to match). Through GDPR enforcement, `regs.gpp` is passed
  through un-decoded and emits NO well-formedness warning; only the
  `regs.gpp_sid`-vs-`regs.gdpr` conflict warning (Task 7 —
  section-id routing, not string decode) fires in GDPR enforcement.

## Execution Handoff

**Which approach?** Options:

1. **Subagent-Driven** — dispatch a fresh subagent per task using
   `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`. Each task is self-
   contained; a subagent with only this plan + the spec link can
   execute end-to-end. Recommended for tasks 2-18.
2. **Inline Execution** — execute in this session using
   `superpowers:executing-plans`. Recommended for Task 1 (the spike
   requires a running conversation) and Task 23 (verification-only).
